ROD Otel tt Everyone believes there is a special person, job and place for him or her. The Astro*Carto*Graphy Book of Maps explores those special places in the lives of celebrities and famous figures. This book by Jim Lewis and Ariel Guttman consists of maps, birth charts and personal profiles of people from all walks of life. The maps, based on the time of birth, graphically reveal lines of planetary influence or concentration at various geographic locations. A planet affecting a certain area is correlated with a person's success, failure or noteworthy activities there. See how Jane Fonda's life changed once she responded to her Moon line. Or maybe you'd like to know which line keeps cropping up at the site of assassinations. What lines similarly influenced the lives of Elvis Presley and Elizabeth Taylor? Gain some insight into possible actions and attitudes during George Bush's presidency. Astro*Carto*Graphy can also be used to bring about the stronger influence of a certain planet by showing its angular positions. Angular positions involve the Ascendant, the IC, the Descendant and the Midheaven. The maps show where planets would have been if you had been born at different locations than at your birthplace. Thus, if you'd like a little romance, maybe your true love is around a Venus line. You may start a successful enterprise near a Jupiter line. Crossings, places where lines intersect each other on the map, affect not only the area where they occur, but also any area on the crossing's latitude. This means that at sucha latitude you will feel the influence ofall the planets involved in the crossing, no matter how far away the actual crossing occurred at the time of birth. Charts and maps of personalities in the entertainment field, such as Joan Crawford, Marilyn Monroe, Grace Kelly, Yul Brynner, James Dean, John Lennon and David Bowie, are included in this compilation. Activists like Martin Luther King, Jr. and Lech Walesa and spiritual pioneers like Freud, Jung and Yogananda are presented. Events in the lives of painters, musicians and sports figures are explored through the maps. The successes, problems and tendencies of such politicians as FDR, Harry Truman, JFK, Richard Nixon, Ronald Reagan, George Bush, Jesse Jackson and Margaret Thatcher are related to their maps. The book closes with maps and charts of nations, including the U.S., the United Kingdom, and Israel, and events, such as the voyage of the Titanic, the first atomic bomb test and the first ingestion of LSD. The prominence of each planetary line in the lives and events of people and nations has also been tabulated. These charts reveal in a glance the correlation between one's profession and the general planetary vibrations s/he found most beneficial to progress and success. An order form at the back of the book allows you to receive your personalized Astro*Carto*Graphy map. Explore the world and your potential by finding your special places on Earth.

Jim Lewis is an internationally recognized authority on relocation astrology. He began his professional career in 1969 asa personal service astrologer for American Astrology magazine, then under the guidance of the late Donald A. Bradley. In 1972, he moved to San Francisco where he has served a large clientele, taught classes, and appeared on numerous radio and TV programs. In 1975, he began work on ASTRO*CARTO#GRAPHY, and now devotes most of his time to popularizing the concepts of locational astrology. His work with ASTRO*CARTO*GRAPHY earned him the Marc Edmund Jones Award for the outstanding contribution to astrology at the 1978 National Astrological Society Convention. Since then, he has appeared on the faculties of almost every important astrological conference; he was one of five Americans selected to attend the First and Second World conferences in Switzerland in 1981 and 1984. His lecturing credits now include 12 nations and 20 states and provinces. ASTRO*CARTO* GRAPHY is available in six languages. In 1982, he completed work on CYCLO*CARTO*GRAPHY, an important adjunct to ASTRO*CARTO*GRAPHY, for which he was awarded a U.S. patent. In 1987, ASTRO*CARTO* GRAPHY E*PLAINED, a computerized interpretive service that analyzes locations according to the principles of A*C*G and creates a written report, was completed. As wellas contributing frequent articles on many aspects of astrology to the popular press, he annually publishes the Source Book of Mundane Maps. He has been very active in AFAN, an activist organization serving the astrological community, since 1982.

Born in St. Louis, Missouri in 1949, Ariel began her formal studies in astrology in San Diego, California where she resided for 12 years. In 1980, she founded Astro Originals, an Encinitas, California-based consulting firm wherein the language of astrology could be utilized and recognized as an important self-awareness tool. In presenting astrological workshops to the public, Ariel has continually sought to introduce material that makes astrology more "grounded" while honoring its mystical and spiritual framework. As a lecturer for the astrological faculties of SWAC, ISAR, UAC, AFA and as past Research Director for the San Diego Astrological Society, Ariel has presented astrological research on topics of compatibility, the goddesses of astrology, A*C*G, and health and wellbeing. In addition, she has been a faculty member at Well Within, a Holistic Education Seminar Network in California and the Western States. There she has presented "Astrology's Role in the Healing Arts" to hundreds of nurses, nurse practitioners, chiropractors, acupuncturists, massage therapists, yoga instructors and health educators. Ariel and her husband Michael have recently relocated to Santa Fe, New Mexico, her "Mercury" line, where she finds a stimulating environment suitable for pursuing her writing career, the photographic arts and astrological counseling. She also maintains an office in Encinitas, California at the Infinite Winds Metaphysical Counseling Center. For those who are not aware of it, Astro*Carto*Graphy is one of the most revolutionary developments in modern astrology. While it grew out of the work of a number of independent workers, the astrological world owes Jim Lewis an everlasting debt for bringing it into a form that is accessible to all who have need of it. Generating an Astro*Carto*Graphy map is an instance of a computer-assisted astrological technique that is more than merely difficult to compute by hand, it is nearly impossible. Astro*Carto*Graphy is the shining example of how the computer can expand astrological horizons. But AstroxCarto*Graphy is more than a technically significant astrological method. It shows more clearly than almost any other natal astrology technique the close relationship between the individual and the cosmos. Not only are we connected to the larger rhythms of the solar system in time, Astro*Carto*Graphy shows how we are also connected to them in space. The horoscope is translated from a map of power points in time to a map of the power points in space. Those who have heard Jim Lewis lecture are aware of the power of the technique in explaining patterns in the lives of famous individuals and history. With this book of case studies, it is now possible for others who have not had access to Jim's lectures to see this as well. In alrnost every instance where I personally knew of the circumstances of an individual's life, | found that a quick perusal of the Astro*Carto*Graphy for that person showed symbolically appropriate planet lines at that place. Astro*Carto*Graphy is not one of those astrological techniques that requires bending and stretching of astrological principles to get results. The results are almost always clear and definite, and they assist the astrologer in understanding the dynarnics of astrologica] symbols. This book is important in another way—as evidence for astrology. In any single case study one could, if one were so inclined, choose to disregard the correlations between life events and Astro*Carto*Graphy lines as mere chance or the result of careful selection by the astrologer. However, there are so many case studies in this book which cover sucha wide range of personalities and life histories, some even involving several characters in a particular historical episode, that it is impossible to regard the results as solely due to chance. This book is powerful evidence for astrological effects in life and history. —Robert Hand

The traditional way of charting the planets at the moment of someone's birth is convenient and relatively easy to figure, but it is also very limited and one dimensional. With Jin Lewis's Astro*Carto*Graphy maps, astrology moves beyond the static idea of an isolated birthplace. Your "horoscope" becomes the whole world, and you can emphasize various parts of the whole by moving to places marked by the lines on the map. Ariel] Guttrnan deserves high praise for sparking a working relationship that has produced a marvelous explanation of how Astro*Carto*Graphy works in the lives of real people. —Kenneth Irving Co-editor, American Astrology magazine . This is a book written by a committee of two, Jim Lewis and Ariel Guttman. Shortly after Ariel's successful coordination of the 1986 ASTRO*CARTO*GRAPHY Professional Seminar in Laguna Beach, she and Jim talked about the attendees' requests (heard often before) for a book of ASTRO*CARTO*GRAPHY maps of famous people from the examples used in the Seminar. Since Jim had lots to do running ASTRO* CARTO*GRAPHY and Ariel had her own busy practice and planned a move to Santa Fe, both agreed that the other one should do all the work. Somehow, this book was the result. It is truly a book about relocation and was created in San Francisco, Santa Fe, Boulder, and Encinitas, California. Ariel did the preliminary research in the library and offered ideas, particularly about the artists, writers, and entertainers. Jim drew from his decade of experience in ASTRO*CARTO*GRAPHY and contributed insights particularly to the analyses of politicians, activists, and spiritual pioneers. Special thanks should go to our editor, Kathy Halgren, who made the resulting patchwork into a whole cloth; to Lois Rodden, who verified birth data; and to Richard Nolle, who created the accompanying horoscopes using Matrix's Blue Star software on his IBM XT computer. Anyone with observations on the maps or ASTRO* CARTO* GRAPHY is welcome to write the authors at: ASTRO*CARTO*GRAPHY, Box 959, El Cerrito, CA 94530.

"Under Saturn's influence in Colorado, I worked very hard ona ranch for low pay and spent my spare time rock climbing."! Prior to 1976, few astrologers would have been able to make much sense out of this statement. But since then, astrology has been augmented by a new technique which has more to do with "where" than "when." Saturn used to be found only in the sky as a malefic, wizened killjoy, spending two anda half years making natives of any one astrological sign miserable as he "afflicted" them. How did he get to Colorado? Astrology was developed back when nobody went anyplace. But now, people move far and frequently; in California, most people live at least 500 miles away from their birthplace, a distance traversed only by a minute percentage of humans prior to this century. And so, astrology has had to catch up and has done so with ASTRO*CARTO*#GRAPHY which enables a person to determine which parts of the natal chart potential will be accented, highlighted, or brought into consciousness in a new location. Currently, astrology accepts that different places accentuate different potentials for an individual through a system that can be used to understand and plan in advance where you might find your Saturn, Venus, or Uranus. Using this system, astrology can anticipate how relocation will change an individual's life experience.

For those unacquainted with modern astrology, a few words might be useful. Most astrologers no longer believe in cause and effect as the principle behind astrology's validity—they do not believe that planets at birth or later on in life "make things happen." Rather, they see a "synchronistic" universe, one in which events ofa similar type are linked by a mysterious connecting principle, a principle which has only recently begun to be defined by scientist Rupert Sheldrake. Astrologers consider that this connecting principle (which Sheldrake calls "morphic resonance") links the birth moment and the individual with whatever else was going on in the world at that instant. Simplistically then, people born in the 1950s will tend as a group to the unquestioning conformity and optimism of that time. Others, born in the '60s, will be more rebellious, iconoclastic, and willing to change and modify institutions. Of course, within such large groups, individual differences will be apparent. And both the individual differences and the broader group identity can be associated symbolically with the positions of planets at the moment of the subject's birth. If Saturn was powerful in the sky at the moment of your birth, then its themes (which have been defined and developed by millenia of observation by astrologers) will dominate your character; you will be expected to be sensitive, reserved, ambitious, autonomous, and interested in rock climbing. Or, if you choose not to assimilate or express these attributes, astrology will expect you to find them outside yourself in other people and external situations.

These don't come up often in the examples given but are generally places where no particular part of the planetary repertoire is accented or emphasized beyond its natal importance or where uniformly stressful natal potentials are evaded. Crossings. Obviously,a place where two or more lines cross is affected by each of the planet energies indicated. But also, anywhere in the world along the latitude of that exact crossing is similarly affected. Example: Jimmy Carter's Jupiter and Mars lines cross at Teheran, but Mars and Jupiter affected him while he was in Washington, which is near the very same latitude. How Close Do You Have toBe? The closerto the line, the more pronounced the effects, but some effects can be felt as far as 700 miles (1,000 kilometers) away. A line passing through Denver might be felt as far east as Kansas City and as far west as Las Vegas, particularly if it were the only line in that vicinity. On the maps in this book, this "orb" of influence amounts to about 1/4" or 7 millimeters. However, the closest line to a particular location should theoretically identify the most potent planetary influence, regardless of its distance. Those Little Boxes on the MH Lines are the zeniths— the places where each planet was directly overhead at the birth moment. They describe a potential center of intense energy and also have latitudinal effect; that is, they affect any place on the same latitude at which they occur. Where All the Lines Cross near the North Pole. Where this many lines cross, they would tend to cancel one another out and have much the same effect as no lines at all; still, it would be an intense place and one which most people have found unpleasant—for the climate, if for no other reason. "Good" Planets and "Bad" Planets. There is no good or evil in astrology. It is only what we do with the planetary energies that might be classified in this fashion. People are constantly looking for "sood" locations for themselves, but astrology teaches that the natal planets are all lessons, stages, ~ and necessary parts of one's maturation. Just as your liver isn't "better" than your pelvis, each is good for something and a part of the whole. Problems result only when one tries to use the right planet for the wrong purposes. It's like trying to run your automobile on margarine or the human body on Chevron No-Lead. Astrology hopes to help you to understand the nature of the planet and use its potentials for your growth and maturation. In this book, the same planet will emerge as "good" and "bad" in different cases, but in either case it will retain its essential character. The definition of this essential character is one of the purposes of this study. The Use of Famous People With few exceptions, we have used here the maps of well-known individuals, a practice that is sometimes questioned by astrologers. Famous people exhibit certain advantages as objects for astrological study. What has happened to them is generally well documented so that a technique can be judged on the basis of a known, historical past. And future developments in their lives are also apt to be widely publicized so the map can continue to be instructive as their lives unfold. In addition, it seems that famous people seem to offer some of the best examples of how ASTRO* CARTO*GRAPHY works. People become famous because they exemplify some universal concept of interest to everyone, and these universal concepts, called archetypes, are the same ones that are symbolized by the planets. So a "match" on their maps is apt to be even more impressive and memorable. Interpreting the map of an "ordinary person" is only slightly different. Liz Taylor moved from London to Los Angeles where she had four powerful lines. If you move to the same lines, it is unlikely you'll star in Cleopatra, be given gigantic diamonds, and pioneer fund-raising for AIDS research. But you might have a couple of ill-chosen affairs, take acting lessons, and volunteer to help the elderly. It's just a matter of degree in the expression of the same symbols. But why is there need for a map of the whole world since so few people ever move outside their own nation? Because even people who never move far from their places of birth are affected by remote locations, as discussed previously. Also, the four lines of any one planet often form consistent patterns of life experience. In the map of the U.S.A. (Boyd's "Declaration of War"), for example, the evolution of this nation's military attitude and involvement is obvious from al the locations of Mars' lines. If the examples offered in the book inspire the reader to wish to obtain his/her own map, s/he will fine

information for this purpose at the end of the volume. Time, date, and place of birth are needed to complete a map for an individual. With such a map, you may better understand the planetary archetype under which you have chosen to live, the one you like to visit, and even those with which you are least comfortable. What is Venus? Why is She Descending? Probably the first accomplishment of prehistoric astrologers was the distinction between the "fixed" stars, whose only motion through the sky was a seasonal function of Earth's revolution about the Sun, and planets (the word itself is derived from the Greek "to wander'), which were observed to move through the constellations in cycles that became the basis of astrology. Over the centuries, meanings were ascribed to these planets from observation and from mythological association, and these meanings are the fundamental origins of the interpretations of time that astrologers generate. This book is obviously not the place for an exhaustive exploration of the significations attributed to the ten planetary archetypes (astrologers, for the sake of convenience, categorize the Sun and Moon along with the other eight planets, excluding Earth). Rather, it is intended to affirm and supplement the planetary meanings astrologers have used by demonstrating their applicability in a locational application with numerous, well-known examples. Still, the book would be incomplete without a brief description of the planets' traditional interpretations and associations. Following are brief synopses of each planet's meaning as usually expressed when dominant in a particular location." This brief listing is intended mostly as amemory aid or guide for the reader unacquainted with astrology; any beginning astrology text will present a far more thorough inventory of the psychological and practical matters associated with these most basic astrological archetypes. SUN: Here, you become master of your own fate and attract others' envy, good wishes, favor and admiration. This is the best place to practice theatre, creative arts, leadership, or to seek publicity. Health improves, and rehabilitation, self-actualization and promotion go well. Dangers lie in coming on too strong, arrogance, inconsideration and egotism. MOON: Under these lines, you are completely immersed in sensation and become entangled, vulnerable and involved with others. Nurturing capacity, sympathy, sentimentality, sensitivity and spontaneity are responses to constant environmental change; needs and appetites emerge powerfully. Negatively, it can mean impermanence, dependence and emotionalism. MERCURY: These areas get you in touch with how you best make contact or have intercourse with the outer world. Symbols, words, writing, ideas, education, work skills, communication, travel, mobility and youthful mental creativity are emphasized here. Negatively, there can be lack of commitment, superficiality, amorality and petty criminality (or exposure to it). VENUS: Here, self-perfection and growth encourage relationship. Love and marriage mates are found under Venus lines. Beauty, sensuality, luxury, money, ease and artistic interests dominate; self-esteem and appearance improve. Dangers lie in consumerism, laziness, superficiality, objectification of people and in an immature, make-believe attitude. MARS: This area is where masterful, dominating, courageous, sexual, passionate instincts take over, but there is danger of attacks, accidents, rashness, injury and contentiousness. Still, zest for life increases, engineering, individual athletics, competition or building succeed, and power is found and mobilized to take care of self. JUPITER: Prosperity, success, social acceptance, exposure to the rich and powerful, status and conformity beckon from this zone. You are taken care of and coddled with success in publishing and team sports. Elevated living standards are balanced against possible boredom, bourgeois complacency and pomposity. Lucky breaks in material and career concerns are likely. SATURN: Fierce personal independence and perseverance develop in the face of difficulties in health, power struggles, poor finances and solitude under these lines. Challenge, maturity and hard work are met and accepted. Though they complain, people find it hard to leave these zones once entrenched by the responsibilities and feelings of personal power that come from accepting them. URANUS: In Uranus zones, the surprising becomes commonplace as boredom and social rigidity are shattered. You grow to be able to see who youare, apart from your social role, and rebel against City Hall, rules, conformity, and your own past; causes are adopted. * List taken from "How to Use Your ASTRO*CARTO*GRAPHY Map," text copyright 1980 by Astro*Carto*Graphy. Impermanence and constant change must be accepted, along with possible scapegoating, inability to relate emotionally and alienation. NEPTUNE: Under Neptune lines, ideals are pursued, romanticism flowers, spiritual progress can be made, and photography, arts and music are inspired. Sigmund Freud proposed the theory of the unconscious, founded psychoanalysis, and has been called the father of modern psychology. He spent his life working in Vienna nearest his SU DSC line and so resembles Jung (q.v.) in this respect. While both had Suns powerful on the angular 7th House and could illuminate for their patients unrecognized regions of the psyche, the principal difference between them is Jung's SU line crossed his PL line while Freud's Sun was closely conjunct natal Uranus and in the same sign as Pluto. Pluto and Uranus both symbolize cathartic transformation, but while Uranus seems connected to ego, ideas and individuality, Pluto reflects the deeper processes of life itself. Freud identified far more strongly with Uranus, living closer beneath its lines, and his famous feud with Plutonian Jung illustrates the discomfort with which he regarded the total upheaval, change and death of the ego symbolized by Pluto. His obsession with the libido can also be traced to this discomfort, but in a time when sexual matters were never discussed, his focus on libidinous instincts, mitigated by appropriate Victorian disgust, was an important step forward for European medicine and philosophy. Four planetary crossings also dominate Vienna's latitude for Freud: MO/ASC*PL/ASC; VE/IC*SA/DSC; NE/IC*ME/DSC, and VE/DSC*PL/DSC. Clearly, the feminine archetype is linked here with unconscious forces so that it is not surprising that so many of his patients were women, oppressed by the limitations of Victorian society. On a trip to the northeastern U.S. with Jung in 1909, both were granted honorary degrees by Clark University (ME MH). Burnings by the Nazis of Freud's work began to occur in Berlin in 1933, so he exiled himself to London though he was loath to leave his beloved home in Vienna. Fond of Greek and Egyptian art and literature, he spent much time exploring the ancient myths of Moses, Israel and Egypt. The last 16 years of his life were severely painful for Freud on account of many jaw surgeries. To relieve the suffering, he used cocaine and was a confirmed addict by the time he died in exile in London (PL and VE DSC) in 1939.

Carl Jung was born in Kesswil, Switzerland under SU DSC and PL IC. Though his travels would briefly take him to several continents, he spent his entire life living and working very near his birthplace. Three pairs of planetary crossings—all powerfully feminine—affect Zurich: MO/ASC*#NE/ASC, VE/IC*MO/ASC, and VE/ IC*NE/ASC. His work certainly has a feminine flavor to it, especially in contrast to Freud's (q.v.) very masculine Sun-Uranus approach, and the preponderance of his disciples and devotees seem to be women. Jung studied medicine at Basel. He met Freud in Vienna (near Jung's UR DSC) in 1907 and became one of his leading protégés. As his own personality developed, he became increasingly critical of Freud's dogma placing sexual maladjustment at the core of all mental problems. With the publication of The Psychology of the Unconscious in 1911-12, he broke formally with his mentor. Jung went on to develop influential theories of psychological types, such as extravert/introvert; he studied psychic energy and proposed the existence of the "collective unconscious," archetypes, and individuation. His work drew from varied and rich cultural sources—dreams, myths, history, tribal cultures, alchemy, even astrology. It encompassed anthropology, religion, art and literature. Perhaps the most notable distinguishing characteristic of Jung's work was its view of the psyche as an evolving, 37 growing entity, linked somehow to a "collective unconscious." With the SU on the DSC, he drew much of his inspiration from his patients, and PL IC shows a singular example of positive Pluto: ongoing transformation of the "base material" of existence into the alchemical gold of consciousness. He received many honorary degrees from such institutions as Clark University, Harvard and Yale (MO DSC); Oxford (ME DSC); Calcutta and Benares (UR IC, MO ASC, SU IC), and, of course, places of learning near his home in Zurich (PL IC, SU DSC). His ME and VE MH lines are over San Francisco, where there are probably more Jungians than in all of Switzerland. In the 1920s he traveled extensively, as noted in his autobiography. A visit to Tunis and Algiers in 1920 hada profound effect upon him personally (PL IC). In 1924- 25, he visited the Pueblo Indians of New Mexico and Arizona (JU ASC, SU MH) and declared their sacred land to be the spiritual center of North America. The following year he visited Kenya to observe tribal practices and later went to Egypt where he commented on the masculine nature of the culture (MA MH). He was in India twice, the last visit being in 1937, attempting to discovera correlation between the unconscious psychic contents of modern man and more primitive manifestations. Here is where he has the SU IC and MO ASC lines crossing, (see also Gauguin map for the same planetary crossing over Tahiti), a place where he must have felt an integration of the masculine and feminine which was an ongoing symbolic quest in his life and work.

He was also a popular radio personality in both San Francisco and Los Angeles where he had a call-in show about Zen. Moreover, San Francisco lies between SA MH and the MO ASC, two polarities that bespeak the humanism and strict traditionalism of his Zen. The "Age of the Guru" may have officially reached its close with the undignified flight, of Bhagwan Shree Rajneesh from his commune in Oregon in 1985. Purchasing desert land in eastern Oregon, he and thousands of his followers built a city, irrigated, and quickly began to outnumber the suspicious and traditional local folks. The media, redolent with parallels to Jonestown, arrived, and the affair concluded with Rajneesh fleeing, immigration authorities in hot pursuit, while several of his followers were charged with mass poisonings, attempted murder, and various degrees of fraud and conspiracy. But how did he know to travel to Oregon, the one place in the world at which they would be on the IC? At this writing (1988) he is back in Poona, under the watchful eye of the Indian government.

Born in Philadelphia on a VE ASC line, Grace Kelly was drawn to acting in New York where she studied drama under her ME ASC line. While ME lines are good for writing, they also identify good places for education since the powers of the mind are in sharp focus. During the filming of Hitchcock's To Catch A Thief on the French Riviera, she met Prince Rainier of Monaco. They married shortly thereafter and so actualized as closely as possible the Cinderella/Prince Charming fairy tale that culturally dominated the pre-feminist 1950s. She gave up a very successful, if short-lived, Hollywood career for a chance to be a princess, live in acastle and raise three children. As Cinderella, her life was entirely taken up by her family and her involve- 73 ment in Monaco's social and political functions, a life which was cut short by an automobile crash in that same location in 1982. The ME MH line passes nearest to Monaco, and its inappropriateness calls this birth time into question, but a case can be made for her ongoing concern with the well-being of her subjects, and it's likely that in the snobbish, glittering milieu of Europe's playground Grace Kelly seemed relatively commonplace. An indication unaffected by birth time is the exact crossing of SU*NE on the latitude of Monaco. A SU*NE crossing unites visibility and myth in an aspect unusually appropriate for a princess living out a fairy tale romance. Under the Sun-Neptune combination, the illusion is often grander than the reality, however, so this princess' untimely exit reflected an inner discontent with the role her life had presented her.

As actor and cult hero for American youth in the '50s, James Dean's meteoric rise to fame was cut short by his passion for life and intensity. Born in Indiana, his family moved to southern California when he was four years old. At the death of his mother, he was sent back to relatives who lived ona farm in Indiana (VEIC, JU MH). Though he felt loved by his aunt and uncle, he experienced deep pain and rejection at being orphaned so early in life. He excelled in sports, exhibited a reckless rebelliousness, and enjoyed motorcycles and terrifying teen pranks. He joined his high school drama guild and participated in poetry readings. After high school, he spent a short period of time with 79 his father in California. In Hollywood (NE ASC), he was encouraged by his mentor, James Whitmore, to study at the Actors Studio in New York (PL MH, SA IC). His first role in East of Eden firmly established him as a serious actor and attracted a youthful following. With Neptune angular over Hollywood, he continued his hero/victim roles in future films and in his private life. Earlier, he had been introduced to Yoga as a means of physical as well as mental discipline, and he continued this practice throughout his acting career. Auto racing was also a passion. While driving his Porsche to an auto meetin Salinas, California, he collided with another car and was killed instantly. His death, at the apex of youthful potentiality, earned him archetypal status as a puer aeternus symbol—never to experience the moderation imposed by maturity or aging.

In the days when it was customary to marry every time an encounter became sexual, her marriages and divorces kept her constantly in the tabloids. Her SA IC goes right through Egypt. Their resulting love affair reportedly delayed shooting of the film tremendously and drove the production costs up into the millions. Near Egypt, specifically the Mediterranean areas of Italy, Greece and Libya, she has a VE-UR conjunction on the DSC crossed by PL MH, and these appropriately describe her affair with Burton. Her Pluto zenith occupies the latitude of Puerto Vallarta where her increasingly sordid affair with thenalcoholic Burton began to go beyond what the public could find amusing. On Hollywood's longitude, she has an exact MA MH- NE IC opposition, two planets which are often the signature of sensational, sexy film stars, and those who may have problems with addictions. Recently, the MA-NE influence has manifested more positively in her courageous fund-raising work for AIDS research, demonstrating how maturity can temper even the most problematical aspects.

While placed under the heading of "Entertainers," jane Fonda has as many facets to her personality as she's had movie parts. She's been a successful Hollywood sex kitten, political activist, serious actress, aerobics instructor, entrepreneur, and wife and mother. This Fire sign woman (Sagittarius Sun, Leo Moon) never stops. Her VE ASC and SA IC are closest to Hollywood, appropriately reflecting the connection to her famous father, Henry Fonda, and her physical beauty. Early in her career, she went to Paris under the influence of her JU MH and PLIC, and there met and married Roger Vadim, a French producer who created many of her films. These early film roles tended to exploit her femaleness, displaying the same welltoned body she now can successfully market in exercise videos at age 51. While her films did fairly well, her campaign to publicly protest the U.S. role in Viet Nam really made headlines. She was under illegal governmental surveillance for several years. The Nixon Administration, operating from her JU ASC and PL DSC, considered her a real threat to their idea of democracy and the American people. She was arrested at a Cleveland airport (UR IC and ME ASC, see also Timothy Leary's map previously in this text) for possession of illegal drugs, which, 89 in fact, were vitamin pills and prescription tranquilizers. The obvious unfairness of this persecution lent credence to her cause. But many of her fans think she went too far when she traveled to Hanoi and allowed herself to be used by the North Vietnamese government. Her MO ASC there shows a genuine, passionate commitment, as well as a childlike naiveté. (See also the Berrigans, North and Secord for other politically passionate MO lines.) After Viet Nam ceased to be an issue, she withdrew from the public arena, emerging a few years later as a serious actress whose production company sought to make marketable films with messages. For the most part, they have succeeded, though her most popular effort also involved Viet Nam (MO ASC) —her role in Coming Home won her an Oscar. Her subsequent films, especially The China Syndrome about a nuclear power plant meltdown, were regarded by many in Hollywood as too political. But the nation and Hollywood were stunned when the Three Mile Island catastrophe (on her UR*ME crossing latitude) occurred the same week the film was released. Making films and marketing exercise videotapes and clothing are what occupy most of her time back on her VE ASC and SA IC. If she divorces her California politician husband, Tom Hayden, she is likely to resume a more direct political activisim.

John Lennon truly became a legend in his own time. Born under the rare Saturn-Jupiter-Uranus conjunction, he had powerful effects in three places where it was angular at his birth. Early rock and roll fans in Liverpool (SA ASC, JU ASC, UR ASC) and then Hamburg (PLIC, MO MH) brought the Beatles to the attention of European audiences. A 1964 tour to the U.S. and the release of "I Want to Hold Your Hand" created a worldwide furor. The Beatles' appearance on the Ed Sullivan Show touched off "Beatlemania." The SA-JU- UR conjunction which occupied his ASC in England came to the IC in New York with the additional influence of the MO ASC assuring popularity with the masses. John Lennon was labeled the "intellectual" Beatle. His opinions, which mirrored the social and political inquiry of the times, became lyrics to one gold album after another. Lennon soon grew weary of being a "star" 91 and having people faint, no matter how absurdly the Beatles performed. In 1967, his assertion that the group was more popular than Jesus Christ led to mass burnings of Beatle albums by fundamentalists in the South and Midwest, but it only fed his popularity among the youthful counterculture. With five planets in Venusruled signs, he opposed Britain's involvement in the Nigerian Civil War (PLIC, MO MH, SA ASC, JU ASC, UR ASC) and its support of the U.S. involvement in Viet Nam (SA MH zenith, JU MH zenith). He became a symbol of the revolutionary peace movement. He met and married Yoko Ono (VE ASC and NE ASC are on either side of Tokyo), whom he acknowledged as his spiritual teacher, and evolved from his pop star persona to a more soul-searching, introspective artist. They set up housekeeping in New York City, raising their son, Sean. During the late '70s, Lennon enjoyed gardening, housekeeping, cooking and parenting. He was just beginning to go back into album-making and musical peformance when an assassin's bullet ended his life outside his home in 1980 at age 40.

Ann-Margaret was born in Sweden very close to her planetary "vortex," one of two locations on the globe where all the planet lines converge. Many show business jobs in Chicago, followed by others in Kansas City, Las Vegas and Los Angeles, started her off on her successful career. A 22-foot fall from a stage platform while performing in Lake Tahoe (SA DSC) threatened not only her career, but her life. Her six-planet stellium in Taurus conferred on her the determination not to let this stop her—she was totally recovered and back 93 on-stage performing again within three months. With JU DSC and UR DSC in Hollywood, she might be expected to mature into more serious roles, ones that deal with moral or philosophical issues, and this has come to pass. She holds awards from the Italian Film Institute for her contributions in international filmmaking and a Presidential Citation for two trips she made to Viet Nam to entertain the troops.

Bette Midler's portrayal of Janis in the film The Rose gave the public a chance to see the sensitive little child behind the hard rock facade.

Georgia O'Keeffe was one of the great American artists of the 20th century. She grew up ona farm in Wisconsin (ME ASC and NE DSC) and began painting as a child. Showing some interest and some talent, her mother encouraged her to continue with her art lessons. She studied fora time at the Art Institute in Chicago (MA MH), but her enrollment there was short-lived due to family financial difficulties. After spending some time in New York studying and painting (VE MB), she was offered a job ina small town in west Texas (SU and MO ASC) teaching art to schoolchildren. While it was a far cry from what she had hoped at the time, she saw this as the only real opportunity available fora woman artist and used her time there productively. She referred to this part of Texas as her spiritual home many years later. Through friends and acquaintances, particularly her lifelong confidante Anita Pollitzer, she and her work were introduced to the famous New York photographer, gallery owner and patron to young American artists Alfred Stieglitz, who was immediately impressed. He photographed O'Keeffe, had showings for her in his gallery, and eventually became her agent, husband and mouthpiece to the world. This arrangement worked well for the very private, double- Scorpio O'Keeffe, who shunned personal publicity and chitchat, and it continued until Stieglitz's death in 1946. 153€ 26' 119 Bs 18" While O Keeffe's artwork showed much promise and merit, it was so different from anything else then being shown that without Stieglitz's patronage and salesmanship it is doubtful that she would have been so successful so soon. They were together for over 40 years, but the relationship suffered several interruptions, due to Georgia's inability to withstand Stieglitz's active New York social life and her own fierce need for independence. One summer she vacationed in Taos, New Mexico (SU, MO and JU ASC), and soon after, she discovered Abiquiu where she knew she had found her home. She, like the other artists that had come to New Mexico, discovered the brilliance and uniqueness of the light that made painting so special. Using New York City for business purposes and New Mexico for artistic and creative fulfillment, Georgia began a 30-year commute. The summers allowed her to paint to her heart's content, and it was here she did her "bones" series that became so famous. Observing the effect that the clarity of New Mexico's light had upon her increasingly more impressive and saleable artwork, Stieglitz honored O Keeffe with an annual show in New York City (VE MH) each winter. After Stieglitz died, O'Keeffe built a permanent home at Ghost Ranch in Abiquiu and lived there full-time. This was also a period when she began to travel, and she made her first trip to Europe in the early 1950s. Europe did little to impress her with the exception of Spain where she immediately fell in love with the work of Goya. In Italy (MA DSC), she was repelled by what she called the "vulgarity" of Italian art and architecture with its ornate frescoes and giant cherubs. Her style was simple, no frills, and to the point. She continued to paint in her adopted New Mexico home until her death at age 98.

Balzac, born in France under his PL DSC, was a man of extremes who alternately experienced poverty and wealth, starvation and indulgence during his lifetime. His lonely and miserable childhood was mitigated by the development of a great love and understanding of literature. All but neglected by his family, he was passed from one boarding school to another. He was an avid reader and studied law as well. Befitting his PL*MA crossing at his birthplace's latitude, and as a desperate measure, he began writing sensational, slightly pornographic novels, publishing them under a pseudonym. Living in a garage, he was ridden with debts which were increased rather than relieved by 127 his business ventures (ME MH opposite NE IC). So, he wrote with feverish activity, sleeping only a few hours a day. Impelled by these constant financial problems, he produced a vast collection of novels over a 20-year period, the best known of which is The Human Comedy. This work is a microcosm of French society of his time, satirizing in merciless Plutonian detail individuals from every class and profession. It was unique in its depiction of contemporary French street life. Despite great success and notoriety in France, his books were banned in relatively prudish Victorian England. After a 17-year relationship with a Polish noblewoman (JU and SU MH), they married in the Ukraine, but, ironically, he died a few months later.

Franklin D. Roosevelt was elected to and served more than three terms as U.S. President, holding the office longer than anyone else in history. Necessity impelled him to institute many governmental reforms and radical responses to the economic problems of the time, and for these he came to be regarded as a genuine hero in those dark days when the country so desperately needed one. But Roosevelt was scarcely a proletarian. Born into a wealthy, upper-class family, he toured Europe eight times before the age of 16. His political life began with his election to the New York State Senate at age 28. While vacationing in New Brunswick, Canada (UR ASC, MA MH) in 1921, he was stricken with poliomyelitis and was paralyzed from the waist down. By unremitting effort, he recovered partial use of his legs, and, supported by his wife Eleanor, he resumed political 155 life and won the New York gubernatorial race in 1928. In the 1932 U.S. presidential election, he beat incumbent Herbert Hoover and quickly asserted control over the devastated economy. The Japanese invasion of Pearl Harbor catapulted Roosevelt and the nation into World War II. Some historians have suggested that he allowed the attack to occur, fearing that only in the face of open aggression would the war gain sufficient public support. In Pearl Harbor, he has the same planets angular that he had in New Brunswick but on different angles: UR IC and MA along with the MO ASC. In Japan, he had SA ASC, while in Berlin his powerful UR held the MH. JU and PL DSC cross exactly over London, suggesting an odds-defying success. He was supportive of the "Good Neighbor Policy" in Latin America, and with PL MH over Mexico City, he increased American influence in that region. At Warm Springs, Georgia under UR ASC, he founded his institute for the rehabilitation of paraplegics. He died there just before the war ended.

When the Titanic hit an iceberg on the night of April 13, 1912, more was destroyed than the largest and most luxurious ship afloat and the 1500 passengers for whom lifeboats had not been provided in the original plans. Western technology, soaring on a cloud of hubris, had proclaimed the ship "unsinkable," and, ironically, "The Last Word in Luxury." Many of its passengers were millionaires, one of whom, upon being informed that the ship had struck an iceberg, demanded that some of the ice be brought to freshen his drink. The news media, certain that nothing could happen to so great an enterprise, originally ran headlines proclaiming that the ship was intact and was being towed to New York. When the real news followed, a national shock wave ensued, comparable to that of the destruction of the Challenger and the assassination of John F. Kennedy (both events show 291 PL angular). Laws were passed requiring sufficient lifeboats for every passenger, lifeboat drills on every voyage, and, most importantly, federal regulation of radio use. But no laws could reconstitute the goddess of technology, who would never again be quite so omnipotent. Investigation revealed that the captain, intent on a rapid crossing, had maintained full speed despite several radio warnings of icebergs in the vicinity. The ship sank at longitude 50W14, latitude 41N46. This map is drawn for the departure of the ship from Belfast, where it had been built. Before setting out to cross the Atlantic, it stopped several times to board passengers, but in this departure, the first persons who would drown in the frigid dark waters 11 days later embarked. Aside from the fact that this sailing occurred two hours after a total eclipse of the Moon and a couple of days prior to a Mercury retrograde station, the map shows a close conjunction of MA and PL at the MH (in Gemini) at exactly 50W00 longitude. The ship never passed this point.

While Dr. Oppenheimer seems to have adjusted to his new role, most of the rest of us have not. The map for this event shows much about the new age of uranium and plutonium. Books for the Leading Edge of practical and applied astrology as we move toward the culmination of the 20th century. Hello, and welcome to Finding Your Best Places: Using Astrocartography to Navigate Your Life. We can do this now, in ways we never could before, by using today's exciting new art and science of astro cartography. This six-syllable boomer of a word will have to do until we can find something shorter and simpler. It was coined by the late, brilliant astrology master Jim Lewis, whom we'll meet soon. He called it Astro*Carto*Graphy when he invented the system in the 1970s. Cartography, literally "chart writing," just means map making. Astrocartography means that we take the same information an astrologer uses to create birth charts and horoscopes - that is, a person's date, time and place of birth - and use them to create world maps that are personal and unique, just as no two astrology charts are exactly alike. We can also zoom in to detail maps like this one of Indonesia, to look at specific places that interest us, or just seem to be calling us. Each map has a set of colored lines that have planet symbols in triangles that point up to the top of 8 Highlighters the map, or the bottom, or east or west. So the lines show us not only which planet energies are at work in this place, but in which direction they're working: the soul (up), the body (down), our individual goals (east) or relationships (west). In this map almost all the lines have arrows pointing east, so we know that in this place the owner of this map will mainly seek personal goals, individual self-expression and creative strategies for emergence into the world. This will all get clearer soon in The Basics, when we look at all four line directions in our maps. Each line represents a planet, so we can tell from the lines, their parallel combinations and crossings whether any given place favors us for jobs and money, health and learning, love, family and community relationships, creative and spiritual paths, travel destinations, whatever is most important to us. Looking at our maps as well as our charts can tell us not only the conditions of timing that apply to us, but also,

for the first time now, the conditions of space as well. While astrologers have long used different ways of connecting zodiac signs with countries and cities, so that, for example, the very theatrical land of Italy may be called a "Leo country," it is only now that we can see, in precise detail, exactly which places on Earth really favor us, personally and individually, or may have important relationships for us. There are profound spiritual implications to these locational matters as well, and we may find in time that our tendencies, interests, gifts and challenges may all be reflected in the astro-geography of the sky, and this is why we feel attracted to the spiritual traditions and practices of specific places. Time will tell, as our research goes on. But for now, at the very least, we can explore how astrocartography, and other techniques of locational astrology reading may show us what places are most important for the fulfilling of our sacred contracts, and the challenges and opportunities they offer for the pursuit of our spiritual goals, and our evolution toward enlightenment and freedom. More about this in our next chapter. The Shoulders of G iants The recent period of the 1970s to the 1990s can be called without any hyperbole the most important time of innovation and discovery in astrology since the 17th century. It was almost 400 years ago that contemporaries of Galileo pioneered the methods we still use today for calculating the cusps that divide the modern horoscope wheel into its 12 houses. Thanks to their pioneering efforts, we can now do exact reckoning of the four angles of the chart - that is, the main strategic points in each chart that orientate the soul in the self, the world, and social and psychic space. The new house systems helped us determine not only the exact positions of planets in the zodiac signs, but perhaps just as important for us as individuals, how the planets are distributed among the houses of the chart. So let's take a brief look at the astrology terrain as it looked 300 years ago to one of the most famous scientists, yet one of the least recognized astrologers, in history. "If I have seen further," the future Sir Isaac Newton wrote in 1678, "it is by standing on ye sholders [sic] of giants." Those who think of Newton only as one of the greatest physical and mathe

matical minds in history naturally assume the giants must have been Copernicus, Kepler and Galileo. Yet there were others whose names are known only to astrologers, because Newton had a little-known but fascinating secret side as a student of esoteric learning. From his student days at Cambridge until the last years of his life, he wrote more pages of notes on astrology, numerology, alchemy and other occult sciences than he published pages of mathematical theory and law in such famous works as the Principia Mathematica. Fearful of ridicule from the scientific establishment, he kept his esoteric studies wellhidden until they were discovered by his would-be nemesis, the astronomer Edmund Halley, for whom Halley's Comet got its name. The full story is in my book Surfing Aquarius. How is it relevant to us here? Because one of the lesser-known giants whose work Newton surely knew was Placidus de Titis, the astrologer who devel oped the method published by Giovanni Magini (1602) into the Placidus system of houses used by most astrologers today. It remains the standard for Western astrologers, though some use the newer house reckoning method created by Walter Koch (1895 - 1970). The first notable figure in the evolution of locational astrology was Zipporah, better known as Zip Dobyns (1921 - 2003), one of the most admired and prolific astrology authors, lecturers and speakers of the 20th century. She was also instrumental in presenting the case for astrology so eloquently and fearlessly that the greater acceptance astrology has gained over the last half-century is due to her patient efforts ever since she began to devote herself to astrology full time in 1956. Her contributions to astrology were wide-ranging and she was especially noted for her mastery in using astrology for the healing of relationships. She was also a major figure in the development of locational astrology, especially in her classic book Planets on the Move, with Maritha Pottenger. The premise of Relocation Astrology, as they and others have developed it, is simple. Cast a chart for the client's actual date and time of birth, but for a different place. Doing this will not change the planets' positions in the zodiac signs, but it can radically change their house positions. Suppose you have a strong planet alignment that has always helped you in your 3rd house of

communications, but you wish it would start generating more revenue. Well, what if you chose a place you like in an adjoining time zone, and recast your chart for that place, so that your very efficacious 3rd house planet cluster would now move to your second house of money? Would your income go up, and your whole financial position improve? Well, yes, and no. Results reported by users of relocation astrol ogy show that yes, it does work, provided that the other essential pieces of good timing, sound decision making and skillful intentional practice are also in place, so the relocation has its best shot at success. The same thing, for that matter, can be said about the other branches of locational astrology that we're exploring here, including astrocartography. They won't work in isolation, any more than we can hope to overcome a severe illness without the combination of good nutrition, exercise, positive thoughts and as sociations that may prove to be more effective than the medical therapy itself.

Dobyns and the other astrologers of her generation benefited hugely from the work of those born in the next generation. The ones born in the 1930s and 1940s accomplished the historic breakthrough: the digital revolution that transformed astrology in the 1970s as radically as it changed everything else. It was time for the queen of the sciences to start dating a genius again, this time one who could work with com puters the way other men whisper to horses. Neil F. Michelsen (1931 - 1990) was one of those rare types who are scientific-minded, yet open to metaphysical possibilities. An honors graduate in mathematics at the University of Miami, he joined IBM at the onset of his Saturn return (see Saturn in The Planets for more about this) and was soon working among IBM's most brilliant computer minds at its White Plains NY headquarters. He got curious enough about the mathematics of astrology to attend a workshop by Zip Dobyns, and was immediately inspired to program the calculations needed to construct an astrology chart on an IBM 1130 computer. Three years later he created Astro Computing Services, and in 1976 he launched ACS Publications by releasing The American Ephemeris 1931 - 1980, a landmark event that established the US as one of the new, leading countries in a field that had traditionally been dominated by Europeans.

Michelsen's work began the process that would soon revolutionize astrology by freeing as trologers from the cumbersome business of casting charts manually with reference books on time zones and house cusps, so it now became possible to generate a chart within seconds, and reallocate to client service and new research the time that had always been needed for routine calculations. The rigorous standards that Michelsen had always applied, and his insistence that ACS ephemerides be corrected as new data became available, have been continued by his star pupil, Rique Pottenger. Their relationship as mentor and disciple has made the New American Ephemeris for the 21st Century the standard for accuracy. While Michelsen did not devote his efforts to locational astrology, his work either inspired, or lent greater urgency, to the new directions that would be taken by other genius pioneers whose work made the 1970s a time of ambitious attempts and breakthrough discoveries not seen since Placidus redefined the house cusps at the dawn of the modern era. One of them is the tirelessly energetic polymath Michael Erlewine (1941 -). He has been prolific as an astrologer and entrepreneur, and as a musician with the chops to play with, among many others, the young Bob Dylan.

He has written dozens of e-books that can be downloaded for free from his website, so he was walking the talk of the Gift Economy decades before it started to become the buzzword it is now. He was the one who took the next invaluable step beyond what Neil Michelsen had prepared, by founding Matrix Software (1977) and creating the first astrology programs for microcomputers, thereby blazing the trail followed by astrology software companies ever since. More important for our purposes here, he was among the first, if not the first, to crack the algorithms needed for locational astrology. His best-known contribution to the field is called Local Space Astrology, also the title of a book that outlines the purpose and method of this new approach. It is a clear step beyond the limits of Relocation Astrology because it does not just propose one or more alternate locations to one's actual birthplace, but projects personal planet energy lines around the entire Earth. How does it work? Imagine that you could superimpose your birth chart on the globe, so that your birthplace is at the exact center of the wheel, and the houses, zodiac signs and planets are all arrayed in a circle around it. Then draw a line from the center through each planet's position, and continue the line all around the sphere until it returns to the center. The result will be your personal arrangement of planetary lines that have irregular intervals of space between them, just as the planet placements in your chart can range from the conjunctions of planets only a few degrees apart, to planets that are separated by the wide open spaces of empty signs and houses in your chart. Each of the planet lines that encircles the Earth in Local Space Astrology marks an energy band where that planet's energy should be especially strong, offering uncommon advantages and challenges, depending on the nature of each planet. In theory, then, areas crossed by our Mercury lines would be active zones for communications, promoting successful results in such communicative activities as writing, editing, teaching, sales, promotion, social life, and, for that matter, larceny, as Mercury is the pa tron planet of thieves and sharp traders. More about this in Chapter 3. The same could be said, then, of other planet lines: uncommonly good prospects for money, love and power relationships under Venus and Jupiter lines; possibilities ranging from physical strength and athletic success to conflict and violence under the Mars line; foggy-mindedness, vivid dreams, troubled sleep and blurry self-esteem along with imagination, intuition and creativity, especially in fantasy-related performing arts, along the Neptune line. The good news here is that now the possibilities of each of your planets are literally world-encircling, showing places all over the globe that can be fertile ground for your best efforts. The tough news, though, is that each planet is represented by only one line. Enter Jim L ewis, B earing Astro*Carto*Graphy But what if each planet's energy could operate in the world through multiple lines? What if a design similar in some ways to Local Space Astrology could somehow be rotated, in the way that architects discovered how to rotate an arch to create a three-dimensional dome? It was time for the birth of Astro*Carto*Graphy.

Jim Lewis (1941 - 1995) effectively quadrupled the possibilities of Local Space Astrology by creating a new system of locational astrology based on the natal positions of the planets and the Moon's Nodes, and the four angles of the chart. By keying his system to the respective directions of (1) the soul, (2) the body, (3) the self projecting itself into the world as an individual creative force, and (4) the self finding its limits, balances and synergies in relationships with others, Lewis constructed a far more complex and dynamic design of 48 planet and nodal lines, plus crossing points corresponding to the planets' angles of relationship. He also devised a body of interpretative lore on the meaning of each line and crossing, presenting it in his posthumously published book The Psychology of Astrocartography, and in the booklets prepared for clients of his Astro*Carto*Graphy website. He also created Cyclo*Carto*Graphy in answer to the inevitable question: Do the lines in my natal ACG map change over time? They do, as he showed, in one of the topics he was working on when he passed away from a congenital cerebral tumor at only 53. It has been nearly a quarter century now since Jim Lewis left us, and those who admire his work and revere his brilliance naturally wonder what he might have done had he lived longer, and what kind of magnum opus he might have produced as the definitive summation of his life's work in astrocartography. It would certainly have reached beyond the limits of the technology available to him in the 1970s. The original Astro*Carto*Graphy packages, like the one I received when I was a beginning astrologer in 1977, consisted of an A5-size booklet, with a single black and white world map in the centerfold, preceded by the basic information on how to use the system, and followed by a list of line and crossing interpretations. The same basic design appeared in The Astro*Carto*Graphy Book of Maps, each one presenting a single world map, though now in a larger book format, with its commentary on the natal planet lines of a well-known person. It is puzzling, given the rapid refinements in computer software graphics during the 1970s and 1980s, that the map design Jim Lewis' Astro*Carto*Graphy website used in preparing map packages for clients, and that he used as an author in the presentation of his work, hardly evolved at all in the nearly decade and a half that elapsed between his breakthrough researches in the mid-1970s and The Astro*Carto*G-

raphy Book of Maps in 1989. But those who have written about his life have more than hinted at a possible explanation. Jim Lewis was, to put it mildly, very much a hands-on trainer and certifier, insisting that those whom he would approve as qualified to practice his system - he personally taught and certified about eighty fellow astrocartographers in the last two decades of his life - pass an uncommonly rigorous set of exams. He has also been described as extremely litigious in taking action against those who claimed to practice his system without being officially qualified. He may have been too busy defending his brand to keep it current with the newest computer graphic technologies. We will never know what culminating work Jim Lewis might have produced if he had lived into his sixties and seventies, and whether, as seems likely, he would have created new software that could generate the full-color world map and detail maps used in this book, all prepared with the Io Cartography program by Time Cycles Research. We'll also never know, until another astrocartography genius compa rable to Jim Lewis appears, what other trails he or she will blaze that are unimaginable to us now. What we do know is that it is time for e-books on astrocartography, if only because a conventional paper book with eighty color maps will be so costly to produce that a book publisher would have to be near a high-courage Mars line to contemplate it at all. It is time for books that can use state-of-the-art software to present ACG to readers who are neither professional astrologers nor certified psychologists, but are convinced that astrology is worthy of study, may already be using it for spiritual exploration and personal guidance, may want to know more about how ACG applies personally to them, and how, in the practical examples and stories of people very much like themselves, we can see how accurate ACG is in showing how people who've used it, and made their moves, have benefited from the insights a percep tive astrocartographer can provide. It is time now to go where Jim Lewis might have gone if he were still here. The shadow he still casts would be gigantic even if he hadn't been extraordinarily tall. Clearly, no one thinks lightly about trying to follow the spectacular act he played. Anyone who actually thinks of billing himself as the successor to Jim Lewis had best meditate on the line from The Mahabharata: "No worthy man speaks in praise of himself." It may be that the main thing that qualifies me to write this book, apart from 38 years of professional astrology practice and work with thousands of clients, is that as a young man I was an actor specializing in comedy, so I'm accustomed to being laughed at. It may be true, as it's often been said, that to succeed in show business, you don't need talent. You just need courage. The same thing may apply now to writ ing about astrocartography. Before we cover the basic principles and rules, the planets and the moon's nodes, and the twenty stories that are the main material of this book, it's time to look briefly at one more giant, and her system of spiritual self-guidance. Jim Lewis never specifically mentioned her in his work. Yet many astrologers use her method as a way of showing to our clients how the life paths we've chosen, and the blocks and turns and bumps we've met on the way, may all be the working out of a design we created before we came here. The Sacred Contract and Spiritual Astrology

For many spiritual astrologers, not just those who do locational astrology readings, one of the core texts that resonates very deeply is Sacred Contracts, the brilliant book by Carolyn Myss (1952 —). The book is astrology-related, using the 12-part design of the horoscope wheel to arrange the archetypes we play within the scenario of the hero's journey that each of us travels. The spiritual issues and challenges we've come to face in this lifetime are clearly related to our birth chart, which can be called - along with the archetypal patterns of the Tarot, the I Ching, the Qabbalah and other symbolic systems - a diagram of the sacred contract, with a special emphasis on the challenges we've come to face and master in this life. Our ACG maps are also related to the sacred contract, so it will be useful here to cover what sacred con tracts are, how we create them, and how they play out in our lives. One of Ms. Myss's key premises, stated simply, is that before we are even conceived by our parents, much less before we're actually born on earth, we sit down with our soul and design our new life mission, like an actor or musician negotiating with a talent agent. The implications of this are enormous. It means that we choose our parents and our other crucial relationships — or we offer them roles and they choose to accept them — but one way or the other, we are responsible for our choices even before we get here, and our life scenario is thus an unfolding of a script we've already written in the spirit world. When the negotiating is done, we accept the deal as perfect, even though there must be some suffering in it, as there always is in third density here on Earth. When we are born, and we descend through the thousands of veils that the Sufis imagine between the light of Spirit and the darkness of the material world, we have forgotten everything, and this is why the theme of remembering is common to so many spiritual traditions, in two main senses of the word. It may entail recollection of where we have come from and what we've come to do. It may also mean the reconnection of dismembered pieces of our lives, so that work and career, health, creativity, love, service and spirituality, which can get so disconnected from one another that some of them even seem not to be present for us at all, come into a complete and harmonious whole. The terms of the sacred con
1.) The Main Mission: Planets that are in close relationships of leverage in our birth charts - that is, at 0

conjunctions, 90° "squares" and 180° oppositions — appear in our ACG maps as planet lines that run in close parallels and convergences through our maps. The densest line formations in our maps often go through places where we're naturally drawn, conscious or ready or not, to go after our mission. That much is clear in this map of a man who has a dense set of oppositions, in his natal chart, so here a complex and not-for-the-faint-hearted set of lines runs through the Middle East, Siberia to the north, and East Africa to the south. Questions of our karma are naturally related to our main mission, and the opinions of spiritual astrologers can vary a lot about how relevant this is. For many spiritual astrology practitioners, even those who don't incorporate the sacred contract paradigm into our work, the idea that our birth chart contains clues to karmic issues - in the Moon's Nodes, for example, as we'll soon see — the statement by Sri Yukteswar is still likely to resonate: "A child 11 Hiahlicjhters is born on that day and at that hour when the celestial rays are in mathematical harmony with his individ ual karma." 2. ) The Compensation Package: talents and advantages that we bring into this life with us, like a wallet or tool kit, to help us pursue our goals. These will manifest most clearly in the "positive" planet placements and relationships that identify our natural abilities and tendencies in areas where we're most likely to succeed. They may be connected in our locational maps with places where "benefic" lines (Sun, Moon, Venus, Jupiter) are present. 3. ) The Non-Performance Clause. The planet Saturn is particularly connected with this, as his role of the demanding teacher often involves pushing against us in order to make us exert a greater effort toward what we say we want. His lines often appear in locations where circumstances compel us to face and begin working out challenges that we tend to resist until we have no choice but to acknowledge and address them. When we do, we can access the higher harmonic of a Saturn line, and see if Saturn will help us carry out our commitments.

4. ) The Limits and Restrictions, without which there is no point in coming to Earth. These will often manifest in our birth charts through the "malefic" planets, especially when they're in stressful angles of relationship with one another, or other planets. And when they're clustered in the same house or adjoining houses, then in the affairs of those houses we'll likely meet conflict (Mars), restriction (Saturn), power struggles (Pluto), upsets and accidents (Uranus), and vagueness, deception and delusion, by oneself or others (Neptune). The last of these was especially triggered by the long-running Chiron and Neptune conjunction in 2009 - 2012. Many people who have planets in late Aquarius and Pisces have reported difficulty in piercing Neptune's fog so that they can see the road ahead clearly, set priorities and make sound decisions. These people have, not surprisingly, often lived in, or had relationship with, areas where their Neptune lines were present. 5. ) The Opportunities, which in a legal contract take the form of incentives, often appear as advantages in our charts and maps, and are also closely connected with planet transits: that is, the movements of planets in real time, in the present and future, as they form angles of relationship with planets and other key points in our birth charts. This is the basis of predictive astrology, as planet motions indicate for each of us when we can move ahead strongly and proactively with what we intend, and when it is best to do the visioning, planning and team-building, and the rest of the preparation for what we'll do when the time is right. Given the delicious perversity of our third density, opportunities have a way of showing up when we're so discouraged by the troubles that we can't recognize our best chances when they do come. But an ACG reading, especially when it also covers our birth chart and transits, can illuminate the moment of the heroic choice, when we summon the clarity and courage to move from restriction, fog and fear to seeing and doing the mission we've come to carry out. We'll look at some heroic choices here, after we get fa miliar with the basic astrocartography terrain.

Astrocartography (ACG) is based on the technology and star lore of the late Jim Lewis, the brilliant astrologer who pioneered both astrocartography and cyclo-cartography. The body of ACG interpretation that Lewis developed in the 1970s has been indispensable ever since to the work of astrocartographers everywhere, and is included as well in his seminal, posthumously-published book The Psychology of Astro*Carto*Graphy (1997). In all the maps we'll explore in this book, four rules apply: I. The Angles of the Horoscope Wheel, and the Directional Arrows in the ACG Maps: This is the most important of the rules, and can be intricate enough, even for people who are more than just acquainted with astrology, that some careful explanation may be useful here. If you look at the famous chart we're about to explore, you'll see a four-armed cross formed by one bold line that spans the chart horizontally from left center to right center, and another vertical bold line that runs from the top center to the bottom center.

July 1, 1961, 7:45pm GMD, Sandringham, UK The points at the ends of the cross are the four key strategic points called angles, Each of them has a specific energy and meaning, and a directional thrust to its energy in our ACG maps. The four angles are:

1. ) The Ascendant, or Rising Point. This is the best-known of the four angles. It's at the left of the chart, between the 12th and 1st houses, and is the cusp of the first house, that is, the door that opens it. The Ascendant in our birth chart marks the point in the zodiac that was on the eastern horizon at the moment we were born. So just as the Moon, Sun and planets seem to rise from this point every day, this Rising Sign also identifies our own rising qualities: that is, the way we project our personality and intentions "outward" into the world, pursue our personal objectives, and tell other people and the world who we are. Princess Diana was Sagittarius Rising, so the direct, outward energy of this point was likely to express itself in a quick, mutable tempo in her movements, moods and self-expression. The Ascendant lines in our ACG maps are curving and sinusoidal, with directional triangles that point East, to the right. 2. ) The Imum Coeli (IC) or Nadir. The Nadir is located at the bottom center of the chart between the 3rd and 4th houses. The word "nadir" in astrology does not have the negative nuance that this word often carries in English usage. It does not mean "the low point" or "the worst," but it means the material foundation of our life, and the way we support ourselves in practical terms on the Earth plane, because the Nadir is the point at the center of the Earth below our feet. The Nadir point is also the cusp of the 4th house of the home and the mother, so it represents the dimension of practical reality, our sense of being grounded and rooted, and of being protected and secure in what is comfortable and familiar. With adventurous, restless Aries on the Nadir, however, Diana was apt to prefer a life in motion. The vertical Nadir lines in our ACG maps have arrowheads that point down and touch the bottom of the map. 3. ) The Descendant (DSC). The Descendant, at the right of the astrology chart between the 6th and 7th houses, is opposite the Ascendant, so it's the point that was on the western horizon when we were born. In general terms, the left side of the chart is the rising of our individuality, while the right side is the setting of our individuality as we accept adjustments and compromises of our personal freedom in relationship with others. The 7th house is central to the right side of the chart because it's the house of marriage and of all partnerships: that is, two people connected in a relationship of equality. Diana had Gemini on the DSC, yet her Sun and Mercury here, in the maternal sign of Cancer, clearly embodied her official role as Mother. The curving Descendant lines in our ACG maps have triangles that point West, to the left. 4. ) The Midheaven (MC for Medium Coeli). The Midheaven, at the top of the chart between our 9th and 10th houses, is the zodiac point that was in the center of the sky above us when we were born, so it's true north in our spiritual compass (even though the MC does not correspond to directional north in our maps). The MC is the spiritual thrust of our chart, our approach to our soul desires, and it embodies our 16 Highlighters most authentic values and goals, so that as long as we act in accordance with what it represents, we'll feel our actions are truthful. As the MC is on the cusp of the 10th house of our profession, it is also often connected with our most important career objectives, our way of being seen in the world, and identified with what we do in the larger realm of public action. The vertical MC lines in our ACG maps have ar rowheads that point up and touch the top of the map.
