II. L ine Crossings There are two basic line configurations in an ACG map: vertical (MC and Nadir) and sinusoidal: that is, curving horizontally through the map from east to west. This means that the maps have dozens of line crossings, in which not only each planet line and its direction is meaningful, but the blending of their en ergies at the crossing points has a specific meaning too. This map is a good example: In this map of Colombia, Ecuador and Peru's north coast, the royal blue Jupiter on the Descendant line favors prosperous relationships, often with powerful and influential movers and shakers. The purple Uranus line has excitement and discovery in it, as all Uranus lines do, but this one points to the Nadir,

and therefore signifies that life here can be unstable, and involve frequent moves from one living space to another. The crossing of these lines marks what Jim Lewis called "your unique magical good luck zone." Here our plans can come to quick success, we can experience unexpected gains with little or no effort to bring them about, even windfalls. We can find that the time lag between conceiving an intention and bringing it to manifestation shrinks to nothing, so we have the appearance of being miracle workers. The technical term for these line crossings in our ACG maps is parans, which is short for paranatellonta, a Greek word that means "rising together." These crossings occur in our natal maps because at the moment of birth, two or more planets were at the angles of the zodiac wheel. For example, in the map we've just seen, Jupiter was near the Descendant at the right of the chart at the moment this person was born, and Uranus was near the Nadir at the bottom. This is why the paran of these two planets appears so close to the Equator. This bears a little more explaining, and it will be worth our while to cover it briefly here. Imagine that the Ascendant in your chart points due east, the Descendant due west, and that these points are on the Equator, which corresponds on the globe of the Earth to our local horizon, where we imagine the planets as rising (ASC) and setting (DSC). The closer planets are to the ASC - DSC axis of our charts, the closer their parans will be to the Equator. The farther away planets are from the ASC- DSC line in our charts, then the farther away from the Equator their crossing points in our maps must be. This is why the crossing points in our maps range all the way up toward the North Pole along our vertical Midheaven (MC) lines, and down to the South pole along the other vertical Nadir line. The horizontal chart points of the ASC and DSC are always exactly opposite to each other in our charts, just as due east and due west are exactly opposite. The same is true of the MC and Nadir points. Each planet in the chart is at an exact distance from every other planet and from all four angles. So as there are four angular points in the chart, there must be four parans for each pair of planets. They must be at consistent distances from the angular points. In the same way, there must be four crossing points in our maps for each pair of planets - and these crossing points have to be at the same distance from the equator. So. If we return to the map crossing where we started, near Piura in north Peru, and we trace a line due east or west, we arrive at the opposite crossing point, between the Malaysian peninsula and the In donesian island of Sumatra.

other side of the Earth. The arrows on the two map lines point in the opposite directions, the blue Jupiter line east to the ASC, the purple Uranus line up to the MC. If we then go along the same latitude to the east and west, we find two more crossings. One is on the west coast of Africa near Libreville in Gabon, and in the Pacific Ocean southwest of Hawaii. The main idea is that the four crossing points of each pair of planets are at the same latitude, so a line connecting them would trace the same latitude all around the Earth. Do the four crossings have an energetic connection as well as relationship in space? Jim Lewis thought they might, and one of the special research topics that drew his attention in his later years was the question of whether the planetary forces that meet at a crossing also extend along the latitude lines, and may even be in effect in a com plete circuit around the Earth. This brings us to our next question: What's the range of the lines and crossing points? Over what distances are they powerful and influential? III. E ffective Range of Lines and Crossing Points While there are differences of opinion among astrocartographers about the effective range of planet lines, and some believe that a line's range may extend to 700 miles, or even more, the safest bet, the closest estimate to a consensus, is that the lines are powerful to a distance of 500 kilometers, or 300 miles, to either side. The closer a line is to a point on your map, the stronger its impact. The same general rule applies to a line crossing. Its effective area extends out to a radius of 300 miles, or 500 km, from the crossing point. As we've seen above, Jim Lewis and other astrocartographers have speculated that the power of a crossing may extend east and west along the line of its latitude, and may even form an energy band all the way around the planet, where we could expect the same energy to be present, and the same possible outcomes in our lives. The experiments with this possibility, including the author's, continue. Perhaps one day each of us will envision our personal Earth ringed by our individual bar code patterns of colored planet lines, each one different, because they're determined

by the distinctive parans in our birth charts. All right. Now we know what kinds of lines we have, where they go, and how they work. What do we do with all this information? Do we just figure out our best place, and get ready to move there? Not really.

IV. If Your Best Lines Aren't Near You — You Don't Have to Move! Astrocartography projects our personal planetary energy lines chart on a world map, and thus shows the easiest - and the most challenging - places for creating prosperity and success, love and family, health, the experience of community, spiritual insight, and other goals. So it's useful for people who feel the place where they are now is energetically played out for them, and it's time to move on. Or they're entering a new creative phase, or changing their goals, leaving an old relationship or beginning a new one, and they want the best place for a fresh start. Or they want to leave the city and the electronic chat ter behind and go to a more Earth-friendly intentional community, even off the grid altogether. But most people want a place where they can live for decades, even a lifetime, and they're about as perfectly happy as they can be in the place where they are. Does this mean astrocartography has nothing to offer them? No. Our map lines don't only show us where we will do well, or not. They can show us where important relationships are: with employers and investors, teachers and healers, communities, and partners for love and creative work. Our best sales territories may be under our Mercury lines. Our pub- 7 Highlighters--lishers are waiting along our Jupiter lines. Saturn lines can help our children choose a university. Venus lines point to love. Moon's lines show a woman's best place to give birth and raise her children. Sun lines show where we can succeed, gain recognition and literally shine in the world. And so on. For example, this map belongs to a photographer who likes it where he lives in New York, but has strong lines in Switzerland, especially near Geneva, where a purple Uranus on the MC line indicates excellent prospects for the kind of cutting-edge, high tech work this artist does. It also fits an imaginative, proactive move he made in opening a new market, by creating successful relationships with art dealers and galleries in Geneva who exhibit and sell his work. It's booming. He sells as much of his work here as he does in his home market of New York. And, as the red Mars on the MC line shows, farther east but still in range of Geneva, the artist and those who work with him here will have the courage to be co-pioneers in introducing to this part of the world a new art style never seen here before. As we'll see in some of the stories in this book, the same is true of many people who choose one location for living, but find their best work and love opportunities in other places. It is really no exaggeration to say that the key difference between Jim Lewis' original astrocar tography, and the ACG that second- and third-generation astrocartographers practice now, is that its emphasis has shifted from the main personal question of Where Should I Live? - and now includes the
interpersonal questions too: Where Are My Contacts? Where Are My Connections? My Opportunities?

Astrocartography had to evolve when it did because it's a guide to finding and building relationships as much as it's a key element of what true astrology has always been, a system of spiritual study and self-direction. Our field of vision now inevitably goes much wider, to cover the fields of interest that we share with others in our social, business and creative lives. The internet, cell phones and other Aquarian technologies connect us closer every year with people all over the world. We work by Skype with clients and colleagues we've never met. We can have thousands of Facebook friends whom we've seen only in online photos, and whose voices we've never heard. Children who've never been a hundred miles from home know people everywhere, and have bigger networks than their parents ever imagined. The connection is what counts now, in the time of the Aquarian Awakening. Aquarius is, after all, the sign of friends, social activity and activism, and community. As more and more of us work on building intentional communities across all the traditional boundaries of countries, religions and jobs, and we look beyond to our greater spiritual goals of planetary health and service, universal peace and brotherhood, we naturally seek the most powerful ways to find the relationships that will help us magnetize our goals. That's why astrocartography is hot, and getting hotter by the year, as our world moves faster and we bring our best possibilities closer. It's all in the relationships.

Now that we know the basic rules about astrocartography, it's time to meet the players in the grand design, the mythic figures and energies who appear in our natal charts as planet symbols, and in our maps as colored lines that cross the Earth vertically like longitudinal meridians, and horizontally in the shape of sine curves related to the position of the Equator. The planets all astrologers work with today include the original "Seven Stars" visible with the naked eye - that is, the Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn, and three planets discovered in recent centuries: Uranus, Neptune and Pluto. We will not pause here to discuss the disgraceful action taken by only 4% of the International Astronomers' Union in "demoting" Pluto from his status as a true planet. Astrologers, who see each planet as a conscious spiritual energy rather than a mere lump of rock or ball of gas, have no doubt that Pluto fully qualifies. So does Chiron, even though he is officially considered as an asteroid. As we'll see in the sub-chapter about him, Chiron the Healer is studied by growing numbers of astrologers, and known to more and more of our clients, because of Chiron's connection not only with the healing arts, but with our own issues of wounding and being wounded, and we recognize the 50-year in terval of the Chiron Return as one of our crucial life passages. Also included here are the Moon's Nodes, which appear in our ACG maps as well as our charts because they're meaningful indicators of conditions in our relationships, especially with associations, alliances and other groups of people, and they relate as well to the karmic forces and directions at work in our lives. We'll look at each planet's conditions of timing, its mythic story and archetypal significance, and its personality and occupational type. The astrocartography information about each planet comes at the end of its subchapter, as we look at its directions of action in our spiritual and professional lives (the Midheaven, or MC), the material plane (Nadir), our individual emergence and personal intentions (Ascendant, or ASC) and our roles and positions in marriage, love rela tionships and other partnerships (Descendant, or DSC). It's time to meet the planets. Here comes the Sun. The Sun: Shining in the World

The Sun is the central conscious energy body in our planetary system. So important is the Sun that people interested in "Sun sign astrology" will usually ask another person only "What's your sign?" as if this alone could tell us in depth about anyone's personality, talents and tendencies. Yet there is no getting around it: while the Sun is only one of 17 major points — eleven planets, two Moon's Nodes and four angles (see The Basics) - in a person's birth chart, he is clearly the most important player, the ruler of the system, around whom all the other planets revolve. The Sun rules the regal fire sign of Leo and, in the northern hemisphere, the hottest month of mid-Summer. In the zodiac wheel, he rules the 5th house of creative expression, children, play and love affairs (as distinct from 7th house marriages). Shown above in one of his lordly Greek identities as Helios Apollo, he naturally embodies such positions of rulership as political leaders and authority figures, including fathers. It is no accident that many famous rulers - Napoleon, Mussolini, Fidel Castro, Hugo Chavez, Bill Clinton, Barack Obama - are all Sun-ruled Leos. The Sun is perfectly comfortable letting his light shine, and this is why such versatile actors as Dustin Hoffman, Kevin Spacey, Robert De Niro, Steve Martin, Sean Penn and Philip Seymour Hoffman, among many others, all express in their work the theatricality of Leo and the Sun. The Sun's positive traits include optimism, breadth of vision, magnanimity, generosity, spon taneity and a hearty good humor. He has little guile, and so attracts those who have a lot more, and he may have to learn the hard way to keep his counsel and give his trust more judiciously. The Sun is a natural seeker of attention and control, and has little desire to share power or ac claim with anyone else, and this is why there are many famous mythic stories - like

Ra (shown here) tricked by Thoth, and baby Hermes stealing Apollo's cattle — in which an over confident powerful being is outwitted by another who is less mighty, but more inventive and less complacent. This is the fundamental scenario of comedy, for the Sun's pride is his weakness. He is no respecter of boundaries. He'll seek status in any environment he occupies, and, given the flamboyant theatricality of his nature, can be self-important — so when human beings are playing their dramas on one another, the Sun's usually in a starring role. His longing to be noticed and praised, and his preference for the one-up position in relationships, may help explain why all the Sun lines in our astrocartographs are strong and beneficial by themselves, yet may be less help ful and advantageous when crossed by other lines. The yellow Sun lines in our Astrocartography maps show the places where we are most 16 Highlighterslikely to shine, gain attention and charisma, achieve professional and social position, and spread our influence through publication and performance, the Sun is abundant in his creativity, so that under his lines we may discover new creative avenues, and greater confidence in using our gifts. For some astrocartographers, the Sun on the MC line is the best one in our entire map. It is sometimes called the Fame Line because it marks the locations where we achieve professional success, gain recognition for our accomplishments, and advance socially with the help of advan tageous contacts. A brilliant career may trump everything else here, and can create a need for social climbing. The Sun on the Ascendant line favors the projecting of one's personal power and leadership into the outer environments of politics, business and society, especially when the Sun in one's birth chart is the "rising planet" in the first house, close to the Ascendant line. This is why this Sun position, expressing as it does a desire to shine in the world, is often found in the charts of peo ple who aspire to political and religious authority, and may actually achieve it. The possibilities of acclaim for one's creative successes are high under this line, so it also carries the risks of all the prancing and preening that can come when the limelight has captured us. Sun lines can be "everything lines," unlike other planet lines that pertain mainly to power and money, health and learning and other specific areas of life, and the best example of a Sun line's all-embracing sweep may be the Sun on the Nadir line, for it favors locations in which we are healthy, financially secure, happily partnered and socially prosperous, blessed by an active and loving circle of friends. As most people seek to enjoy all these advantages in later life, this line is sometimes called, not so surprisingly, the Retirement Line. The Sun on the Descendant line is one I know well. I'm writing this book a few miles from it in a place that favors the building of relationships for intellectual work, project organization, publication and performance. I've published two books while living under this line in Peru; and have built good relationships not only with people in the local community, but with people all over the world who seem to find me under this line. Productive partnerships flourish here, especially with colleagues in Europe and the Americas.

Considered in spiritual terms, the Sun is the most luminous and powerful of the planets, so he also bears the greatest risk of vanity, ego clinging and self-aggrandizement. Laurence Olivier (a Gemini, not a Leo) was once asked what made theatre special, and different from the other arts. He replied, "Look at me !" Those who live Sun lines in their full radiance and arrogance may in time have cause to wonder whether there is anything to me at all, any spark or substance inside this role I play so proudly. The Embrace of the Mother: The Moon Considered only in the materialist terms of physical "science," the Moon is not a planet at all, only a satellite that circles the Earth in a visible orbit of 28 days - so this number is associated everywhere with the labyrinth and the sacred feminine, and a synodic cycle of 291/2 days, includ ing the Black Moon time of invisibility before she reappears each month. Since ancient times, before solar calendars emerged, her monthly cycle, and the timing of the female body, have been the basis of lunar calendars that are keyed to the lunations - New and Full Moons - that are key points of sacred timekeeping for the Hindu, Buddhist, Muslim, Taoist, and Celtic-Druidic traditions, and for indigenous peoples. The Moon's rebirth each month at the thin crescent of the New Moon was our first celestial symbol of immortality, suggesting that we too might be reborn after the passing of the physical body. The Moon rules the water sign of Cancer and the 4th house of the Home and the Mother in the horoscope wheel. Thus she is naturally associated with birth and the "inner" domestic pole of our lives, opposite to the "outer" professional pole of the Father and the 10th house. She embodies the emotional, intuitive and receptive side of our being, and the maternal virtues of nurturing, protection and compassion. So Moon and Cancer occupations naturally include moth erhood and midwifery, nursing and child care, home economics and organizations of sisterhood relationships among groups and communities of women. The Moon and her sign of Cancer are said to be sensitive, indirect in the sideways manner of the Crab, and vulnerable.

Yet she also has the quiet fortitude of one who endures the searing pain of childbirth, and some of history's fiercest characters - Alexander the Great, Julius Caesar, Meryl Streep - have been lunar personalities, or have at least, like the Dalai Lama, John D. Rockefeller and Nelson Mandela, brought the Mother's patient determination to their pursuit of great goals. A surprising number of successful prize fighters, like Mike Tyson, Jack Dempsey and Julio Cesar Chavez, have been Moon-ruled, perhaps because the boxing ring itself is their home turf, which they defend with all they've got. But no matter what extraordinary men have been born in Cancer, it is still the Moon women like Emma Goldman, Frida Kahlo, Princess Diana and Ginger Rogers - famously said to be able to do everything Fred Astaire did, only backwards and in high heels - who embody the uncommon flexibility, ingenuity and perseverance that the Moon has always represented in our experience and vision, her ability to keep coming back and staying the course no matter what happens, in, as a famous noh play Hagoromo says, the "dance that makes to turn the towers of the Moon." The Moon rules the realm of imagination, as in this painting by Henri Rousseau, and is connected with the unlimited possibilities of night, as contrasted with the "factual" and "real" solar dimension of the light of day. To "sing down the Moon" means that we use sound and intention to realize imaginative vision in concrete terms. So as we now understand and practice manifestation more skillfully than we did before, many people live by the Moon, following her cycles carefully to time important actions. There are three main points in each cycle. At the Black or Dark Moon, the invisible Moon is aligned with the Sun at a moment that favors psychic receptivity and the driving of our efforts with powerful currents of emotion, which is why we set new individual and communal intentions at the Black Moon. At the New Moon, which comes two days later when the first new crescent Moon appears, we launch the new intentions into action. At the Full Moon we bring them to culmination and completion. Plato wrote about the difference between the Black Moon, when Moon and Sun are in conjunction, and the Full Moon, when they're opposed: "When planets are in conjunction, all of society implodes. When planets

are in opposition, all of society expands, innovates, and prospers." This applies to private lives as well as to communities. People here may come to appreciate Groucho Marx's line: "There's nothing better than a close-knit, loving family living 200 miles away." Let the L istener Heed, Let the B uyer B eware: Mercury Mercury the Messenger and Communicator is the "innermost" planet in our solar system, the one closest to the Sun. His orbit around the Sun takes only 116 days, so he is by far the fastest-

moving of the planets, and his rapid motion has always linked him, since very ancient times, with the speed of thought itself, and the element of air. This is why he's been linked with bird beings like the ibis-headed Egyptian deity Djehuti, or Thoth (below), said to have been the inventor of writing, mathematics, music, and astrology - in other words, all arts that rely on precise reckoning of exact data in words and numbers. Thoth also embodied the idea of a universal core Truth above and apart from all practical facts and figures, and divine wisdom available to those with the devotion to seek it. Like all the Neters of Egypt - that is, manifestations of The One Divine being, often in the animal forms of nature (nature
came from neter) - Thoth had an ibis' head for a reason that was clear to the people of the Nile.

knew the ibis always seeks the place in the lake or the stream where the water is purest, like Truth itself, symbolized also by the feather that often stands straight up from Thoth's crown chakra, like the single feather worn by the feminine netert Ma'at, Lady of Truth. Thoth - Hermes is thus the patron deity and ruling planet of thinkers, writers, editors and all seekers of not only a practical and commonly-accepted everyday "truth," but the Truth with a capital T. The Greeks, though, brought winged truth closer to Earth, and into the forum and the market. Crafty Odysseus, the "man of many plots," would have understood why Hermes, or Mercury, as the Romans called him, was also invoked by lawyers and other orators, salesmen and mer chants, and why he's also the patron of thieves. After all, the quick, sharp force of the intellect can be used not only to convey the true story, but also to bend and hide it. Like all the planets and zodiac signs, Mercury too can be a whole spectrum of ethics and qualities, from the noblest, kindest and most loving to the meanest and cruelest. So people born under Gemini and Virgo, the two signs said to be ruled by Mercury, may be courageous spiritual communicators like Dante, Tolstoy, Yeats and Hildegard von Bingen.

Or they may be something else, and our dealings with them may show us why the Romans coined the adage Caveat emptor - Let the buyer beware - and the German mystic Meister Eckhart wrote that it is not in the nature of the intellect to be kind. Mercury types may also be so talkative that they can be too busy getting it all said to get anything actually done. They may lack focus, and move rapidly from one interest to another, instead of holding a consistent course. It's not that Mercury types, especially Geminis, are superficial - they just like everything. One way or the other, whether it's as an actor, a way-shower, a wounder or a crook who's mercurial - the word captures well the mutable fluidity of the Mercury archetype -- the common elements are in telligence, verbal facility and a quick liveliness and adaptability. This is why the green Mercury lines in our astrocartography maps favor good progress and success in verbal activities like writing, teaching, sales, publishing, advertising, community projects and politics. Professional ambition and success are especially highlighted when the Mercury line goes up to the Midheaven, at the top center of the birth chart, and all that this implies about our efforts to inform and direct the consciousness of others, even many others in an intentional community that may be global in scope. The emphasis goes the other way when a Mercury line points down to the Nadir, as here we will tend to fit in to prevailing ideas and customs, rather than seek to change them, and this is why people living on Mercury-on-the-Nadir lines often feel they're more progressive-minded and aware than the others around them, whose patriotic and religious values may seem stolid and denial-bound to the mercurial observer. Or, as can happen within a Nadir line's grounded stability and familiarity, a Mercury line aimed at the bottom of the map can feel reassuring, as cozy and welcoming as a small town where we all know everyone else, and we're happy to talk about the same things we talk about every day, as long as we keep talking. Mercury lines get more specific in their focus, for example on law and government near a Jupiter line, on digital technologies and telecommunications near a Uranus line, and so on. Oc cupations linked to transportation are relevant too - especially near the mobile, outward-directed Ascendant line — as Hermes/Mercury usually appears with wings on his feet, or his helmet, or both, and in a herald's traveling costume of a broad-brimmed hat, a light, loose-fitting tunic and a staff topped with the god's own symbol, the twined serpents of the caduceus. Constant motion rarely favors a life of stable relationships, so it's best that we understand here what Mercury is, and is not. As he represents mentality and verbal facility, he tends to be glib, sexually immature and emotionally neutral, and this is why we normally don't find hot, sensuous, passionate love unions near our Mercury lines. Instead, we're more likely to get, at best, what Ben Franklin and the Paris women who adored him called a "sentimental romance" that was voluble, affectionate and warm, but not likely to get hot. We may be good at our jobs, even absorbed by them, near a Mercury line, especially when it's near a Saturn line. Or we may be well-known and well-liked by wide circles or friends and business associates, but not on re

ally intimate terms with the one who shares our bed. So those who are looking for love relationship would do better to look at the light blue lines in their maps, and the planet they represent. It's time to meet Venus.

Venus-Aphrodite, goddess of love and beauty, is the second planet in the solar system. Her orbit around the Sun takes 225 days. Just as Mercury's swiftness is said to mirror the speed of thought itself, Venus' rapid orbit too is linked to transient things: beauty and glamour, inconstant affection, sexual desire and the passion of love, all of which, as the Japanese say, can be quick to take fire, quick to go out. Venus rules the sign of Taurus, and has traditionally been said to rule Libra as well. She is clearly connected with the second month of Spring, so her luxuriant, abundant energy drives the leaping and leafing out of new life. She's connected with the second house of money in the horoscope wheel, and with wealth in all its solid, tangible forms, especially with works of plastic art. Thus the Venus professions include painters and sculptors, art curators and dealers, fashion models, beauticians, gardeners and landscape artists (as Taurus is an Earth sign) and courtesans. The work of Venus-inspired Taurus artists - Shakespeare, Streisand, George Lucas, Miro, Brahms, Tchaikovsky, Duke Ellington, Orson Welles - is easy to spot as there is a sheen to it, the quality of having been slowly crafted to perfection. Though Venus is highly acquisitive, her style is enticing and receptive rather than aggressive. At her best, Venus is sensuous and playful, quick to enjoy and share fun experiences, and her home is apt to be graced by exquisite art and furnishings. She is, as Winston Churchill put it, easily satisfied with the very best.

Like every planet, she has her less admirable side. Venus can be vain, selfish, petulant, lazy, easily offended and vengeful — the original high-maintenance woman. But her beauty isn't all glamour. As the brightest figure in the heavens after the great lights, especially as the peerless beacon to whom Wagner's Wolfram sang as "my blest Evening Star," Venus represents an ideal perfection beyond the flaws and limits of the Earth plane, the inspiration that waits for those who have the patience and devotion to seek and serve it. The Mesoamerican peoples identified her with the Feathered Serpent Quetzalcoatl, Lord of Illumination. The ancient Mediterranean cultures, who respected the feminine for millennia before a toxic fear of women, sex and the body itself began to go viral during the Piscean Age, called her Lucifer, the Bringer of Light, and prayed to her to bless them with healthy children and prolific creativity. So the blue Venus lines in our ACG maps are good for prosperity, for finding and keeping love relationships, for gaining success in professions related to beauty and art, and for enjoying art, music, theatre and dance, especially in social groups. While all four of the Venus lines are good for money, the two best love lines are the ones pointing up to the MC, and west to the DSC. As the vertical Venus on the MC line carries the nuance of a spiritually nourishing union, it happens often that people find, or have already begun, happy marriages or other intimate rela tionships with partners who were born under this line, or whom they encounter there. The Venus - DSC line is not called the Marriage Line for nothing. A Venus line pointing east to the ASC is more likely to favor individual artistic achievements than shared success, but it surely can't hurt that we will appear more beautiful under this line. The Venus line going down to the Nadir may be the best and most dangerous one, at least for those who are engaged in spiritual practice. Here life is so easy, materially and emotionally - we may be supported by another, and not have to earn a living - that we lack nothing except a soul life, and we may lose all sense of striving toward spiritual goals. That's why I call this the Gina Lollobrigida line, for the high-end, low-talent starlet who made a life of being supported by generous men. Yes, enjoy this line if you've had years of exasperating struggle. But beware of getting stuck there. No line, and no planet it represents, will deliver everything for us, and as with everything else in line, our lines and locations may present tradeoffs and choices. Our Venus lines can bring opportunities for higher income, love links and adventures, and in general terms for stability, ease and comfort. They favor habit and stasis rather than innovation and change. This is why they're less appropriate choices for those who are making brave attempts to pursue challenging goals, whether on the inner plane of soul evolution or in outer environments that may be less than receptive to anyone who wants to rock the boat, uncork some new wine or otherwise catalyze anything original, or propose anything that may require anyone else to change in any way. For that, we follow a different, hot, bright red arrow. For those who aim to be assertive and proactive, some of the lines that may benefit them belong to Venus' impetuous zodiac neighbor and lover,

Mars. Mars: O n the A ttack Mars-Ares, god of war, fiery moves and assertive actions, is the fourth planet in the solar system. His orbit around the Sun takes two years. Mars' distinctive red color, and his association with violent events in the human heart and on the planet - wild fires, volcanic eruptions - have always linked him with forceful pain and conflict. Yet there is more to him, as we'll see, and he has a useful side for those who respect fire. Mars rules the sign of Aries, and was traditionally called the ruler of Scorpio too before Pluto was discovered and became the Lord of Scorpio. Mars is naturally associated with the first month of Spring, when the Earth in the northern hemisphere grows warm with the March Equinox, and, as 2 Samuel puts it, kings go forth to war. In the zodiac wheel he rules the first house of the individual personality and its active, outward expression in the world, and in all arenas of courageous action. So Mars professions include soldiers, police and fire fighters; mechanics, surgeons, dentists and other workers in fire tech nologies; athletes, sales people and others whose work requires courage, including many Aries movie stars: Charlie Chaplin, Marlon Brando, Russell Crowe, Ewan McGregor and Bette Davis, who said, like a classic Aries, "No set goal achieved ever satisfies. Success only breeds a new goal. The golden apple devoured has seeds. It is endless." Mars was hated by the other Olympian gods, and in The Iliad Zeus says to him, "You lover of quarrels and beginner of bloodshed. If you were not my own son, I would have killed you long ago." Mars is impetuous, quick to anger, sexually relentless and insatiable, inclined to act once and think later, if at all. Who was likely to have coined the outrageous order, "Kill them all. God will recognize his own?" Mars, of course. Yet there is a positive side to him, unlikely as this seems at first. The Black Mars who was once ruler of the death sign of Scorpio is easy enough to recognize as the murderer, rapist and

bully, and the competitor so addicted to the fight itself that he will even try to beat the other mem bers of his own team. But the Red Mars who is the true ruler of Aries will run into a burning house to rescue a child, sacrifice himself on a battlefield to save his comrades, push his body and will to their limits as great athletes do, and dare the most dangerous journeys and other new paths, as Jason, Odysseus, Abraham and the Buddha all did. In the extreme case he may be an intrepid Aries leader like Bismarck, or a genius like J. S. Bach, who wrote thousands of works of music, sired 22 children and supported them all. Or Thomas Jefferson, who was assigned to draft the Declaration of Independence, and turned it out at the speed of Mars, in a few days. Considered in spiritual terms, Mars is energy and the courage to pursue our most cherished goals, to protect and defend others from harm, and the ability to take fast, resolute action and respond at once to an emergency. He is everyone's masculine side, excellent at beginning things but less good at maintaining or finishing them, so that an Aries like Leonardo da Vinci was a creative fountain who started a huge variety of engineering and art projects, but brought relatively few to completion. The Red Mars lines in our ACG maps can therefore show places where we will have to take brave action in pursuit of our goals, as conditions we face will usually be disharmonious and conflictive. Some Mars lines are easier to navigate than others, depending on the arena of our efforts and the direction of our goals. Perhaps the best is the Mars line that points up toward the MC, as this line can fortify our courage in going after challenging career and spiritual goals. This one is called the Pioneer Line because it carries the bold heart of the one who builds the log cabinet in the wilderness, braves the animals, the elements and other dangers, but gains in the end the satisfaction of having dared and done an ambitious goal that demands everything we've got. There is something to be said for the Mars on the ASC line too, for this can enhance

our valor in committing ourselves to our goals, and giving them our best shot. Those who've been timid and irresolute in asserting themselves, setting boundaries and otherwise finding the resources hidden deep within their well of courage can benefit from being temporarily under a Mars line, or from building relationships with other people under their Mars lines, who can help them in the aggressive roles of agents and sales reps. The Mars line pointing down to the Nadir is one of the toughest in our maps, as it can mean an aggravating friction in practical matters of making a living, maintaining a harmonious home life and relating to the Mother. This line is not an easy one to travel under, as it can entail mechanical breakdowns and practical difficulties, so that one who travels under this line in rural India during Mercury retrograde may have a hidden masochistic streak. Mars on the DSC is one of our worst lines for love, marriage and all kinds of cooperation, as it can represent disputes, conflicts and out-and-out fighting with spouses, colleagues and partners of all kinds. You'd do well to find your true love under a Venus line, but don't honeymoon with him or her under a Mars on the DSC line unless you want what the Japanese call a Narita divorce. It is well to remember what attack literally means: the daring and drive to go so close to what we want that we can touch it, in the manner of the American Indian warriors whose bravest deed was not to kill an enemy, but to come close enough to touch him on the head with his coup stick. An actor or musician who plays with a sense of attack overcomes fear, and is doubly fascinating to watch. Mars lines in our maps, and Mars transits, can help us see how, and when, to commit to the good fight. Lightning and the L aw: Jupiter Jupiter is the first of the "outer" planets beyond Mars, moving in a 12-year orbit around the Sun. His physical size as the largest planet, and his brilliance as the brightest after Venus, make him an apt symbol for Zeus, the ruler of Olympus, and his role as the most expansive, enthusiastic, optimistic and abundant of all planets. And the happiest. Known as the Bringer of Jollity, he was also called Jove, and so he has the jovial qualities of hearty good humor and the love of laughter.

rules the fire sign of Sagittarius, and is the lord of the lightning he bears in his right hand, as one of the great sky rulers - along with Indra, Odin and Yahweh - in world mythology. On his left hand a dove is perched, for it's clear that Jupiter would rather feast and make love than fight, so he's the natural adversary of his son Mars - and he'd much prefer to establish good order than cause ruin. This is why he, and Sagittarius, the zodiac sign he rules, are linked with in stitutions such as governments, courts of law, banks, universities, and "higher communications" in philosophy, law and religion. Jupiter has a broad strategic vision, so Winston Churchill, and mold-breakers like Berlioz and Beethoven, fit his mutable personality and speed. While many actors are Aries and Leos, Sagittarius prefers directing the movie. In fact, movie director - e.g., Steven Spielberg, Ridley Scott, Woody Allen, Walt Disney, Jean-Luc Godard, Kathryn Bigelow, Kenneth Branagh - may be the perfect job for a Jupiter-ruled Sagittarius, as it gives him or her a glorious way to rule one kingdom after another for a short time. Jupiter rules the last autumn month when the year has yielded its abundance, and we weigh and reckon its money value. This is why so many late autumn harvest festivals, are celebrated at the beginning of Sagittarius month. Jupiter is optimistic, thinks big and lives large, and is gifted with a generous good humor and a hearty appetite for life's pleasures. He'll tend to overdo it, as this fleshy image shows, which is why an afflicted Jupiter can make one corpulent. He loves

variety, and is the most fidelity-challenged of all planets. He insists on getting his way, resists compromise and can be rash, so he may have to learn painfully to think before speaking and acting. The blue Venus and Jupiter lines in our maps are both considered "easy" and "happy" money lines. But while a Venus line spells love, sex, beauty and art, a Jupiter line means power, and a possibility that one may gain authority in politics, finance, religion, medicine or education, and form connections with influential movers and shakers. A blue Jupiter on the MC line points up to the professional and spiritual sphere, this is where we are apt to rise in business and social status, to achieve public office and a position of leadership in medicine, music and religion, even to attract devoted and zealous fans and fol lowers. This line's values are conventionally religious rather than spiritual, and we are more likely here to become a pillar of the establishment and an exemplar of bourgeois morality than to rock anyone's boat, so the corrupting temptations of money and power, and the pursuit of pleasure, can come to outweigh the altruistic motives that first led us into the public arena. A Jupiter on the Ascendant line is even more likely than the MC line to make us so ebullient 13 Highlighters-....... ......................................... ...................... .......................................................... ......................................... ...................................................................................... and confident that we exert an irresistible charismatic appeal to others. We may embody the hope for a better life than can lead others to invest us with the spiritual power of a God-touched faith healer leading a train of enthusiastic devotees. We can gain such professional success and prosperity, and display such largesse, that we become like Lorenzo the Magnificent looking for some Botticellis to patronize, so the risks of attracting sycophants, and getting carried away with the huge importance others see in us, can bring some hard lessons in humility. Jupiter on the Nadir is the most prosperous line in the map, and marks the place where we 11 Highlighters-....... .................................................................. -....................................... ............... ................................................................... .................................. ........................ are most likely to gain a life that is solidly and richly rooted in material wealth and substantial, even ostentatious, possessions. We are apt to retire in status and comfort here, to enjoy a fine home and, as landlords, to gain from building and managing homes for others. We are apt here to put down roots, start a family and continue established patriotic and religious traditions, or start new traditions of our own. We may become noted for our generosity as donors to charity and patrons of the arts, sharing our bounty not only with those closest to us, but with those whom we assist through funding and education to create a better life for themselves. A Jupiter on the Descendant line means professional, financial and social connections, so that here we may excel in business, sales and the practice of law or medicine, and gain high prestige in professional associations. Our chances of "marrying well" are high under this line, and we may attract help from powerful allies who seem miraculously to appear whenever needed. As Jim Lewis notes, "this is one of the most fortunate areas possible, one in which forces beyond your control seem determined that you are to have an easy time of it." Jupiter's special status as the "happy, lucky planet" may be more evident here than anywhere else, so that even when we blunder, we land on our feet not just like a cat, but a very sleek, smooth and well-heeled cat. The main spiritual theme of Jupiter is expansion, and the rewards and risks of living as though

there are no limits - limitation is what Saturn is for - and that life will continue to grow bigger and happier, more enlightened and graceful and easy as long as we pursue our ambition with a fiery, self-assured passion. The danger is obvious: under Jupiter lines we may come to believe that bigger is invariably better, less can never be more, and always quantity trumps quality, until we start to resemble Citizen Kane, longing for the simplicity of childhood and Rosebud.

Saturn: S erious Business Saturn is the most distant of the seven "classical" planets, including the Moon and Sun, that are visible to the naked eye. The slowness of his 291/2 year orbit caused the Greeks to name him Kronos, and thereby to equate him with the inexorable motion of Time itself. He is the most maligned planet. Traditionally called the bringer of old age, sickness and death, he is also associated with separation, inhibition, estrangement and above all limitation, the heavy earthen wall that our lives in this physical realm must hit, the weight of practical reality that must sooner or later bring our dreams back down to the ground. In contrast to his zodiac neighbor Jupiter, who is all fiery enthusiasm and expansion, Saturn is earthy common sense and contraction, the cold weight of re-ality - that is, the perception of our world as a realm of solid things (Latin res) subject to unvarying material laws. But considered in spiritual and energetic terms, as we'll see, Saturn is much more, and for those who are willing to respect and even love him, he is an invalu able ally who can assist our best efforts. Saturn rules the earth sign of Capricorn, and the 10th house of profession and public life in the horoscope wheel. The symbolism of his sickle is complex. In ancient Italy he was an agri cultural deity whose good will could help bring an abundant harvest. He was a Titan, and ruled supreme on Earth until his son Zeus/Jupiter overthrew him, and was kinder to him than Saturn had been to his father, the sky god Uranus, whom Saturn castrated, throwing his father's genitals into the sea, and this is how Venus was born from the sea foam. As he is often depicted as a tall, white-haired old man in a cowled black robe, carrying an hourglass and a scythe, he is also identified with Father Time and the Grim Reaper, whose stroke cuts what is due to pass away, so that new life can come. He is connected with laws of science and mathematics, so that many Saturn-ruled Capricorns are accountants, engineers and inventors of mechanical systems and

discoverers of physical laws, so it fits that Isaac Newton, Benjamin Franklin and Stephen Hawk ing are all Capricorns. Natives of this sign bring the same practical precision to human relations, and are natural organization men and women, building their professional power and success on the careful management of official rules and structures. Capricorn is the most ambitious of all zodiac signs. Many dictators, and those who longed for such autocratic power - Stalin, Mao Zedong, Mark Antony and Caesar Augustus, Gamal Abdel Nasser and Anwar Sadat, Lorenzo de Medici, J. Edgar Hoover, Richard Nixon and the Borgia Pope Alexander VI, among others — were all Capricorns who built organizations of their creatures through personal loyalty, fear and subtle, secretive manipulation. Saturn rules the first month of winter, beginning in the northern hemisphere with the Winter Solstice. So while he is the winter god who fades in the snow and the night, he opens the door for the countless solar deities who are born each year on and in the days after Dec. 21. Saturnian Capricorn personalities are industrious, thrifty, prudent, disciplined, matureminded even in early life, and attentive in managing careers, money and personal relationships. Shakespeare's Camillo, in The Winter's Tale, could be a Capricorn. He sees a solid financial foundation as essential for marriage, as he says "Prosperity's the very bond of love." Saturn types can be moody, withdrawn and slow to open up, pessimistic, cautious and stubborn. They prefer established routines, so the person in your team meeting who says, "We've never done it that way before" may be a Capricorn, or doing a good impression of one. The yellow Saturn lines in our maps are above all work lines. They represent seriousminded, disciplined effort in pursuit of important goals, often under adverse conditions that call forth our grittiest determination. While these lines are never easy, especially in contrast to the blue Venus and Jupiter lines, they may be exactly what is needed for people who have never learned to apply themselves, and they often mark good university locations for people who are about to outgrow the breeze and fluff of high school, and begin to focus on the practical busi ness of preparing for a career, often under the guidance of an older Saturnian mentor. This applies especially to the studious, dogged Saturn on the MC line, often thought to be the best of the Saturn lines because it points up to the apex of the professional success and recognition that come from the hard work that the I Ching implies in its famous line, "Persever

ance furthers." This Saturn line focuses to the point of solitude, and applies to figures like the author or scholar working through the night, the monk in his scriptorium. The dangers of the line are easy enough to imagine, for one can adopt an adversarial, ego-bound "I'll show them" posture rather than a commitment to produce one's finest, and be refined in the crucible of sac rifice for a spiritual goal. Under a Saturn on the Ascendant line, we can project Saturn's sober, heavy qualities into our outer environments, acquiring at best a dignity and gravitas that gain us a reputation as seri ous characters who can be relied upon to be impeccable with our word, and deliver what we've promised. If we take ourselves too seriously, we can become figures of ridicule, like the blackgowned, pedantic II Dottore (the professor) in the commedia dell' arte. We can also respond to criticism from others by taking on a self-righteous posture of Puritanical self-denial, depriving ourselves of life's pleasures to gain goals that may seem worthier only to ourselves. Success can come in time, but the price had best be well understood. The Saturn on the Nadir line will usually mark our least happy places, unless we are moved by a compulsion to drive ourselves to the point of exhaustion. Here all our energies are devoted to the practical business of supporting our material life, so that under this Workaholic Line our job can become all-consuming to the exclusion of friendship and love, healthy pleasures, spiritual stillness and everything else, as though here we are in continuous monkey mind, only at a much slower, leaden tempo. We can be burdened here with home and family responsibilities, though it is possible to bear them gracefully, and gain the serenity of a stoic, contemplative life. The Saturn on the Descendant line is not a pretty sight either. Here the emphasis is on relationships, which tend to be long on duty, short on delight, so that here one can carry a heavy load of professional and marital responsibility, and can become the complaining martyr who attracts the contempt of others. Job partnerships may involve older colleagues, and one may have an older love partner or spouse. There is a danger here of unequal partnership, in which one carries more than his share of the weight, and feels resentment from being ill-used. We can think of this as the Bitter Parent line, for it often appears in locations where people in late middle age are doing their best to care for elderly parents who give back nothing but abuse. A great line for masochists, and those who believe it is their lot in life to suffer. Saturn is devoted, determined effort aimed at our worthiest, weightiest goals in the higher harmonics of communal and cosmic service. He is the enforcer of the non-performance clause in our sacred contracts, and this is why the longer we evade our true soul objectives, provided that we are conscious at all, the harder life gets. Those who see a link between effort and outcome can get along with Saturn, even get his help. And, as counterintuitive as it seems, he is also the patron of comedy. He is the solid common sense that human beings find boring in their endless chase for cheap thrills, easy scores, free lunches, good games in bad places, ways to drop a dime in a dream and break the bank at Monte Carlo, and every other chance to get something for nothing.

He's a severe, majestic piece of work who does not suffer fools gladly. But he will reveal his secrets to those who stay the course in calm and patience. One of the first things a beginning astrologer learns is: "You have to love Saturn." This takes time. But then Lord Kronos has more of it than anyone. The Wounds and the Medicine: Chiron Chiron is officially not a planet at all, but a "small planetoid" whose 50-year orbit takes him through the asteroid belt between Saturn and Uranus. He was discovered in 1977, right at the beginning of the holistic health movement. So just as other newly-discovered planets have been named in ways that reflect currents of science and history - revolutionary Uranus in the 1780's, spiritualist Neptune in the 1840's, turbulent Pluto at the beginning of the violent, transformative 1930's - Chiron too reflects the moment of his arrival in our consciousness, heralding this time when we move away from materialist and often corrupt institutional white-coat medicine toward more spiritually-based, Earth-friendly and communal health practices based on our taking of re sponsibility for our own health. Chiron is not the ruler of a zodiac sign and a house on the horoscope wheel, though he would be a plausible alternative to Mercury for service-directed Virgo and the 6th house of health. His story from Greek mythology is crucial to an understanding of how he affects us, and we can work with him. He is not a centaur, though he does have the human-and-horse shape of this race of violent, drunken beings. Chiron was the son of an act of rape by Saturn on Philyra, the shapeshifter nymph who was changing from woman to mare at the moment the god ejaculated into her, conceiving a being who would be a composite of man and horse. Philyra screamed in horror as she saw him emerge from her womb, throwing him to the ground and wounding him from the moment of birth. He lived in solitude in the woods of Thessaly. In time he fathered children of his own, mastering hunting, star lore, music and herbs. The kings of Greece sent their sons to him to learn the arts of healing and peace as well as war. One of them, Achilles, shown here - maybe thinking "Enough with the music. When do we get to the spear?" - was the most skillful of the Greek wound-dressers at Troy, thanks to what he had

learned from Chiron. In the end, this master healer suffered an incurable wound when Hercules, his prize pupil, defended himself from an attack by centaurs by firing a poisoned arrow that missed its aim and hit Chiron in the foot. Chiron had not prepared an antidote, and endured an excruciating wound until a reluctant Zeus granted his request and allowed him to be the first demigod to die. He is said to have been placed in the zodiac as the constellation Sagittarius, whose arrow is aimed at the Scorpion's heart as a medicine arrow to preserve the Scorpion from his tendency to sting himself to death. Thus Chiron is often called the Wounded Healer, who is incomparably skilled at healing everyone but himself. So Chiron's energy flows two ways, in healing intentions and practice that we direct "out ward" for the benefit of others, and to the recognition of healing of our own wounds, and the barriers they often form against creativity, health and love. The most common Chironic wounds are those of intimate relationship - that is, our longing for the love union we don't have, or the pain of lost love - and the sense of an undiscovered pur pose and underutilized gift among those who wonder what they're supposed to be doing here, or, if they do know, how they'll summon the clarity, courage and resolve to pursue the creative direction they already intend. The wounds become especially intense at our Chiron Return, which comes at 50 when Chiron has moved all the way around the wheel and returns to his position in our birth charts. This moment is hugely important, as we see how often those who've navigated it well seem to get a second wind in middle age and live vibrantly into old age - and how those who don't handle their wounds may start to decline more rapidly. The green Chiron lines in our Astrocartography maps relate to our own medicinal activity as healers, counselors and sympathetic listeners, and our ability to see and address our own wounds, in ways that correspond to the directions in our maps. Chiron on the MC lines point to professional activity, success and recognition as alternative health practitioners, and to our wounds concerning our professional path, spiritual direction and sense of connection with the universal energy field. Such lines may also be present in places where we have a strong sense of

what we ought to be doing . . . but are not doing. Chiron on the Ascendant often applies in places where we are seeking to establish our selves as health practitioners, or are seeking in other ways to gain the courage and assertiveness to project ourselves more confidently into the "outer" world and tell the planet who we are. Issues of worthiness and deserving, or of being in retreat from the inhibiting effect of one's own shadow, often apply here. Chiron on the Nadir can mark a place where we come to terms with our struggles to support ourselves on the Earth plane, whether as health practitioners or in other livelihoods. This line can also be present in places where we address inherited and self-imposed limits of scarcity mind, or assist others in their efforts to dissolve their own poverty consciousness. Chiron on the Descendant is relevant to the work of medicinal teams and projects, our own wounds of love, sex, intimacy and partnership, and the ways in which we may retreat from the challenges of professional teamwork and the rough, sometimes competitive pressures of cre ative and marital collaboration. WhiteW ater: Uranus Uranus is the first of the planets to be discovered with the aid of a telescope in the modern era, and the first of four new planets, including Chiron, to arrive in our consciousness amid political and social conditions that fit the new planet's role in our history. Uranus, the Bringer of Change, revolutionary and agent of surprise and upset, was discovered and misnamed in 1785, two years after the former British colonies in New England won their independence, in the same year as Mozart's The Marriage of Figaro first took stage, four years before the fall of the Bastille triggered the French revolution. Some astronomers considered naming the new planet Prometheus for the rebellious titan who stole the secret of fire from Olympus, but Uranus, father of Saturn, was a safer choice, more acceptable to the astronomers' employers: insecure monarchs who could al

ready feel their people stirring, their thrones tottering. Depictions of Uranus in classical art are rare. The painting above by Vasari and Ghirardi (1555) is one of the very few - not surprisingly, given the gruesome mythic story of how his son Saturn not only overthrew him, but castrated him with an iron sickle, and threw his genitals into the sea, so that his seed engendered Venus. Maybe Europe's astronomers were prescient after all, anticipating that in a few years Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette would lose their heads to an iron blade. This does fit the identity of Uranus, associated with shocking, often violent events. Uranus is the nearest planet beyond the asteroid belt, moving around the Sun in an orbital period of 84 years. His half-orbit of 42 years, called the Uranus Opposition because the planet has moved to a point exactly across from his natal point in our birth charts, is a crucial life passage when we feel a strong impulse to change our jobs, places of residences or relationships, or all these things and more. This is one of the reasons, among other planetary stresses that are also present in our early forties, why this time is called the mid-life crisis, when work, family and other obligations and constraints limit our freedom to choose the changes we want. Uranus rules the zodiac sign of Aquarius the Water Bearer and the 11th house of the zodiac wheel, which relates to friends, social activity, community, social and political activism, and new technologies, especially as they relate to electricity, another of the epochal discoveries of the late 18th century, thanks to Benjamin Franklin, his kite and his key. Thus Uranus occupations include science and engineering, electronic communications in film, TV and other digital media, revolu tionary activity and cutting-edge innovation in every major field of human creativity. Aquarian personalities don't just upset existing structures and rules, and bring in what is new and can no longer be denied and delayed. They delight in it, and enjoy the shock value of their surprises. So just as the Aquarian US presidents Abraham Lincoln, Franklin D. Roosevelt and Ronald Reagan revolutionized their country, Thomas Edison upset the field of electrical engineer ing, James Joyce and Frangois Rabelais reinvented the novel, Babe Ruth shattered the mold in baseball, Oprah Winfrey has galvanized countless American women into more assertive life roles and choices, and Aquarians in all arenas, public and private, have a way of opening new percep tions for which the less airy, quick and flexible zodiac personalities may not be ready. Uranian personalities born in Aquarius love novelty. They are communicative and versatile, and not just comfortable with change, but often seemingly wired to it. They are bright, inde pendent-minded, inventive, loyal, altruistic and humanitarian, They can also be inconsistent and unpredictable, absent-minded and ditsy, and apt to espouse extreme views just for the sake of enjoying the discomfort they create in others, like the monkey who drops a mango into the clear ing below so he can enjoy watching the other monkeys fight over it. Uranians can be notoriously detached in their intimate relationships, much to the distress of lovers who crave warm gestures and romantic reassurances. The themes of change, innovation and creative excitement run through all the purple Uranus lines in our astrocartography maps. Independence and freedom are key priorities, and self-rein-

vention can have a rapid, recurring rhythm of its own. When Uranus is on the MC, occupations and professional goals can shift suddenly and radically, and the urge to rebel against institutional structures and rules can be all but irresistible, so that one goes his own way and can relish controversy and the attention of others who admire, and may envy, his spontaneous zest. Here we may identify with political and social causes, and attract others who aim to enlist our support for their agendas, or become adherents to our objectives, so that we can get more caught up in the egoic electricity of a role than in the principles we advance. Uranus on the Ascendant can bring a craving for notice and impact, as though we need to be validated by the attention of others, and may have to engage in endless reinvention of our selves in order to maintain our position of notoriety and acclaim. We may have a truly inspiring, empowering effect on others, but the usual detached postures remain in effect, so that we resist being needed by others who expect from us more attention and interest than we may be ready to give. We may relish the role of the rebel for controversy's sake alone, without walking the talk of change. As Uranus on the Nadir lines point down to the practical, material dimension of the home, life here can be unstable, and we may find ourselves constantly moving to new living spaces, unloading personal property for the sake of easier mobility, and avoiding any planting of physical and emotional roots. Individuality, independence and unrestricted freedom of choice are para mount here, and we may feel driven to escape all limits and definitions. We are apt to become here the black sheep to some of the people in our families, the heroic trailblazer to others. Uranus on the Descendant has its predictable effect on our relationships. Here, while we naturally seek cooperation and intimacy, we can resist commitment, and expect others to mirror our detachment in ways that are not as comfortable for them as they are for us. We are likely to form friendships, and sometimes fleeting love unions as well, with people who are eccentric and flamboyantly individualistic, though there is also a possibility of relationship with Aquarian ideal ists of the most admirable kind. Uranus is much noticed and followed now as we enter the Great Age of Aquarius that he rules, and many of the changes that come in the pivotal years of 2012 - 2016 are connected with

an ongoing angle of stress between Uranus in the fiery, assertive sign of Aries and the deeply transformative planet Pluto in Capricorn. Profound changes abound, superficial ones too, and the challenges of this moment include the strength to hold firm in turbulent times, and to re member that the changes of consciousness, leading to a universal awakening across our shared intentional field, are the crucial weave in the design. There is more about this in my book Surfing Aquarius, and the Universal Festival Calendar, published monthly. See Bibliography.

Neptune is the second planet, after Uranus, to be discovered in the modern era, and is an example of how new planets are named in ways that reflect political and social conditions, and shifts in human consciousness, at the time the new planet arrives. The new planet that was named — really misnamed -- Neptune was identified in the mid-1840s when spiritualism got hugely popular, and the first Opium War was fought over a mind-altering drug that was introduced from Asia to Europe. The birth of the Baha'i faith, and its stunning new premise that all religions are valid if they honor the core values of love, mercy and compassion, heralded the Interfaith Movement that has continued since. All of these events are appropriate to Neptune and his zodiac sign of Pisces, and their themes of mystical perception, spirituality, altered states of mind, the dissolving of boundaries and the union of human and other beings - especially cetacean beings - in the compassionate universal heart that embraces all. Neptune has a long orbital period of 165 years, and key moments of spiritual crisis and awakening in our lives may come in the "mid-life crisis" of our early 40's, when Neptune is angled toward his natal position at 90°, the famously baleful "square" that is not so much stressful or negative as it is a moment that may catalyze more deep self-awareness than many human be ings want to face. Neptune rules the 12th zodiac house of intuition, dreams, imagination, psychic powers and all other faculties of perception that open beyond the limits of the intellectual mind. The 12th house is also the domain of secrets and shadows, and energies that are in potential, not yet fully formed and ready to emerge into the light of day. As we can expect from Pisces, the most dualistic of all signs - the fish usually swim in opposite directions — Neptune has a curious dou ble personality. He is imaginative, sensitive and kind. The first thing Neptune awakens in us is often our creativity and our capacity for realizing beauty. This is why more notable composers of music are born in Neptune-ruled Pisces than any other sign, and why the vulnerability and impressionability of the Neptunian nature shows up so abundantly in actors and other performers. At his best,

Neptune has the psychic power of an Edgar Cayce or the spiritual vision of a Rudolf Steiner. The Neptunian type can feel the universal heart so sympathetically that even when he has the formidable intellect of an Einstein, he will feel that "kindness and a good heart are more impor tant than intelligence and learning." But before one locates the treasure cell where Neptune's boundless store of empathy, intuition and compassion waits to be found and used, he can be very easy to see as a perpetual victim and energy vampire, the artist of addiction who gets stuck in every available substance, then gets measurelessly deceptive in lying about it. He is also the wishful thinker who conceives the most fantastic, gorgeous dreams, but can't seem to start himself toward realizing them - or gives everything he's got to the most impractical, unrealizable goals, with predictable effects on all his relationships, at least those that survive with people who may enable him yet again. In Greek mythology, Poseidon-Neptune is said to have the crankiest, most morose personal ity of all the Olympian gods - as this image suggests. As we can imagine, Neptunian types can be moody, impressionable and depressive, prone to erratic sleep and disturbing dreams - and to drug habits, as Neptune rules the entire spectrum of altered states of consciousness, in ev erything from meditation and psychic journeys to nicotine, alcohol, cannabis, LSD and shamanic plant medicines. All of the pink Neptune lines in our maps carry this double set of possibilities, with deep spiritual insight and imaginative creation on one side, and fantasy, fraud, victimhood and addiction on the other. Such lines require, naturally, that we make sober, judicious choices without sacrificing the beauty of the dream altogether, and that we set milestones and check our progress with a clear, cold eye. Neptune on the MC lines can apply to both professional and spiritual paths, and can certainly yield impressive successes in art-related field, especially performing arts - for Neptune rules music, theatre and dance - and creative work in the realm of fantasy. We may also find that we have become objects of fantasy to others, who wish to cast us as characters in their fantasy lives. This line is sometimes called the Hollywood Line, for the thousands of people who go there

every year hoping to be Brad Pitt or Nicole Kidman, only to find that their dream is far tougher than they thought, if it's realizable at all. Under Neptune on the Ascendant lines, the same fantasy-object outcomes can be even more dramatic in every sense. Others who see us as intriguing and beautiful may not see us at all - Marilyn Monroe said, "They don't see me, they only see their own desires" - but may only see us as a mirror or remedy for their own sad self-image. We are likely to be hypersensitive here, especially if substance use, even addiction, opens our emotional field to any and all illusions and temptations. While we may pursue spiritual paths here, and identify ourselves as "spiritual people," we may invest a guru, even one teacher after another, with expectations that are sure to be disappointed, with depressing results when the balloon bursts. We can become self-suffi cient in time, but at a painful price. On Neptune on the Nadir lines, we often suffer from false hope and delusion in the areas of home and livelihood, and we may be prone to disappointment from business associates who are either actively dishonest, or are ethical enough, and have the best of intentions, but seem to live in a Neptunian fog, unable to deliver what we've agreed. The unreliability of others around us may force us to become more inventive and resourceful, yet a reliable, predictable way of making a living can still be very hard to create here, to the point that we may contemplate communal, even monastic living. Life here is built on "foundations of sand," as Jim Lewis put it, but deep spiritual rewards may still come from all the slippery dreams. Neptune on the Descendant lines may be the most agonizing of all, as they raise possi bilities of love unions that are based on pure fantasy, or that subject us to love swindlers and people who lose themselves completely in the beloved, so that all their self-esteem depends on their partner's love, or at the very least they are too emotionally dependent to love from a position of clarity and strength. Similar outcomes can apply to other relationships too, especially with spiritual friends and teachers, so we may come to believe that all, not just some of the people we meet here are spiritual scam artists. Checking perceptions with truthful friends, and being open to what they really say, is essential. Death and Regeneration : Pluto Pluto is the outermost of the nine planets in our solar system, notwithstanding a travesty of science committed a few years ago when Pluto was named a non-planet at an International As tronomers' Union convention attended by only 4% of Union members, who did not submit their resolution for approval by the membership at large. So much for peer review, and ethical science - but this is what happens when sterile materialist prejudice views planets only as physical ob jects, rather than as the powerful and conscious energy beings that astrologers know them to be. Like the other planets discovered in the modern era, Pluto embodied when he was first

identified in 1930 the new themes and forces that were about to be unleashed upon the world, when the hounds of Hell seemed to be running everywhere at once. Pluto rules mass political and social movements, like the totalitarian regimes that arose in the 1930's in fascist Europe, the Soviet Union, Argentina, the Dominican Republic and imperial Japan. Pluto is also linked with subliminal imagery and propaganda, and their technologies, as practiced from the 1930's in the age of radio and polemical film and poster art. And as Pluto traditionally has been called the Lord of Death, though modern astrologers now consider him the agent of death and regeneration, he is a fitting herald for the appalling bloodshed of the mid-20th century. In the Greek myths, the three Olympian brothers who led the overthrow of the Titans drew lots to decide which domain each would rule in relation to Earth, which all would share. Zeus- Jupiter got the sky, and with it supreme power. The sea went to Poseidon-Neptune, and Hades- Pluto became king of the underworld. His first priority in this dark, cold realm was to find a queen, and so began the famous seasonal myth of the Rape of Persephone (Latin Proserpina), daughter of Ceres-Demeter, whom Pluto dragged down to his joyless realm until Ceres trumped Zeus by threatening to wither all plant life on Earth, thereby starving everything to death. Zeus had to accept a compromise. Persephone would live in Hades in Fall and Winter, and return to the land of the living in Spring as the maiden Kore. Just as Kore resurges in the Venus-ruled Taurus month of mid-Spring, Pluto rules the Scorpio month of mid-autumn, when the leaves go sere, the air grows cold, and the rites of Dead Moon warn that what moves and pulses now will blacken and fall in the months to come. The mortal effects that Pluto brings are not merely physical. In spiritual terms, he represents that which must die in us if we accept that the life of the soul is a process of ongoing, sometimes harrowing purification in which we refine away the qualities in ourselves that are weak, fearful, and unloving, in order to awaken and free the truth of our being in its courage, freedom and joy.

This theme is universal, as in the exhortation of the prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, to "die before you die," and in the teachings from other traditions that polishing the mirror of the heart can't be done with feathers or silk, but will likely require abrasive sand, and fire that burns away all that is not love. The life passages when we undergo these stark insights and rough remedies on the wheel of birth and death, shown above Pluto's throne here, are often connected with Scorpio and the 8th house of changes, death and transformation, which Pluto rules. Pluto has an extremely long orbit of 248 years, so that his transits to planet positions in our natal charts can last for years, and be felt as intensely heavy and deep, as a dark night of the soul that may or may not be easier to bear if one remembers the advice of Winston Churchill: "When you're going through hell, keep going." Pluto's method, like a siege miner, is to dig under the wall and under mine it, so whatever is due to dissolve and evaporate now just falls of its own weight. Pluto himself, and the dark red Pluto lines in our maps, have a way of delivering not always delightful insights about things in ourselves that we must change now. Our experiences here may show us ourselves in ways that we do not admire. This by itself is no problem. Pluto lines are excellent for pilgrimages and vision quests, as we expect to endure some hardships and risks in a journey of self-discovery. But Pluto lines are not excellent places to live and work for years at a time unless we want to practice masochism as an art form. Pluto on the MC in a birth chart often shows a person hungry for power in politics and government, religion or big business, so the same planet's map line means a competitive, driv ing quest to claim one's own personal power while covertly gaming the system to yield power through indirect means, so the inner emotional games can get thrilling and deadly, now or in time, as the power and success that can come under this line can become even more corrupting than money, and goals of celebrity, mass appeal and sexual excitement can go well on whatever scale one aims to hit. Burnout from the heat of intense effort is possible under this line, where "The road of excess leads to the palace of wisdom," as William Blake wrote - if, that is, we survive the

road. Not for the faint-hearted. Pluto on the Ascendant is also often a power-seeker, though not so much in wanting public office as in projecting his energy with force toward getting what he wants.
