The secretive side of Scorpio especially manifests here, and we keep our secrets close, so that others then naturally become more curious about us. Life is passionate here, and competition and power-playing can get heavy in business and personal life. Here you may find that, as the Romance of the Rose puts it, "... kings are like paintings .. . they please us when we do not come to close to them, but the pleasure disappears at close quarters." Pluto on the Nadir is the line that most embodies the fixed quality of Scorpio, the zodiac sign that Pluto rules. Here this sign's loyalty is admirable and his tenacity commits to jobs and rela tionships so fervently that we can get stuck in them, and hang on much too long to jobs, places and intimacies that are not working and will not improve. Matters of home, property and wealth go through upheavals under this line, and as the line's energy draws us down into the Earth, the taste of mortality is strong under it. We can survive and prevail here with immense effort, though the price may be heavier than expected. Pluto on the Descendant is aimed at our relationships, and may involve power struggles, and a longing to get the upper hand in work or sexual relationships. Here you may feel that the world is determined to push back against you or draw away from relationship with you, so this line can be a struggle for survival within our love unions and in our relationships with everything else, so locations under this line can be physically and emotionally dangerous. Living under this line for longer than we absolutely must is not the most wholesome and brilliant idea we have ever had. Indeed, life has a way of being shorter under this line than it would be in other places. An extraordinary portal to understanding Pluto and Scorpio is in the way the mother scorpion gives birth. She goes to the deepest, darkest part of the cave, where she will not be disturbed, and she sits herself down for the last time, for she will never get up again. At the moment of birth, her back cracks open and exposes five to seven baby scorpions who begin their life by feeding on their mother's body. As they gain strength and try to crawl out, she uses the last of her strength to pick them up in her claws and put them back inside, so when all her young ones are fed and gone, there is nothing left of their mother but her shell. Few images express so well the Scorpio's drive to give her all for the ones she loves - even if she may not survive the giving. The Dragon Returns: the Moon's Nodes

O' D*m VIA! The Moon's Nodes are not planets, or physical bodies of any kind. They're two exactly opposed points in the zodiac where the wavy motion of the Moon crosses the ecliptic, the imaginary orbit of the Sun. The Nodes move north and south of the Sun's path, so each of us has in our birth charts a North Node, or Dragon's Head, opposite to a South Node, or Dragon's Tail. A few pre cise terms will help us understand the meaning of the Moon's Nodes a little better. The Ascending Node, at the bottom of this diagram, is the point where the Moon begins to move from the South of the Sun's path, or ecliptic, to the North, and this is why the Ascending Node is called the North Node. As the Node begins moving South in the opposite direction, it be comes the Descending Node, called the South Node. The Moon's Nodes have naturally been of interest to the physical science of astronomy because eclipses always occur when the Moon crosses the ecliptic near one of the Nodes. If the crossing point is right on a Node, the eclipse is total; if a few degrees away from it, the eclipse is partial. The North Node is generally considered "positive" in western astrology, as it is associated with the themes of guidance and order at the Pole Star and the circumpolar stars. But when the Descending Node goes South, away from the North circumpolar constellation of Draco the Dragon, the South Node connotes disorder, darkness and the animal passions, as when Edmund the Bastard in King Lear says, "My father compounded with my mother under the dragon's tail,

and my nativity was under Ursa Major, so that it follows I am rough and lecherous." Curiously, apart from any cultural nuances of geography, the Nodes have the same respec tive meanings in Vedic astrology, which sees Rahu, the North Node, as fortunate, and dreads the baleful Ketu, the South Node. Vedic astrologers wrote prolifically about the catastrophic position of Ketu on Sept. 11,2001. This is apt, as the Nodes, in both Western and Vedic astrology, have always been seen more in collective than personal terms, insofar as they involve group associa tions and alliances more than individual relationships. Thus, in general terms, the North Node is the attracting, cementing force that strengthens our relationships, especially with groups, while the South Node is the splitting force that stresses relationships, and its transits mark the ways and the moments when bonds of relationship are under greatest pressure, and may dissolve. So transits by the Nodes to our natal planets, and by planets to the Node positions in our birth charts, show us when we are most likely to attract new relationships, and to modify, even bring to closure, relationships that do not serve us. More on this soon, when we look at Nodal Cycles. The Nodes are also said to have karmic implications, so that the zodiac sign and house where the natal North Node appears can be said to represent karmic credits and advantages, and intentional targets, while the South Node marks comfort zones to be transcended, and life areas where karmic debts are waiting to be seen and paid. The gray Moon's Node lines in our ACG Maps show the places where these group dynam

Moon's Node on the MC directs the Node's energy to the professional and spiritual dimen sions of our lives, showing places that involve alliances with professional teams and collectives, rather than solitary work; and involvement with spiritual study groups and religious communities. This line may suggest higher and deeper purposes to the relationship than social and family lines do, so that under this line we may be attracted to our true spiritual family and find our soul brothers and sisters. We may also address karmic relationship with our father, as the 10th house in our birth charts, next to the MC, is our father's house. Moon's Node on the Ascendant lines exemplify the general theme of interaction and po tential tension between our individual personalities, and the way we project and assert ourselves in the world, and relationships, especially with groups; work teams and projects, professional societies and organizations, families, social circles, every group that may influence our self-ex pression into the wider environment of the world. There is a strong emphasis here on leadership and the gaining of support for our endeavors, and on introducing new communal values and ideas, to which others, and community as a whole, may be receptive. Moon's Node on the Nadir: This line favors work with production teams on large-scale projects, community building and social activities involving extended families and other group of like-minded friends who bring a satisfying social dimension to your life. On this line you may work from your home, which may also be an active social center. As the 4th house of the mother is next to the Nadir, maternal karmic resonances may surface here. This line often marks locations

of family lineage. Moon's Node on the Descendant concerns partnerships of all kinds, including love unions and marriages. Combinations of this line and other lines, whether in parallel or crossing, help to identify which kinds of relationships - professional, personal, spiritual, social - are most appli cable here, but the common element is that here you are most likely to come into contact and friendship with congenial, like-souled people who nourish your heart with a strong sense of ac ceptance and belonging. Moon's Node lines in our ACG maps can be read usefully in relation to Nodal Cycles, which take 18.6 years. This is how long it takes the Nodes to move by precession "backward" (clock wise) through the zodiac signs, unlike the planets, which move "forward" (counterclockwise) by procession. Every time one of these nodal cycles is completed, we form a number of new rela tionships, and modify or release existing ones. The first time this happens is the most obvious, as in our first year of university we meet new professors, lovers and friends; and while we treasure our family, we will probably leave our childhood home, and we will see our old friends much less than we did before. At 37 another cycle is completed, and we may change jobs or move to other teams and positions within work associations. Divorces are common at this time too, as children now in their teens are mature enough to handle a parental split that can no longer be postponed. The third nodal cycle ends at 55 14, when our own parents often pass away, grandchildren are born, and we gain work positions of seniority and mentorship. Nodal half-cycles, when the transiting North Node crosses our natal South Node and vice versa, are important too. They come at 28 (preceding and heralding our first Saturn Return), at 46 and 65. As the emphasis in Nodal half cycles is often stronger on the releasing of old relationships, the custom of job retirement at 65 is not just a matter of government and corporate custom. It's in the Nodes' rhythm. The half-cycles can be useful for coming to closure with negating dream-killers and abusive "friends" who will not accept our desire for relationships of mutual love and respect.

Stories Part 1 The main section of this book is a gallery of stories, all of them the products of actual astrocartography readings for clients who have kindly reviewed their stories and noted where corrections were needed, and have given their permission to include the finished stories here. Some are clearly very exceptional. Few of us are beautiful enough to work as a fashion model in Milan and Paris, or have the skill, luck and iron nerve to be professional poker players. Most of the people we'll meet here have the occupations we encounter often: as salespeople, wordsmiths and teachers, as holistic medicine practitioners and health service workers, as suc cess coaches, project organizers and builders of community. The common thread in all these stories is that they offered their main actors the Heroic Choice. The options are always the same. One can stay put in a life that is unfulfilling, even frustrating, but at least has the negative comfort value of keeping them in a familiar scenario and sparing them the scary step into the Unknown. Or one can take the risk, even to the point of leaving behind a safe job and long associations for the sake of gaining a greater goal that is be yond fame and material rewards. It is small wonder that it's been only in the recent decades since astro-cartography first appeared, that we've added the new term comfort zone to our usage, and we understand the risks and rewards of staying in it, or leaving it behind us. Our first six stories are typical of what most people seek in an astrocartography reading: the new direction, the fresh choice, the bigger accomplishment that haven't come in the place where we started, even after many years of honest, patient effort, but which could be within our reach and intention in another place. It's story time, and we start glamorous: in the fashion capitals of Europe. Fashion Model Hits Her S tride Our first story shows what happens when we align with Venus, and her energy of attraction. Not everyone can be an exquisitely beautiful fashion model, as the owner of this first map is. Yet as we'll see in a moment, this example can still be useful, as anyone can tap into her - or his — Venus energy and use it once we gain a better understanding of how it works. We see two sets of lines in her first map (below): To the right, running near Naples and Vienna, are a purple Uranus line pointing to the east, in the direction of our personal intentions and selfexpression; and a green Chiron line pointing to the west, toward arenas of partnership and rela tionship. This means that areas on or near these lines would be excellent for self-reinvention and the pursuit of cutting edge projects and technologies (Uranus) or for teamwork with other holistic

health practitioners (Chiron). To the left, running east of Paris, is a blue Venus line pointing to the east, so on or near this line in our map, we can gain success in activities related to art and beauty — and as Venus is one of the money planets in the solar system, we can also earn significant in come through art endeavors. Our heroine — an Israeli woman whom we'll call Sarah, namesake of the famously beautiful wife of Abraham — spent years in the Italian fashion capital of Milano, but gained no notable or consistent successes there, and no wonder. If we apply the 300-mile rule — that map lines are powerful and influential within a range of 300 miles (or 500 kilometers) to either side — Milano is so far from any lines in this map that it's neutral territory, so it neither advances this woman's in terests, nor impedes them. Paris, on the other hand, represents the difference between nuit and jour. Here Sarah is seen as a rare beauty, thanks to that Venus line. She's greatly in demand, works with the most pres tigious designers, and is beautifully rewarded for her work. Milano is not knocking at her door, but Paris is at her feet. Once we know which lines in the map favor the goals we most want to achieve, it's easy to focus our efforts where they're most likely to bring a rich — and in this case, elegantly beautiful — harvest. Everyone "knows" what Venus is about: the irresistible goddess of love, sex and beauty who can have any god or mortal she wants, but doesn't stay attached to any of them for long, and leaves in her wake a stream of broken hearts and hopelessly devoted lovers who lost themselves in her, and never found their way back out. The lower harmonic of Venus as the ruling planet of Taurus - sensuous, possessive, devoted to material wealth and physical pleasure — is all that most people ever perceive (or misperceive) of her, so it's hardly a surprise that they lurch and careen from one failed love union to another. Yet Venus also has a higher harmonic as the planet of spiritual love, who is exalted in Pisces, the Neptune-ruled sign of spirituality and mystical consciousness. Here she tends to attract conditions and relationships of enduring value, as the emphasis is on what will be to the highest

and best interests of the one who exerts the attracting force, and the others who are pulled by it. One way or the other, Venus gets her goal. Every planet has its way of getting what he or she wants. Saturn earns it, Jupiter buys it, Mars takes it, Uranus pulls it out of a hat that isn't there, Mercury steals it. But Venus looks it in the eye and says, "Come here. I want you." And it comes, because she has a surprising gift for holding in her mind one thing at a time until she draws it to herself, and she has no doubt whatsoever that she deserves what she wants. Uniquely among the planets, she the master of attraction, using a focused force of will and a playfulness that dissolve all resistance. This is why the Venus lines in our maps don't relate only to matters of love relationship, or wealth or beauty. They can be used by anyone as zones for magnetizing our goals. And the more generous and communal the goals are, the more devoted to the highest good of all, the more subtle and effective our power of attraction can be. For Sarah, the attraction zone in Europe is superbly positioned. She can expect anywhere under her Venus line the same conditions that apply in Paris. If she chose, she could create a work circuit running from Amsterdam down through Brussels, Paris, Barcelona and Ibiza, all of it likely to be lucrative and rewarding in other ways. Once we know where our best lines are, the whole world can be our runway. Until, that is, it's time to stop walking for a while, listen to that nesting instinct, and do the things one does at rest rather than in motion. Sarah now lives in San Francisco, where she has birthed her first child under the best possible line, the gray Moon on the Nadir line that points down to the Moon-ruled house of the home and the mother. She and her husband both benefit too from the proximity of the Sun on the Nadir line that is out in the ocean, but still well within the 300-mile range. So Sarah enjoys excellent health - she also teaches kundalini yoga - the rich creativity of successful marketing and business coaching enterprises, and the social prosperity of a life surrounded by friends, and the cultural abundance of a great city. Her intuition guided her to Paris before she'd ever experienced astrocartography. But her ACG map lines were among the crucial factors that guided her to the City by the Bay. She followed not only her lines, but their directional arrows, which showed where to stride and shine,

where to build her home and birth her family. Dr. B reathwork and the P ot of G old Generally speaking, the two blue lines in our astrocartography (ACG) maps are the "easiest" and most obviously beneficial. We've just seen, in our story about Sarah the fashion model's success in Paris, how good a blue Venus line can be for anyone in a profession related to beauty and art, and needless to say, for matters of love relationship as well. Here we'll look at the other blue line: it's royal blue, fittingly enough, for any Jupiter line carries the regal, jovial force of the King of Olympus himself, the bringer of joy and abundance, prosperity and expansion, enthusiasm and the love of life and laughter. Jupiter is also associated with successful individuals, and institutions of power and authority - governments, courts of law, churches, large financial enterprises, universities - so life on a Jupiter line can bring us into fruitful and lucrative connection with movers and shakers who can emphatically move and shake things to our benefit. The owner of the maps we'll explore here is a Toronto-born health practitioner whom we'll call Dr. Breathwork for short, because a name listing all of this multitalented man's skills would be too long even for a Spanish nobleman. The doctor is a master of chiropractic, Network Spinal Analysis, nutrition and shamanic healing as well as breathwork, and in his fifteen years in Peru he has clearly found what could be his best spot in the world for his own practice, and for contribut ing as well to the health and success of his patients, and his community. Our first map, of his birth location in North America, shows Toronto in the upper left corner, well outside the 300-mile effective range of the blue Jupiter line to the east. To tap this line's potential, he'll have to move east to the New England area of the United States, or, if he wants to remain in Canada, to Montreal or Quebec City, just out of frame close to the Jupiter line at the top of the map. Or he can build relationship with this powerful line, traveling to teach and prac

tice under it, or using its power as one of the best publication lines. Or he can see where else the line goes, farther to the south, in the Caribbean islands or South America. One way or the other, if he wishes to develop his gifts fully, he'll have to move from the energetically empty area where he started, or project his efforts to another place at a distance from Toronto. He chose Cusco, Peru. He has acquired Peruvian citizenship, and as the high-effort yellow Saturn line off the coast west of Lima indicates - more on the Saturn lines soon in another story -- he needed some pa tience to navigate the pertinent hoops toward his goal. But the blue Jupiter on the Nadir line just east of Cusco is clearly the jewel in this map. Whatever Jupiter touches will expand and gain gravitas. As the line is pointing downward here, to the foundation of our material life at the bottom of the map, it's fitting that Dr. B. has built a solid, well-known practice, and is sought after for mentorship and assistance with community health and education projects. He has bought land, and has built, in the heights near the Temple of the Moon above the city of Cusco, a beautiful home that he happily shares with a beautiful partner. He has also built a guest house for visiting colleagues, and for patients who are committed to long-term courses of healing. And he and his partner - also a holistic health practitioner - are building another house to rent out in the Sacred Valley near Cusco. The doctor travels often from his base, as we'd expect, since Jupiter rules the 9th house of travel in our charts, and is often connected with happy journeys that bring new knowledge and expand the frontiers of our vision - as well as the frontiers of our bodies, as Jove is also a figure of hearty appetites. Not that Dr. B is big around the panza. He walks his talk as a health practitioner, and is as wiry as a jaguar. But he does live joyously when he travels away from his Jupiter line, and lives large about as modestly as man so blessed can. The doctor is also a good example of why it's important to look beyond what "everybody knows" about each planet, and its lines in our maps. Superficially considered, Jupiter is all about the money, the status, and people and organizations of power, and so it's easy to assume that he affects only the material plane of our lives. Yet as the 9th house of a chart also relates to the

"higher communications" of religion, philosophy and law, it is often prominent in the charts and maps of highly intelligent people who have a wide, sweeping vision, and a range of interests that is deep as well as broad. In every dimension of his life, Dr. Breathwork has found his place in Cusco - or his place has found him. The Alchemist Finds Her L ab Here we'll look at the map of an Australian woman whom we'll call the Alchemist, whose crucible and alembic are waiting far from the area where she lives Down Under. Her best location in her native region is northern New Zealand, as it has pointing down to the Earth plane the gray Moon's Node line that signifies acceptance, belonging and communal support; and especially the superb blue Jupiter line that we saw in Dr. Breathwork's map of Cusco, Peru. Her actual location, on Australia's east coast near Brisbane, is much less advan tageous, having as it does a yellow Saturn on the Descendant line. This signifies that at best, Alchemist will be involved in serious, disciplined study or research, possibly with an academic team. At worst, this line marks a place where partnership is unequal, and we give much more to a joint undertaking than we get back from people who are inert or resistant - in short, non-per forming team. While this Saturn line also crosses through the bottom of New Zealand's southern island, it's far enough from the northern island, especially Auckland, that it has no limiting effect there. So why doesn't Alchemist just move there? It's not so easy when one has that gray Moon on the Nadir line crossing the Saturn line and kissing Australia's east coast. This line, connected so strongly with the Home, the Mother, and our sense of security and belonging, is one of those that

will tend to keep us in one place, even a place that is not comfortable or is even challenging. While this line greatly favors a woman for giving birth and raising small children, it can have a certain constricting effect on those whose creative interests and horizons stretch far beyond the home. So Alchemist is one of those who will seek alliances in other places that can benefit her even if she doesn't live there. Her lab is across the world, in the Netherlands. Here we see three lines pointing upward, to the top of the map, toward the Midheaven, or MC for Medium Coeli, the point that was right above us in the center of the sky at the moment we were born. It has a double reference: (1) to our main career goals, as it's the cusp of the 10th house of the profession in our birth chart; and (2) to our most authentic and cherished soul objectives as well, because the MC is the spiritual upward thrust in our chart and maps, the true north point in our soul compass, so that when we're in alignment with it, we have a strong and sure sense that we're aiming at exactly what we're here to do. Alchemist is a creator of vibrational essences made with gems, flowers and other materials. She feels very strongly drawn to Amsterdam and the Friesland islands, and not just because this has long been a place where genius artists and creators have done cutting-edge work at the frontiers where material and spiritual sciences meet, beyond the control of state and church authorities. Her map shows a pink Neptune on the MC line passing vertically near Amsterdam and other major cities on the Dutch west coast. This line applies especially to spiritual explorations, notably those that may involve occult sciences, dreams brought to concrete realization, and discoveries that may serve Neptune's agenda as mystical teacher: to expand our consciousness, and give us a better understanding of the all-embracing Universal Heart. Vibrational essences, as they can open our emotions, empathy and deepest strata of memory, are clearly a way to access Neptu nian dimensions of imagination, intuition and non-linear perception.

Neptune lines, like this mysterious planet himself, are always tricky and elusive, and Neptune always has an enigmatic double identity as both mystical voyager and con man. He does embody, after all, the whole range of altered states of consciousness, from mystical visions, meditation, dreams and shamanic journeys to nicotine, alcohol and drug-induced hallucinations, and fantasies and illusions of all kinds. It is often hard to tell, with people of the Neptunian type: Am I dealing here with a sincerely spiritual seeker of the truth? Or only with an artist of fraud who is stuck in his addictions, and his habit of lying about them? This is why the house where Neptune appears in our birth chart is usually the area of life in which we are most likely to deceive ourselves or be deceived by others, and get hooked on fantasies and unrealizable schemes. That's also why some astrologers call the Neptune on the MC line the Hollywood Line. It fits well the thousands of dreamers who go to Los Angeles every year to be movie stars. Only a few make it. Those who do are the ones like Alchemist, who've done their experiments, know what it will take to gain their goal, and can be free of attachments and ego agendas, ready to pierce the deepest secrets of their art. But Alchemist's focus on this part of the world is not all wishful thinking. Farther west, in the UK, are the same three lines we saw in Australia-New Zealand, only now pointing in opposite directions, so that Europe's west coast is a "bookend" location where we may be attracted to the same lines that magnetize us in another place. Here in the UK, the yellow Saturn on the Ascendant line favors original, pioneering work. The gray Moon's Node and blue Jupiter lines, both pointing up to the Midheaven, suggest that here, across the channel from the Netherlands, a strong sense of spiritual community (Moon's Node) and like-minded visionary financial backers (Jupiter) could both be present, helping in their different ways to move her alchemical work out into the world. Tenacity Gets the Red O ut The maps in this story, like the others we've just seen, show us an astrocartography scenario we encounter often and like to see, because involves a move from a location that doesn't favor us to one that does. Here we'll look at the maps of a woman who moved from a Pluto line that was difficult, to say the least, to a Moon's Node line that has proved much better. We'll call her Tenacity because as a person born in the middle of the sign of Scorpio she has that sign's qualities of stamina, loyalty and determination to carry the job through, whatever it is. The downside of these virtues is that we can overdo them by hanging on too long to jobs, living locations and whatever else does not work in our lives. Tenacity was born and grew up in Ada, Oklahoma, then moved to Oklahoma City and lived there until she was 50, when she was in the important life passage of the Chiron Return (see Chiron profile), when we normally feel keenly a sense of being wounded and incomplete because something we very much want is missing from

our lives. For Tenacity, the wound was one of feeling stuck, and unable to find a creative path and a sense of living in a nourishing spiritual community. As we see in our next map, she spent the first 50 years of her life well within range of one of the toughest lines we have, the dark red Pluto on the Nadir line that raises first one of the basic rules of thumb about our Astrocartography planet lines. Red lines - this one and the bright red Mars line we'll meet later — are the most difficult and challenging, just as the light blue Venus and royal blue Jupiter lines are the "easiest," "happiest" and most harmonious. So some of the stories we'll see here involve moving from one of the difficult red lines to other lines that are often easier, and better aligned with our goals. Tenacity's life in Oklahoma City was what we'd expect from her Pluto line here. She felt trapped in a dead-end job and an unfulfilling relationship that in time became unendurable, be cause Pluto lines are transformative, showing us the ways in which we must change now. Pluto lines often hold up to our vision the things we like least about ourselves, so the longer we live under these lines, the more trouble we have with self-esteem, until we get what Thoreau called "lives of quiet desperation." This can go double when we're in a passionate encounter that's not the one for the long run, but is so afire with sexual intensity that it is hard to break away.

So when her love partner told her that he wanted to spend some months in eastern North Dakota working on one of the lucrative mining projects there, and asked her to go with him, her intuition kicked in loud and clear, telling her in so many words that this new location would be more of the same. Here we see the exact same Pluto line she had in Oklahoma, only in a place where work would be even harder to find than it already was, so the sense of being stuck, without prospects or resources, would be even harder to bear. Besides, in her meditations and dreams, the Sun Belt was calling. The next map, of Arizona and New Mexico, shows us why. In New Mexico we see a green Chiron on the MC line pointing to the top of the map, just east of Santa Fe, and a purple Uranus on the Nadir line pointing to the bottom, west of Albuquerque. When we see parallel lines with arrows that point in opposite directions as these do, then we know that the two plan ets were in opposition when Tenacity was born, in the early 1960s.

J K • j _________________ Santa Fe was naturally attractive, as the Chiron line pointing upward can direct us toward the discovery of new creative and spiritual paths that may be waiting for us. But the Uranus line was much less desirable, as the arrow points down to the home, and signifies what a Scorpio native, born under a fixed sign, least wants. Uranus is the Bringer of Change, the revolutionary and trickster who brings new conditions and effects that can be more turbulent and upsetting than we bargained for. Here his line points down to the Home, so New Mexico was likely to be for Tenacity a place where life feels unstable because we are moving our living space constantly amid the unpredictable surprises and pres sures that Aquarius, the sign that Uranus rules, so often pours from his urn of water. Tenacity went to explore her chances in Phoenix, Arizona, and she knew at once that her choice was right. She landed within days a better-paying and more fulfilling job than anything she'd had before. She also began to make a lot more friends a lot more quickly. This is what we would expect from the vertical gray Moon's Node on the Nadir line that runs west of Phoenix. This line, aiming downward as it does to the point of the Home and the Mother, is often a heritage line that shows where our ancestors lived. It feels like a good family, welcoming and embracing. But here, for Tenacity, this line manifested one of its key features, in connecting us with community and a strong sense of nurturance and belonging, so that here we feel as though we're truly at home, held in the arms of the Mother, strengthened and protected in ways that we'll never be in places that feel afflictive, as though they'd like to kick us out to some better place. The line itself doesn't do this, of course. But the lines do show, in places we leave and places we find, how the moment of change that we've written into our life script can induce a move in our psychic soulscape, and in physical

space too. That green Chiron line near Santa Fe isn't going anywhere, and visiting this place can help Tenacity open up new creative avenues, while living farther to the west in a place that em braces her.

The map we're about to view belongs to an energetic, sophisticated Japanese woman — we'll call her Activist — who lived her early decades in Hawaii as the daughter of a wealthy developer. She has traveled extensively since then, and has been active in a variety of humanitarian and environmental projects. Even before the Hawaiian islands were endangered by the impact of the Fukushima catastrophe, she was looking to move to Central or South America with her husband and their newborn son. a I yQ. ******* One can see from her Hawaii map why a move was only a matter of time. There are three sets of lines here. To the west are a bright red Mars line, congruent with a green Mercury line because these two planets are in conjunction in her birth chart. Both point to the top of the map, toward spiritual values and ambitious goals. Activist has been proactive and courageous in pursuing her goals (Mars), and is highly communicative (Mercury) in business and social circles, and in launching a blog and other communications in support of her goals. To the east of the "Big Island" is a gray Moon line pointing east, in the direction of her individual self-expression. As Moon lines pertain to home, motherhood and familial relationships, it's fitting that in Hawaii she attracted her mate and bore her first child. The kicker among these lines is in the middle. The dark red Pluto line, between Kauai and Oahu, marks a place where we often encounter power and boundary issues, and feel embattled, as Activist was in conflictive

relationships with both parents. This Pluto line, like the lines to the west, also points to the top of the map, and our most ambitious career goals and our most important spiritual values and guid ing principles. Thus it marks an area that is profoundly formative, yet may at the same time force us to join the ultimate battles of defining ourselves by differentiating ourselves from others, and committing ourselves to our most difficult and challenging goals. In our astrocartographyy maps, as in many other things, red lines can be danger signals that show where conflict, even crisis, can occur. Just as some banks became notorious years ago for "redlining" inner-city zones that were high in crime and low in prosperity, red lines in one's maps can likewise be indicators that in these areas, our lives and activities are going to hit some opposition. All Mars lines are inherently conflictive. They represent the energy of Mars the Warrior, who moves bravely and assertively in the direction of what he wants, seizes it, and is ready to fight over it when he meets resistance. Thus Mars lines often show the places where we are fighting against someone or something. In this case, as the Mars line points upward, we're in a test of courage, fighting against our own perceived limits. This is why this Mars line has been called the "pioneer line." It marks an area where we're likely to be engaged in some new, courageous and even heroic effort, like the pioneer who builds the log cabin in the wilderness, braves the elements, the animals and all the other challenges, but in the end completes the task, and gains the sense of achievement that comes from gaining a great goal. So the question of whether to get close to a Mars line can depend on your position and your needs. If you've been through a rough patch, then it may be best to get a break from Mars. But if it's time for you to find your bravery and get ready to make the heroic choice that will call forth the best you have, then a Mars line might be a good one to try for a while, especially if it's point ing up, toward your truest and most cherished goals. All Pluto lines, as befits this planet of death and regeneration, are inherently transformative. They mark areas where we may have to face conditions around us, and within us, that are due now to pass away, and yield to newer energies that are best for our growing through the changes that must be faced now. Near Pluto lines we will come into contact, even collision, with things in our belief system and ego structure that must be raised and faced, and when we're ready, be changed. This makes Pluto lines excellent for a pilgrimage or vision quest, because these journeys of spirit can bring, along with the inspiring and confirming visions, some less thrilling insights about the parts of ourselves that are hardest to admire. This is why traveling on a Pluto line can bring valuable insights — but one who lives there will wind up thinking about whether this place is really worth all that deep, searing perception. Pluto rules Scorpio, the most tenacious of all signs, who embodies our longing to keep hanging on and on, even to people and situations we want to leave behind. The question will often be: when and how will the decisive impulse to leave this lo cation come? What will it take to get free?

How We Gravitate to Harmonic L ocations Activist's maps are a good example of how we can often gravitate to places that have the same lines - even challenging ones - that we've experienced elsewhere. Our lines in South America will point in different directions from our lines in Hawaii, so that while the planet energies are the same, the thrust of their energy changes from one place to another. The implication of this is easy to see, even if surprising at first: that we tend to seek not only the same advantages in different places, but also the same challenges. So areas that are thousands of miles apart in physical space are closely related to us in personal harmonics among the same planets. One excellent example of this is Activist's Peru map. Vive la difference. All four of the lines we saw in Activist's Hawaii map are present here, but are mostly pointing west, in the direction of relationship. Reading this time from east to west, we see that the dark red Pluto line, fortunately, is well out of frame to the east in the Brazilian jungle. The red Mars and green Mercury lines that go through the Sacred Valley, east of Cusco, are a perfect match for places where Activist enjoyed productive partnerships and lively communica tions, though she also encountered some conflictive personalities. To the west, the vertical gray Moon line points up to the Midheaven. This is the Goddess Line. It appears in places that awaken and strengthen the Sacred Feminine in men as well as women, and it could not be more fitting close to places where Activist worked with the Pachamama Alliance, in service to the Mother Goddess revered throughout the Andean region. What makes Peru a much easier location than Hawaii is the blue Venus line that is close to Lima. This line was not, for Activist, the "Marriage Line" that it has often been called, but it may as well have been, because here this very attractive woman found corporate and governmental officials more than willing to assist her. Here again, as so often happens under Venus lines, the

force of our personal attraction can be very strong in helping us to manifest our goals, if our aims are clear and our sense of deserving is solid. Now, as her first boy is three and she'll soon have a second child, she lives in California in a location that is neutral for her, but financially advantageous for her husband in his breadwinner role as the father of a young family. This raises two important points about our lines. One is that a neutral location may very well be useful to us at a time when we are not in motion or achievement mode, but are devoting our efforts mainly to domestic goals. We can always go at other times to active places that have a number of planet lines. The other point is that in the life of a couple, the principle of "What's mine is yours" applies also to our ACG maps. An advantageous line in our partner's map will benefit us as well when we're in that place, and a line that limits one will tend to limit both. Activist will return when the time is right to her powerful line combination in South America, and will explore the places where the same lines extend north to New York and Washington DC. Part of the art of living by our planet lines is to know when to go where the action is, and when to go to the places that are neu tral and restful. Konstanze and B elmonte Break Out This story is a simple and direct one about a German couple whom we'll call Belmonte and Konstanze, for the lovers in Mozart's Die Entfuhrung aus dem Serail (The Abduction from the Seraglio). While the parallel to their lives is not pinchingly close, and Konstanze is not - Gott hilf uns! - in danger of any scary indignity in the harem of the Sultan, she and Belmonte did wish to break out of an unsupportive, even oppressive area and go to a freer, better place. Konstanze's map is not completely neutral for her birthplace in Hamburg, and the rest of

Germany. The green Chiron on the MC line running through the Netherlands, Belgium and eastern France can bring some valuable insights about our own healing gifts, other talents that are waiting to be found and tapped, and the ways to address whatever wounds we carry, in this case the unfulfilled desire to tap and express her creative gifts. Areas just to the west will have some Sturm und Drang, under that grinding combination of yellow Saturn, purple Uranus and dark red Pluto lines in eastern England and Spain, and western France. Konstanze already knows that Uranus line well, as we're about to meet it in Belmonte's map. For her, the best places in this map are on the flanks: a yellow Sun on the Nadir line that could beckon her brightly in later life, and a blue Venus on the Nadir line that runs from the Baltics down to the Balkans. More on this one in a moment. One thing that both these lines embody, as they point down to the home and the practical dimension of making a living, is a sense of being rooted, grounded and well-supported that Konstanze has not had in Germany, and longs to find. For Belmonte, even a place that is only neutral would be a welcome relief, as his Europe map shows. Born in Switzerland at the purple Uranus on the Nadir line that can make life and work unbearably unstable for a continuity-loving Scorpio, he's afflicted by the conflictive red Mars on the Descendant line that spells dispute and perhaps even more explosive trouble with business and personal partners. This is most intense where the Mars and Uranus lines cross just west of Bremen, because this combination involves fire technologies (Mars) and electrical machinery (Uranus), and carries a danger of physical accident and injury. If Belmonte goes to Bremen, he had best wear a helmet. It is well that he and Konstanze did not honeymoon there. Interestingly, he has the same green Chiron on the MC line as Konstanze in the same place, just west of Germany. And he too has a stressful, wrenchingly transformative dark red Pluto line in eastern England. He too has his best Europe lines on the flanks. The gray Moon's Node on the MC line in Ireland is an excellent complement to Constanze's

earth-centered Sun line there, as Belmonte's line in Ireland marks this as a place that will have for him a strong sense of spiritual connection and inspiration. Like his partner, he too has a blue Venus line near Greece. In fact, he has both blue lines there. We're about to see why sun drenched Mykonos appeals to these two even more than it does to other lovers. As his Aegean map reveals, the red Mars line he has in Germany is present here too, but distant and much less dire. It is more than outweighed, as the two blue lines are the "easiest" and "richest" of all, by the most prosperous of all lines, Jupiter on the Nadir, west of Athens and the Venus on the Nadir line, our best for material comfort, through the east Turkish coast. The match with Konstanze's Greece map could have been made on Olympus, even by Aphrodite/ Venus herself.

Konstanze's Venus on the Nadir line is between Belmonte's two blue lines running through the center of the Greek islands and Crete. (Istanbul, a natural focal point of interest, is out of frame, and unaffected by planet lines, in both maps.) Between them, the lovers have three blue lines, all aimed at the Nadir here in the Aegean, which must look like Homer's Lotus Land itself after the stress they've experienced in Germany. So. Do they just move here and have it made, for a life of oranges and retsina until some caressing zephyr bears them up into the blue? Hardly, because the Venus on the Nadir line is in its way the best and most dangerous of all. It marks a place where life is materially easy, often because we're supported by another and don't have to work at all. We enjoy life's pleasures, including the joy of a loving relationship. We live in a beautiful home enriched by exquisite works of art, and a garden so fertile that we can throw a grape seed out the window, it takes root at once, and a new vine springs up. We may gain a wider waistline from all that moussaka — and we may lose all sense of creative gifts and purpose, and of striving toward a spiritual goal. Many people would want nothing more, as long as they have a TV and the servants don't steal. But those who feel they're here to give and create as well as get, and serve some purpose beyond their own amusement, will need a challenge sooner or later, at least some of the time. Curiously, and counterintuitively at first for many people, there can and will be times when we avoid the "easy, happy" lines and actively seek the ones that will offer us a challenge. Ideally, we will be able to integrate and balance both. But for Konstanze and Belmont, the next choice is clear, After years of blockage and difficulty in northern Europe, it's time to head south to the Aegean at least part of the time. Will the lovers choose a Rhapsody in Blue Lines in Greece for the rest of their lives? Not likely. Germans love to work. But the direction to go for rest, pleasure and beauty is clear.

Stories Part 2 - 5 The rest of our stories are grouped in three categories that are different from the most common theme and questions that an astrocartographer usually addresses: What's my best place in the world? Do you see one place that's better than all the others? Where do I go to find a life that's less stressful and lonely, more prosperous and happy, and filled with opportunity? The six Going Toward the Challenge stories all feature people who were born into lives of high social status and wealth, or who gained prominent and lucrative positions in their profes sions through decades of effort in early and middle life. The common thread in all these stories is that it's time to find the situation, the test, the location that will call forth the best that I have in me, and demand the best I can give in service to my community, my country, and my planet. The four Casting Lifelines stories are about people who love living and working in locations that are either neutral or actually unfavorable for their goals. But they've created relationships

with partners, publishers and other associates in other places, thereby benefiting from energies that are present in places where they don't want to live, but that can still help them by offering the good relationships they can build with supporters, colleagues and teams. The three Mastering the Currents stories are spectacular. At first glance they appear to be tales from the 1001 Nights, even Hollywood movies. One of them emerged from a reading in which a professional gambler wanted to know which casino locations, besides the ones he already knew, would favor him most for continuing to win big. Another is about a successful beauty products marketer and blogger who had already developed two of the best places for her teaching and travel, was opening up the third, and had her eyes on the fourth. Like Constant Gardener, whose first astrology reading was his ACG session with me, she "knew" her best places intuitively, before hearing anything that might confirm her hunches. The implications of this are clear enough. The hunches we have that some places may be calling us are confirmed constantly in our ACG maps. The last story shows how we can use our astrocartography maps to complement the other techniques astrologers use to rectify an approximate birth time, or determine a person's correct time when no information is available at all. And now - get ready for some challenges, and the brave souls who faced them. Hearing a Different Drum Astrocartography can show what places are most important for the fulfilling of our unique sacred contract, and the challenges and opportunities it offers for the pursuit of our spiritual goals, and our evolution toward enlightenment and freedom. Here we'll look at the map of an American man whom we'll call Lakota. He's an accomplished photographer, marketing coach and master of digital media who lives in San Francisco, and travels and teaches in the Americas and Europe. His business and network are especially strong in New York, as his spectacular New England map (below) shows. The green Mercury line is too far west to have much impact on New York — though it greatly favors communication-related work in the Baltimore-Washington DC, Pittsburgh and Cleveland areas — but the two lines flanking New York more than compensate. The yellow Sun line is superb for creativity, leadership and large-scale project organization, while the blue Jupiter line is excellent for prosperity, expansion and interactions with powerful, influential people. Both lines point west, to partnership and connections, so New York is easily Lakota's best networking zone. While his heart is in San Francisco, his best business prospects are on the other coast.

So — what would draw a sophisticated, bicoastal creator like this to the plains of South Dakota? Neptune, the Moon and Saturn called him. Our hero spent years living in the eastern area of South Dakota, learning Lakota spirituality, ritual song and drumming and other ceremo nial practices, which he has often applied since to vision quests and shamanic work he has done elsewhere, most recently in South America. In and near the Dakotas, we see both of the lines that

The pink Neptune line relates to spirituality and mystical consciousness. Here the line points west to the Descendant, so it refers to relationship and partnership, thus linkage with spiritual teachers. The gray Moon line, also pointing west, often signifies motherhood in a woman's map. In a man's map, it can mean that the place itself has maternal qualities for him, and a sense that here one is in the motherland, embraced in the nurturing energies of a land that gives us a profound sense of home and belonging. Moon lines are rich and complex in their meanings, often

linking with ancestors and earlier incarnations. Lakota's most important line in this location is the yellow Saturn line that runs congruent with the Moon line, and points to the opposite direction: to the east, the Ascendant, the direction of personal self-expression and our ways of projecting our intentions outward, and declaring who we are. This line often marks a place that fascinates us and anchors us so much that we are willing to devote years of patient study and practice to the things this place has to teach us. Here again, a Saturn line is not necessarily "difficult" or limiting. But it requires that we be ready to de vote right effort for whatever time the goal demands from us. It often happens that we may follow similar life paths on different locations under the same sets of lines. Here's an example of the opposite choice from what most people seek. This brief story is about one of the bravest characters I have been honored to meet. We'll call him Advocate. on the Ascendant line just west of Ireland and through northern Scotland, and the yellow Sun on the Descendant line running right through the British isles. The red Mars on the ASC line descends through Belarus and Ukraine, areas that are suffering upheavals of their own. So if Advocate were mainly looking for peace and quiet, western Europe would be his best zone in this area. even revolutionary action (Uranus) and efforts to act as a conciliator (Chiron). Advocate has a prosperous leadership line, blue Jupiter on the Midheaven, going up through Qatar, and well within range of Abu Dhabi and Dubai to the east. The Oracle Guides the Journey Here we'll explore another fascinating example of how people who understand their ACG lines can match their activities in different locations to their best lines in each place for living and working successfully, and developing important relationships. qualities of leadership, communication and attentiveness are likely to shine near this line. One other major implication of a Jupiter line also applies here. Jupiter is the majestic ruler whose realm spreads through the entire domain of the sky, so he is associated also with publishing, broadcasting, and all ways of disseminating our words and images through a wider audience and readership. The Sun lines are also relevant here. So when Oracle completes the book she's working on now, her natural publication and marketing targets will be near Texas: in Albuquerque and Santa Fe, and also in places along that central Colorado axis of Boulder, Denver, Colorado Springs and Pueblo. Her renown continues to expand, as she becomes one of the world's most authoritative voices in using Mayan symbolism and spirituality for the practical guidance of our lives. She has effectively combined the ambitious, expansive Jupiter lines, the emotional dimension of a Moon

line and the communal force of a Moon's Node line to create experiences that are as enriching for the entire group as they are for each one. The groups who have joined her journeys of exploration have been remarkably cohesive, free of the ego agendas and dramas that so often plague travels of this kind. But then people who meet under Moon lines may prove uncommonly good at help ing one another toward a common goal. The Shaman Comes B ack to E arth Many of us have experienced and been touched by the stories of those who have followed the path of service with passion and courage, and have given so much that they may have little energy and strength left for themselves, so that in the end they have no choice but to seek their own journeys of insight and healing, and intend that they can regain some of what they've given so generously to the lives they've helped on the paths they have lighted and led. This map belongs to a Swiss woman whom we'll call Trailblazer because so much of her life, even before her 17 years in Peru, were a brave spiritual adventure in guiding the journeys of oth ers. As we see in the center of this map, the neutral, restful Cusco area works well as a base for the medicine explorations she has led, often involving experiences of ayahuasca, huachuma and other plant teachers. This map of southern Peru and northern Bolivia shows where Trailblazer has guided many journeys of insight and spiritual exploration to pre-lncan sites on Peru's north coast

The blue Jupiter on the DSC line, as always, is expansive and optimistic; and as it points west to the dimension of partnership and relationship, may be the best possible line for group experiences of exuberant, pleasurable travels that expand our field of vision. The yellow Saturn line, likewise on the DSC, is deep, diligent and studious. It embodies the devoted effort of the scholar or other hard worker who invests disciplined energy - often at the

price of solitude - to the accomplishment of important goals. Thus these two lines make Peru's north coast, sierra and jungle perfect locations for the journeys Trailblazer has created, as these places combine profound and sometimes demanding inner processes with exciting, affirming discoveries. To the east of Cusco, near the jungle city of Puerto Maldonado and extending through Lake Titicaca near Tihuanaku, is a purple Uranus on the DSC line. It carries the explosive, electrical energy of the innovator and revolutionary, the bringer of change. Uranus can be exciting and inspiring to those who welcome change, upsetting and frightening to those who resist it, but one way or the other, he offers us a simple choice. We can get proactive and ride the rapids in the right canoe, with the right crew and a courageous eye on our goal; or we can be reactive, even in denial, so we ride the rapids alone in a tub, and hope for the best. But no matter how we play it, we're in for some white water. The triangles on all three of these Peru lines point to the west: the Descendant (DSC), the direction of linkages and collective scenarios, where we seek teamwork and connection with others, and often find our best creative expression in group work and communal projects. Places with DSC lines are perfect for acts of service, and efforts that are devoted to the benefit of others. Trailblazer's purple Uranus line is especially notable here. It often appears in the maps of teach ers, healers, activists and other leaders who catalyze new awareness in teams and communities, so the line is the right one for a shaman in motion like Trailblazer, and those who travel under her guidance. If there is a drawback to a line pattern like this, it is that life can become completely otherdirected, leaving little room for our own personal self-expression. If one is a creative and self directed type like Trailblazer, it will be only a matter of time before her longing to pursue her own objectives becomes too insistent to ignore. When the invitation came, as it did for her at 72, it had a perfection and rightness to it. We see it in the map she's recently explored (below), in the Yucatan peninsula and Guatemala. While the blue Venus on the MC line at left in Mexico is highly beneficial - the best line in the map for successful love relationship and for attracting our worthiest soul objectives — our main interest here is in the green Chiron on the MC line at right. It runs through the northeasternmost tip of Guatemala, and so, under the 300-mile rule - every line is effective for a range of 300 miles (500 km) to either side - it covers all of Guatemala. A colleague of Trailblazer's, who is an accomplished initiate into the Mayan mysteries, has invited her to explore the area for her own purposes, rather than work on guiding the explorations of others. So the Chiron line here is appropriate, as its emphasis is on the pursuit of our own most authentic goals, especially the ones that are closely connected with our truest sense of the spiritual aims we are here to seek and attain for ourselves. Not only this: but Trailblazer was amazed to see that so many other places in this region that have long been calling to her - Belize city, Chetumal, Cozumel, Cancun, Merida, all of the upper

Yucatan - are on or very near this Chiron line. For this intrepid voyager, the choice became clear when she was in Central America: redirect her focus to her own well-being, and remain in the game until 90 and beyond; or continue to spend her energy only for others, even to the point of exhaustion, and risk a shorter journey. Her choice was predictable for one whose choice of the Virgo path of service tied her tightly to the many lives she helped and supported in Peru, especially at the inn that was the base for her medicine journeys. She passed away at 74 at the juncture of a Moon's Node cycle, which so often accompanies the beginning of new relationships, and the closure of others. She played, at the ultimate crossroad, the shaman's choice between self-preservation, and insight and sac rifice, even at the risk that it may not keep happening for long. Not everyone will take the safe, easy route. The Heart Warrior Raises the B ar Most astrocartography map readings entail a search for something better than what one has: more money, a more satisfying job or creative path, a more fulfilling love relationship, a solution to family problems, or another outcome that is somehow easier than the life of pain, disappoint ment, financial and emotional stress that one has had in the recent, sometimes more than recent past, as in an agonizing right now that feels as though it will never end. Whether we use astrology or another method of self-exploration and soul growth, it is unusual to meet a person who is actually looking for a more challenging and demanding life. Yet this is what we'll explore here, in the maps of an intrepid Dutch woman whom we'll call Heart
Warrior. Raising her family in her early adult life proved to be as pleasant as this can be, and life

All of her lines here are a close fit for her experiences in this easy, delightful location. The easternmost of the lines, the gray Moon line pointing to the Nadir, is the classic "Mother Line," under which Heart Warrior gave birth to her daughter. She then lived here for ten more years in ways that fully expressed the two lines to the west. As befits the blue Jupiter on the MC line, she enjoyed prosperous circumstances and connections with other wealthy and powerful people. She was also active and accomplished as an organizer of social projects and community events that her gray Moon's Node line especially favors. As this line points east, to her personal self-expression, she gained recognition for her tireless energy and leadership. Her life here was rewarding, blessed with love and praise from the many lives she touched. Little did she know what a tragic turn life would take when she moved back to her native land. It was never going to be carefree here.

Trouble was only a matter of time. The purple Uranus on the Ascendant line in Germany, to the east of the Netherlands but still within range, hints that something here, and possibly a shocking, upsetting event, will rock Heart Warrior's life and cause her to re-emerge into the world in a new role that is not to her comfort and choice. A dark red vertical Pluto line bisects the country and runs only a few miles east of her birthplace in 's-Hertogenbosch, north and west of Eindhoven. Pluto lines have a curious double nature. They may manifest in strong bonds of loyalty and attachment to one's family, to local traditions and other anchors of our akashic history. And yet, as we strive for independence and identity, power struggles can ensue. The battle, when it comes, is played for the highest possible stakes of our self-esteem, confidence, even the desire to live at all, so when the dust clears, we sense that we have just survived one of the truly defining moments of our lives. Heart Warrior's Pluto line points down to the Nadir, to the most basic root chakra issues of survival on the Earth plane. As Pluto is the dark lord of death and regeneration, who sweeps aside what must now pass away and be replaced by the new, it's not surprising that he brings brushes with mortality, in ourselves and others. Under his Nadir line we may meet danger, and the death of more than just our opinions. Pluto may "kick us out" to another place, as he did to Heart Warrior, through the kinds of severe, harrowing losses that can either break one's spirit, or can arouse a determination that after rest and renewal, we will join a new battle in a place where we can win it.

The new challenge lay on the other side of the ocean, as Heart Warrior set her sights for the years ahead in the town of Urubamba, in the Sacred Valley near Cusco in Peru. She created a foundation that over the years has lifted hundreds of orphans out of dire poverty, illness and domestic abuse, and has instilled in them a creativity, confidence and sense of purpose that they would never otherwise have had. We can discount the green Chiron line to the east, too distant to be effective in Peru, and focus on the other three lines, two of which show what kinds of challenges Heart Warrior has faced for the last 14 years. The capital city of Lima, where she had to register her foundation and navigate the complex bureaucratic maze of permissions and licenses, is between two lines that point east, toward achievement of our individual goals: The yellow Sun line is highly advanta geous, marking a zone where we are literally likely to shine, to exercise creativity and leadership, and attract recognition. Here she got successfully through the official hurdles, but only after some determined struggle. Why was this? Because the red Mars line, like all Mars lines, is potentially conflictive. This one, pointing east, signifies a need for courage and determination in pursuing our personal goals. It happened more than once, as it often does under this line, that Heart Warrior felt she was fighting alone and uphill against national, sexist and other prejudices, and against the subtlest yet deadliest adversary of all: deeply ingrained cultural habits and beliefs that nothing can ever be done to make anything better in this desperately poor place, least of all by a woman from the other side of the world. The yellow Saturn line to the east of Cusco shows the other major challenge that Heart Warrior would labor patiently for some years to overcome. The nature of Saturn lines is that they are serious and slow. They entail long, devoted, painstaking effort, often in a spirit of service and

self-sacrifice, to great goals that demand our best. Heart Warrior's Saturn line in Peru may be the toughest of all four of our Saturn lines because its directional arrow points west, to the direction of partnership and teamwork. The special difficulty of this line is that it often involves unequal relationship, in which we are giving to the other much more than we get back; and if we are unable to turn this imbalance in a more fair and equitable direction, then the consequences in resentment and frustration can cu mulate to the point of breaking the relationship — if, that is, it can be broken. Fortunately, Heart Warrior is as patient as they come, and was able after years of ineffective teamwork, empty promises and broken agreements to create the atmosphere of faith and op timism that led to loyalty and trust, and the formation of strong, empowered teams within the foundation, and fruitful alliances with an expanding array of supporters among public agencies and private philanthropists. And — in what may be Heart Warrior's most enduring, gratifying legacy, she has replicated her spirit in hundreds of hearts who know now that they can dare and do anything, as long as they are driven by courage, compassion and love. Corolla O pens to the S un It is easy enough to see how people who feel stuck, turbulent or conflictive under the most challenging lines in their maps, especially the red Mars and Pluto lines, will be drawn to places where life is easier, and they have greater chances for smooth, successful outcomes. But the opposite pull may apply too, for people who've gained their goals in their present location, and may feel that this place is played out. Or they may feel a strong urge to open up in another place new creative channels that seem less active and available where they are now. Everyone knows the scenario of the struggling artist who has to create good work in order to survive. But the opposite scenario can get agonizing in time. Imagine what it's like to be a talented person whose position is financially sound, so the motive to use her gift is not nearly as strong as it would be if she had to use it, or starve and die. In time, the underutilized gift can cre ate unbearable pressure, and the longer the gift is unused, the more intense the pressure gets. That's how it was for the Norwegian woman we'll call Corolla for the blossoming that she has done in the last few years. Yet her intuition has called her to explore other places that would be valuable sources of inspiration, especially in her work with her Buddhist spiritual teacher in Nepal. The area of Nepal farther west, where she has also traveled and meditated, is relevant too, because here she has a dark red Pluto on the MC line running in close parallel with a green Chiron on the Nadir line. It was in Nepal that Corolla took extraordinary photographs, some of them mountains re flected in lakes, that seemed not only to embody beautiful sacred geometric shapes, but to invite her to capture them, turn them into beautiful works of art, and thereby help Nepal to present itself to the world in a new way. When she returned to Norway, a creative explosion occurred - Sun lines will do that - and a series of paintings inspired by the photographs, new poetry and other writing all poured out, and within the year she was moving this new work toward publication in books and digital media. And the creative flow goes on. Corolla's a fascinating example of how planet lines that affect us in one place may attract us to another place that has the same planet lines, only pointing in different directions, so that the two places seem to have a harmonic relationship, and to offer similar results. In this map of eastern Mexico and Guatemala, we see the same planets that we tracked in Corolla's Nepal maps, only now aiming in different directions. But there is still much creative stimulation here, and strong affirmation of new creative goals under that Chiron line. For an emerging artist, this area has strengths that Nepal does not have. The Sun and Jupiter lines are the best publication lines in our maps. They show the places where we'll shine in the world (the Sun) and can disseminate and broadcast our message (Jupiter) over a wider readership and audience. So the blue Jupiter on the Ascendant line just west of Mexico City and Acapulco, and the yellow Sun on the Descendant line west of Guatemala City, and affecting all of the Yucatan, suggest that new inspiration that comes here could be published not only in Mexico City, but in Denver, Vancouver-Seattle, Calgary and other locations near Corolla's Sun and Jupiter lines. If we accept the premise of the sacred contract under which our lives unfold within a script we've already written, it appears that as Corolla approaches her Chiron Return at 50, she is likely to get some very affirming results within her es tablished profession, and in new art work as well. Some maps convey a very strong sense, as Corolla's do, that this is a highly-evolved soul who has unlimited potential for joyous creative success and freedom, once the challenge in the Sacred Contract - in this case the Capricorn caution that delayed the crucial moves until Corolla was past the midlife crisis of her mid-40's - is mastered.
