He could also experiment with Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, where he has the yellow Sun on the MC line pointing to the top of the map, called the Fame Line because here we can achieve leadership, uncommon success and recognition. But note that just west of this Sun line, running almost parallel to it, is a gray Moon on the DSC line. It is less than superb for a man as free-spirited as SWM because here he'll tend to devote himself almost entirely to emotional relationships, especially within a family, and will seek to fit into relationship roles defined by oth ers, instead of blazing his own trail as he prefers. The trap of this Moon line, especially for people with less independent and adventurous personalities, is that here we are sensitive to the wishes and feelings of others, and may end up giving away the store, serving the agendas of everyone but ourselves. How does it look in North America? Decidedly better.

Born in the east-central area of the Florida peninsula, SWM grew up in an even more neutral area on the Florida east coast, where he was out of range of the royal blue Jupiter on the Dsc line that curves from the west Florida panhandle up through the western areas of the Carolinas, Pennsylvania and New York. It's easy to decide which areas of the USA favor him, and which do not. In the west the red line of Mars on the Asc can make Arizona and Colorado very conflictive, and the vertical dark red Pluto on the MC line crosses his Sun on the Asc line right in Los Angeles, making this a place where he can shine his light out into the world and gain rewards and renown, but likely at a price of more inner upheaval than he may want to endure. The east and center of the continent are a different story. Those blue Venus and purple Uranus lines, both pointing up to the MC, form a corridor that encloses most of the Mississippi Valley, and offers him chances in St. Louis, Memphis and New Orleans. Better yet - there's inspiration and buzzing creativity under the Uranus line, especially in state-of-the art technical areas, and the Venus line may be the best love line in the map. Here SWM is likely to find both of the basic things - fulfilling, rewarding work and good love relationship - that most of us seek. And there's more. The Gemini owner of the online dating site SWM writes for is located in Atlanta, close to the royal blue Jupiter line that continues up near Asheville NC, Pittsburgh, Buffalo NY and Toronto. This is a superb example of how an ACG line of relationship can benefit us even if we don't live near it, but find a way to connect with some one who is on it.

Is there still more? Yes. When we recall that in our ACG maps, blue lines are for "ease" and high prosperity, then we'll naturally want to see where the three lines we just tracked in the USA converge in Central America. The blue Venus and Jupiter lines cross in the Pacific, off the coast south and west of Guatemala City, making this one of SWM's best places in the world in material terms, and also for links and teamwork with movers and shakers - the arrow on the Jupiter line points west, to rela tionship - and perhaps also for a love union with a well-to-do SWF. Farther up the Yucatan peninsula, the Jupiter line crosses the Uranus line, forming the combination that Jim Lewis called a "unique, magical good luck zone," where gain can come without effort, windfalls drop out of the blue from unexpected directions, and we seem to mani fest what we want so abundantly and instantly that we look like miracle workers. As our hero navigates the years ahead and approaches his mid-life transformation of rela tionships at 37, Guatemala and eastern Mexico are more than likely to call him. A lot more than some margaritas could be waiting in Merida and Cancun. There's no telling if they might call him then, or later. But when a mobile, curious, enterprising person knows that advantages like these are waiting to be tapped, they may not have to wait for long. The Yogini Goes to the S ource Here we'll look at another example, like the Dakotas and South America maps of Lakota, that shows how we can "ride our lines" — that is, use for our benefit the same advantageous lines that can appear in more than one place in our maps. Here we'll look at the India and UK lines of a British woman whom we'll call Yogini because she's a successful yoga teacher in her home location of London, and has deepened her mastery by going right to the source of Vedic spiritual practice. We'll start with her map of north-central India.

The purple Uranus on the MC line, pointing vertically to the top of the map, is a signal that this place is a high-inspiration zone. Here one can gain exciting insight, and experiences that are aligned with the true north point of our soul compass, and confirm that what we learning and do here is not only what we ought to be doing here and now, but is also a clear guide to our life's ultimate purpose. The vertical green Chiron on the Nadir line, and the blue Jupiter on the ASC line that runs just west of the India-Nepal border, are the crucial elements here, as they cross near the sacred site of Rishikesh, famous for its temples and ashrams, and also as a place where people who are serious about yoga go to learn and refine their practice from some of the world's great yoga masters. The Chiron line, pointing down, shows that here one can absorb valuable lessons that will help her earn a living in a health-related profession. She may also heal self-limiting beliefs about practical Earth-plane issues. The Jupiter line, pointing east in the direction of the Ascendant, shows that here Yogini could broaden her knowledge and skill, and — perhaps even more important for this shy Cancer native — also gain an empowered, optimistic confidence in her ability to teach others what she learned here. The crossing of these two beneficial lines here near Rishikesh amplifies the force of both in a power

Two of the same lines that we saw in India are present here, only now pointing in directions more relevant to Yogini's life and practice in the UK. The purple Uranus line points east, toward a successful reinvention of oneself, and the green Chiron line points west, toward the produc tive partnerships she has created with the health centers and yoga studios where she teaches. Further east and going just outside Paris is a gray Moon's Node line that is strongly in effect for all of England as well as all of France, the Netherlands and Belgium, and offers a possibility that Yogini might travel and teach in all these places. This vision is by no means naively optimistic. We see in western England and Scotland the line some astrocartographers consider the best of all. The vertical yellow Sun on the MC line is sometimes called the "Fame Line" because even more than the other Sun lines, it marks places where we are likely to gain the material rewards and recognition that can flow from knowing what we are supposed to be doing, and doing it supremely well. Here in England, Yogini is perfectly placed to tap the energies that she has avail able here, and also in India, the source of her art.

Most of what's been written about astrocartography so far has focused on our best - or least good - places for living and working, with the understanding that to gain any advantages from our best places, we have to be there. But - and this is a big But where ACG goes - our lines can also benefit us even when they're far away from us, if they show the locations of important rela tionships that we have, or want to have: with investors and markets, employers and colleagues, teachers and healers and love partners. In fact, this is how locational ACG benefits most people. They're happy living where they are - but it is definitely in their interest, in this Aquarian Age of networking, long-range digital communications and travel for business and fun to more parts of our country and our planet than we've ever explored before, to know what opportunities are wait ing in other places. It's possible to live successfully in a place that is neutral, even disadvantageous, with lines that don't favor us at all, if we can develop the right relationships with our "lifeline" places. One good example is the man we'll call Pioneer. Like many successful American artists who aspire to be bicoastal, he has active, fruitful relationships on both the east and west coasts of the USA. He has to, as his home map for Col orado shows. Both of the lines we see here in Colorado are within range of his location on the urban axis of Fort Collins-Denver-Pueblo. The purple Uranus on the ASC line to the west is relevant to his position as a prolific author, cutting-edge musician and recording artist, and influential innovator in high-tech media. The rub here is that as active as the Uranus line is, the vertical yellow Saturn

line that runs even closer to his home is not helpful at all. It marks a place where making a living will be heavy Saturnian drudgery. Fortunately, a red Mars line out of frame to the east in Kansas is well out of range, or life in Colorado could be a battle as well as a chore. The Saturn line alone is challenge enough. If one must count on this place to support his activity on the Earth plane, even an artist as well-married as Pioneer will otherwise have the kind of solitary life that befits a monk in his scriptorium, having little social contact with individual friends or community. Clearly, for professional and social purposes, this man will need a lifeline or two. Two are on the west coast. The yellow Sun on the DSC line in the ocean and the green Mercury on the DSC line inland — a green Chiron line to the west is out of range — favor fruitful collaborations as both point west, to the dimension of partnership and teamwork, and indicate active creativity and inspiring leadership (the Sun) and successful teamwork in commu nications (Mercury). Both are close to the major coastal media center of Los Angeles, where his music distributor is located, and San Francisco, home of some of his main musical collaborators.

The east coast is both stronger and trickier for him, in his native New York and the rest of the eastern heart of the American publishing industry. Here the blue lines of Jupiter (left) and Venus, both pointing west to linkages and relationships on the Descendant, run in close parallel. Both are good for financial gain and general "happiness" and "success". They differ insofar as Jupiter is a power line that connects us to important individuals and institutions - in this case prestigious publishing companies - while the Venus line is more relevant here to successful teamwork in artrelated fields. The whole area from Toronto to Connecticut is affected by those brilliant blue lines. But New York is best because it's farther east, and well away from the vertical pink Neptune on the Nadir line just west of Baltimore. Neptune is the ruler of mysticism, music and all arts of fantasy, so we'd expect that in this part of the US, Pioneer played as a young musician, met his first spiritual teachers and first experienced altered states of consciousness. Like all of Neptune's dualistic lines, this one too can be vague, slippery, watery, even startlingly deceptive. It does not favor reliable, predictable operations on the Earth plane, or business alliances that are smooth, clear and reliable. So it will not surprise us that the kindest description we can give to some of Pioneer's publishers is ... Ethically Dubious. So Baltimore-DC requires caution in this map, Philadelphia is better, and New York favors him most. Like the classic pioneers of the American Old West, our hero is making the best of a place that is not hugely hospitable to him. But unlike those original pioneers, who were very much on their own, today's Pioneer is getting powerful help from other places. It does help that he's very well married. But LA and New York, even from far away, are throwing him a good, strong rope. Pioneer's maps are remarkable in another respect too. It will often happen, as Yogini's map shows, that even if we never go to a place, our map lines there can signify a profound interest

in its history, culture and traditions. This is abundantly clear in Pioneer's next map, of northern India, Nepal and southern Tibet, where Lhasa is visible near the top center. Pioneer has long been an avid student of the Buddhist path, so it makes sense that his green Chiron on the Asc and his yellow Sun on the Asc lines - note that the latter is the reverse of his Sun line in California - both pass through the area where the Buddha lived and taught, and where some of the great Buddhist pilgrimage sites are located. Some of Pioneer's singing techniques and methods as a sound medicine practitioner have been inspired by this part of the world. Distinguished Tibetan lamas have accorded him empowerments rarely, if ever, granted to anyone from the West. He has yet to set foot in the Land of the Snow Lion. But, as his maps show, it has surely left its footprint on him. So has anther place he longs to see and hear, as a student of vibrational medicine who will, when the time is right, walk the road to esoteric knowledge that was ancient long before Pythagoras devoted twenty years of his life to learning what the physician-priests of the Nile had to teach, and why Plato, another of the distinguished Greek visitors who came here, called the Egyptians the healthiest, holiest and happiest people in the world.

Pioneer has going through the Nile valley the same blue Jupiter on the Nadir line that Dr. Breathwork has in Cusco. So it is not surprising that Pioneer is taking his time. A highly intuitive man, he knows that once he comes here, he may not want to leave.

We've explored the maps of people with unusual career paths: an alchemist, a fashion model, a writer of online dating profiles and other exotic professionals who've aligned with their best ACG lines. But maybe our most unusual and even spectacular set of maps belongs to a man who might have created the kind of soul contract that many people fondly dream of, and wish they had the chance and the courage to try. We'll call him Player because his job is betting and winning at cards. He's a professional poker artist who enjoys increasing success in his native USA, and now in other countries too. It's uncanny. If he'd actually designed his ACG maps to align with countries that have the most gambling houses, as listed by Countries Worldwide with Casinos, he could hardly have done a better job. You know by now which lines are likely to apply: both of the blue money lines for Venus and Jupiter, plus the yellow Sun lines that can favor material prosperity as well as health, prestige and social success. Also green Mercury lines, for commercial success, and the purple Uranus lines that can sometimes bring surprising and lucky outcomes.

Player's home is near the Missouri Valley, where he has no planet lines at all. He will have to go hunting in other places, and we can easily see where: at the yellow Sun line that goes almost right through Las Vegas. Our reading backed Player's sense that the World Series of Poker in Las Vegas was an essential target, not only for getting the good hands, but also for getting known as one of the best, for this vertical Sun line pointing to the MC is, as we've seen in other stories, called the Fame Line. He may have to play this line with some subtlety, to avoid getting so notorious for his white hot touch that he gets barred from the 378 casinos in Nevada, and 180 more in California. This is hardly an issue, though. This high roller has literally thousands of other tables to play. Where are they? Read 'em and weep, or laugh, depending on how another man's whoppingly wild good luck hits you. We start in the Caribbean and Central America. The royal blue Jupiter on the DSC line in the west goes through Jamaica (27 casinos), the Bahamas (4) and Costa Rica (49), and near Panama (47). The light blue Venus - DSC line is just

west of Trinidad and Tobago (11 casinos) on the north coast of South America, and continues through Peru (61). In these places, as in others as well, these lucrative blue lines are not crossed by less advantageous lines. He has a pink Neptune on the MC line (out of frame to the right) in Brazil, but it's far east of the Caribbean isles, and thus unlikely to affect them. Just as well. This Neptune line may be the last one a gambler wants, as this "Hollywood Line" can bubble his brain with fevered fantasies, and rob him of the coolness and calculation he must have. Now that we've noticed the main pattern of parallel blue lines, we can see how it favors Player in many other places. And so — Bon voyage. The blue Jupiter on the Nadir line, as we saw in Dr. Breathwork's map of Peru, may be the richest line of them all. Player has it going through the middle of France (461 casinos) and in range of everything from the Italian border to Barcelona and Ibiza. It also goes through the Netherlands, with 113 potential targets, and Belgium, with 65. But the farther north this line goes, the less advantageous it is, because it converges with the dark red Pluto on the DSC line curving through England. While Sun lines like Player's yellow Sun on the DSC line in England are always generally positive, they're less good in Player's maps (with the notable exception of Nevada) because they're flanked everywhere by the Pluto line and the red Mars on the Dsc

line, here in Ireland and northern Scotland. Under that Mars line, sore losers may even be ready to fight, and that's why the green Mercury on the DSC line to the west, normally a good one for business, is less good here because it's too close to the Mars line. Player even has a gray Moon on the Dsc line running through the English channel, so in London and the Low Countries, he may have too much warm, compassionate heart water flowing through his veins, rather than the ice water a card pro needs. Better to spend some of his winnings in London than to play there, even though those 461 British casinos may appeal. The same general idea, of concentrating on places where the most favorable lines are farthest away from the tough lines, applies to the light blue Venus line that points down to riches on Earth in Greece (10 casinos), but, more enticingly, goes just west of Sofia, which has many of Bulgaria's 71 legal gambling houses. Rumania has another 26 casinos, but note that Player should try his luck only in the west, near the Serbian border. Bucharest is too close to the yellow Saturn and pink Neptune lines to the east in this map. This is why, if we track these lines to the north, Player should avoid Warsaw, which has some of Poland's 43 casinos, and Stockholm, with some of Sweden's 31. If he visits these places, he'd best go as a tourist rather than a high roller. Are there other places where a wealthy Venus line favors him? Yes and no.

The blue Jupiter on the ASC line that runs through India in Player's map is negligible for his purposes, as there are, whether wisely or surprisingly, only 12 casinos here. But the Venus on the Asc line in his east Asia map is very near to Cambodia's 30 casinos. Player may also be inclined to explore the nuances of that green Chiron on the Dsc line through Macao (48 casi nos), and find out whether in that place, he gets flush or fleeced in a zone ruled by the Wounded Healer. One thing is clear by now. The whole world is a green baize table for this man. His story is so amazing it would be too ridiculously incredible even for the movies, which resemble other movies much more than anything that actually happens in "real life." Thrilling? Perhaps. People who haven't explored sacred contracts, or seen the risks and responsibilities of Player's life, might envy him, and wonder why he got to be so "lucky." Is he? Let's just say his travels are lucrative, and his French is getting more fluent. He plays life close to his vest, telling those who don't really need to know that he travels a lot as a marketing rep for recreational products. His sacred contract choices show, as we'd expect, that the one evolved enough to choose these maps will likely be no fool. He knows that the more he wins, the greater the risks of addiction and arrogance will get. He's a Leo who prefers continuity and stability to being in motion. He doesn't like to be away for long from his beloved wife and his Pisces son, who misses him terribly when he's away. He carries their pictures everywhere, and sometimes has one face down on the table, so he can look at it when his hunch says: Raise Big. The Abundant E arth Some charts and astrocartography maps display Sacred Contracts in coherent designs that reflect life choices and learnings that reveal their harmonics in time. One such design belongs to a man we'll call Constant Gardener. Born in England in the Earth sign of Virgo, he loves to work with plants, and shares with his partner a home where they grow a magnificent variety of medic inal plants, herbs and flowers.

As his UK map shows, his native land is almost energetically neutral. His birthplace in Yorkshire on the east coast is within range of a green Mercury on the Ascendant line that runs west of Amsterdam, so in this location he'll likely be curious-minded and communicative. He is the son of a Royal Navy officer who evidently saw in his boy the same longing he had to see the world, and find in it the mirrors and doors to new creative paths that would not be open to him in England, but were waiting an ocean or two away. Mercury lines like this one may have some wanderlust in them, as this one does. With his father's blessing, the future Gardener took off at 29 - in his Saturn Return — to the place that called him, and the young man spent many years traveling through India and living in the northwestern area that is his energetic sweet spot in this part of the world. Here we see the places that most inspired him, flanked by a blue Venus on the MC line east of Jaipur, and a gray Moon's Node on the Nadir line west of Ahmadabad and Mumbai.

Here, as so often happens under a Moon's Node line pointing down to the point of Home and the Mother, he felt embraced and lovingly held in a place that nourished him in all ways. He learned the Sanskrit language and Shiv — that is, the spiritual path of Shiva. The Venus line manifested its predictable effects too, in love unions with women who were not just lovely and sensuous, but attuned with his soul. He also developed, in ways that Venus favors, the beautifully resonant baritone voice that he uses for devotional singing, sometimes in the plant medicine cer emonies he guides in Peru. As his next map shows, his home in the Sacred Valley of Peru is flanked by two advantageous lines. The yellow Sun on the Nadir line is often called the Retirement Line because it means vibrant health, financial security, happy love relationship and the social prosperity of good friends - in short, the main assets that we seek in later life. The green Mercury on the Nadir line means that we are likely to feel comfortably at home in a place where we have good business communications with clients and colleagues, and lively social exchanges with friends. The social and political climate here is relaxed, easy, old-fashioned, and aligned with traditional patriotic and religious values. But this, for those working happily in the Earth, is all to the good. So this location near Cusco is superb for Constant Gardener's work of raising and preparing traditional Andean plant medicines that he and his mate use in therapies and rituals for visitors from around the world.

His continental map of most of South America is also worth a look, for two reasons. One is that here, as also elsewhere in the world, his excellent lines, including the magnificent blue Jupiter on the Ascendant line, are remarkably "in the clear" - that is, they're not compromised by crossing points or proximity to less favorable lines, so they can work to their best advantage. And, if we remember the Relationship Rule - that our lines can connect us to other places that offer us similar outcomes to the ones that apply where we live - we notice that the Sun-Mercury line corridor also embraces or strongly affects all of Chile and Colombia, and also extends

north to the New York - Boston area, making these excellent marketing zones for attracting new clients. So are Sao Paulo and Brasilia, near the blue Jupiter line, as well as the Baltimore - Wash ington DC area farther north. The same line combinations are present in Hawaii, Central Europe, South Africa and Singapore, making all these relatively "developed" places excellent targets for the new website and other publicity materials that the Gardener and his team are creating. Is there more? Yes, as we naturally imagine in a soul who has created such a rare assortment of advantages. and gray Moon's Node on the Ascendant lines are too far inland from the coast to be more than faintly influential, but the yellow Saturn on the MC line is close enough to be relevant, es pecially in linkage with the crown jewel here: the blue Venus on the Descendant line pointing west to the dimension of partnerships. It's called the Marriage Line, and no wonder, as so many people find fulfilling love relationships with partners who were born on this line. So it should not shock us that the Gardner's mate, another Earth sign (Capricorn) who loves to work with plants just as much as he does, was born here. We'll call her Ceres for now, for her superb green thumb and the magical abundance that she brings into the Gardener's life. The combination of Venus and Saturn planet positions and map lines has often been misunderstood to mean inhibition, separation and other difficulties in one's love life. But it may also signify, as it does here, a serious love opportunity, one of the best, if not the best, that will come in one's life. So both partners were more than a little nervous, as the stakes of the journey were so high, when Constant Gardener went to Sydney to meet Ceres' family and homeland, help her tie up loose ends and plan her move to Peru for good.

Where are the potholes in these maps? It's not that they don't exist, but rather that the Gardner's intentional radar has somehow consistently guided him away from his tough places and toward his good ones. The challenges will come in time, as the Virgo Gardner - like this Virgo author - meets and overcomes his natural timidity about projecting his intentions with confidence, and going after what he wants with a strong sense of deserving. He couldn't be better partnered or prepared, though, and his maps are a prime example of how life looks when we do what we love in the place we love with the one we love. The garden flourishes. Mastery in Motion As we've seen in our stories so far, some lines, especially the blue ones and the yellow Sun line, are generally favorable to us, offering us material and creative advantages. Other lines, notably the red ones, can be challenging, presenting us with scenarios of external and inner conflict. Our maps have line combinations that are unique to us, just as our astrology charts have their own alignments of planets that are linked in angles of relationship. Just as we learn to work with our planet dynamics, so we can navigate our challenges and make the best of our opportu nities, we can also learn how to tap the energies of our ACG lines - and we can do this not just in one place, but in other places where we have the same lines. When we get good at this, and we're as creative and confident as the owner of the maps we'll look at here, we can practice a mobility and mastery that few of us manage to gain, but more of us could practice once we learn how. We'll call her Autumn, for her birth season and the Scorpio qualities that make her tenacious and brave in pursuing her goals. She's a master networker and entrepreneur who created a successful beauty and image consulting business in her native Australia, and has since built her following through a blog that reaches 20,000 clients, and hundreds of fun, informative videos. She coaches others in creating blogs, e-books and other cutting-edge methods of finding their niches and their audiences, and bringing them into the most powerful, profitable relationships.

Like Trailblazer's Peru map, Autumn's has near the eastern jungle a line that promotes progressive ideas, technologies and creative efforts, and also brings us into relationship with hip, forward-looking kindred spirits. Yet it's the other two lines that make this place, and others like it, especially good for Autumn and her clients. To the west, crossing the coast north of Lima, is a green Chiron line pointing to the Nadir at the bottom of the map. As Chiron is often called the "Wounded Healer" who is brilliant at treating everyone's malady but his own, the key theme and symbol of all Chiron lines is the wound, which typically manifests in one or both of two ways. In most people, who are other-directed and define their lives through relationships, the wound is usually felt as the pain of rejection, betrayal and abandonment by others. In self-directed people, who are more interested in pursuing their individual goals, the wound often takes the form of the unutilized gift, the dream not activated and followed, the uncomfort able sense that there's something I ought to be doing, but I either don't know what it is, or I do know, but I can't seem to marshal the focus and determination to go for it. The longer the dream is left unexplored, the more insistent it becomes, and the more we will get serendipitous hints and reminders of it in myriad ways, and from all directions. It fits, then, that Peru is where much of Autumn's livelihood comes from helping others to go after goals that have long been elusive, if understood at all, but come into focus with the help of her other Peru line. The yellow Sun on the Midheaven (MC) line is the crown jewel in the trio. Some astrocartographers see it as the best line in our maps. The Sun is our vitality, life force, creativity, solar intelligence and ability to think and organize on a large scale, so an entrepreneur will naturally align with such lines. And as the line points to the top of the map, to the true north point in our soul compass, it marks a place where we will have a sense that we're acting courageously to pursue our truest and worthiest goals. This Sun line is sometimes called the Fame Line, as it runs through places where we are likely to gain recognition for our talents and accomplishments.

Naturally, we want to see where else these Big Three lines appear in Autumn's maps, now that she's just enjoyed an exciting, inspiring time on the Hawaiian island of Kauai. And no wonder. The same three lines that we've seen in her Peru map are all here, only now they're closer together, so their power is more concentrated, especially in densely-populated east Oahu, which will be a place where she really shines. Oahu and Kauai are framed by her Sun and Chiron lines, so for her the best way to play Hawaii is obvious: live in Kauai, and be active there in healing cen ters and teams, near the medicine line that points west, toward connections and relationships. Oahu, most of all the Honolulu and Diamond Head areas to the east of the island, will be more advantageous as a business zone where Autumn is likely to shine, and gain recognition for her creative and organizational skills. Fascinatingly, the energy polarity of the Hawaiian islands is evident too in Autumn's maps, and offers a clue as to how she can tap this location to her maximum benefit. The water pole of Kauai - the wettest place on Earth, perhaps the most feminine environment on our planet -is balanced at the other end by the fire pole of Pele, Lady of the volcano, on the "Big Island." It's enclosed by Autumn's Sun and Uranus lines, both pointing east, so this is a zone for asking Pele's blessing and inspiration, when it's time to reinvent oneself and project our new energy and image out into the world again. And that's not all, by any means. There are times when life does not seem fair, as though some people are blessed with more gifts and opportunities than others have. Autumn may be one of these very advantaged souls, as we see in her map of Western Europe: The same trio dressed in green, yellow and purple, the Chiron, Sun and Uranus lines, are running here through the British isles, eastern Spain - including Ibiza and other upscale islands and west-central France, with the Uranus line close to Paris. As the Chiron line now points east, Autumn emerges here as a creator engaged in healing others. Her other two lines in this set point west, so that this is where she is likely to attract synergies and collaborations, and to catalyze exciting changes in the other lives she touches. And is this all? Not quite. The two lines to the east may make Europe her strongest arena of all.

The light blue Venus line and the green Mercury line run in close parallel through the heel of the Italian boot, up the Adriatic, through central Europe and out the Dutch coast, and then close to eastern Scotland. Thus the lines cross or strongly influence all of Italy, Austria, Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands, Denmark, England and Scotland. Both the lines point west toward partnership and connection, and they could hardly be better for a master communicator (Mer cury) engaged in the beauty business (Venus). These two lines, together with the three others to the west, indicate that Europe may be Autumn's best location for business, for partnership and connection, for helping to bring positive change into the lives of others, and perhaps for personal happiness too. The Venus line pointing west is called the Marriage Line because we often find our best love partners, and long, happy marriages, with people who were born under this line, or whom we meet there. Would I recommend to Autumn that she travel through Europe looking for the man of her dreams? No. But I would tell her that the one woman I've married in this life was born under my Venus on the DSC line near Kyoto, Japan. We'll look here briefly at the fourth of Autumn's maps in her Chiron-Sun-Uranus trio (next): As if a feast of opportunity in Hawaii, the Americas and Europe weren't enough, Autumn's Chiron and Sun lines also flank the key business center of Singapore, and run close to Kuala Lumpur and Jakarta. It's rare to see, in any person's maps, their best line combinations all running through progressive, sophisticated areas that are perfect matches for their professional and personal goals.

It's easy to imagine from all of this that for Autumn to be pulled to all these exciting opportu nities and destinations, her native environment in Brisbane must have been dismally negative, or at least neutral. Not quite. Astrocartography is a captivating branch of astrology that delves into the intricate relationship between celestial bodies and terrestrial life by combining the principles of astrology with the tools of geographic mapping. At its core, astrocartography involves the process of plotting the positions of the planets at the exact time and location of an individual's birth onto a map of the Earth's surface. This mapping allows astrologers to identify specific geographic locations where the planetary energies exert a pronounced influence, creating what are known as planetary lines or axes. The foundation of astrocartography lies in the belief that the planetary positions at the moment of birth hold profound significance and influence over various aspects of an individual's life. Each planet in the solar system is associated with specific qualities, energies, and archetypal symbolism that are believed to shape human experience. For instance, the Sun represents the core essence of the individual, their ego, and life purpose, while the Moon signifies emotions, instincts, and nurturing tendencies. By superimposing the astrological birth chart onto a map of the Earth's surface, astrocartographers can identify the geographic regions where certain planetary energies are accentuated or emphasized. These planetary lines are determined based on the angular relationships between the planets and the Earth's surface, as well as the individual's unique birth chart. For example, if a person's natal Sun is aligned with a particular longitude on the map, they may experience a heightened sense of vitality, self-expression, and purpose when residing or visiting that location. Astrocartography offers a multifaceted approach to understanding the influences of planetary energies on different areas of life. It can provide insights into various aspects of human experience, including career opportunities, relationships, health, personal growth, and spiritual development. For instance, individuals may consult their astrocartography maps to identify auspicious locations for living, working, or pursuing their passions based on the alignment of planetary lines with their natal chart. Moreover, astrocartography is not limited to individual analysis but can also be applied to broader geographic regions, such as cities, countries, or even continents. By examining the planetary influences present in a particular region, astrocartographers can gain insights into the collective energies and themes that characterize that area. This broader perspective allows for a deeper understanding of cultural dynamics, historical events, and societal trends within different geographic contexts. The practical applications of astrocartography are diverse and far-reaching. Individuals may use their astrocartography maps to make informed decisions about relocation, travel, or career opportunities, seeking out locations where the planetary energies align with their personal goals

and aspirations. Astrocartography can also be employed to deepen self-awareness, explore karmic themes, and navigate life transitions with greater clarity and purpose. In addition to its practical applications, astrocartography offers a profound spiritual and philosophical perspective on the interconnectedness of the cosmos and human existence. By recognizing the influence of planetary energies on our lives, astrocartography invites us to embrace a holistic worldview that acknowledges the intricate web of cosmic forces that shape our reality.

The history of astrocartography is a fascinating journey through the evolution of astrology and the exploration of human consciousness. While the precise origins of astrocartography are difficult to pinpoint, its development can be traced back to ancient civilizations that looked to the stars for guidance and understanding. Ancient civilizations such as the Babylonians, Egyptians, Greeks, and Mayans were among the first to observe the movements of celestial bodies and develop systems of astrology to interpret their significance. These early astrologers recognized the profound influence of the planets and stars on earthly events and human affairs, laying the groundwork for the astrological principles that would later inform astrocartography. The concept of mapping planetary influences onto geographic locations began to emerge in the early 20th century with the pioneering work of astrologers such as Sepharial and A.E. Pearce. Sepharial, a British astrologer and author, developed a system of astrological interpretation known as "Astro Geodetics," which sought to map the positions of the planets onto the Earth's surface to identify areas of planetary influence. However, it was the groundbreaking research of American astrologer Jim Lewis in the 1970s that brought astrocartography into the mainstream. Lewis developed a systematic approach to mapping astrological influences onto geographic locations, laying the foundation for the modern practice of astrocartography. Lewis coined the term "astrocartography" to describe his innovative approach, which involved plotting the positions of the planets at the time of an individual's birth onto a map of the world. He developed specialized charts, known as AstroCartoGraphy maps, which depicted the planetary influences present at different locations around the globe. Lewis's work revolutionized the field of astrology by providing a visual representation of the astrological energies at play in different regions. His astrocartography maps offered individuals a practical tool for understanding how planetary influences may manifest in their lives depending on where they reside or travel. Since Jim Lewis's pioneering efforts, astrocartography has continued to evolve and expand, with astrologers refining techniques and methodologies for mapping planetary influences onto geographic locations. Advances in technology have also contributed to the accessibility of astrocartography, with the development of astrology software and online tools that enable individuals to generate their own astrocartography maps with ease. Today, astrocartography remains a popular and widely practiced branch of astrology, offering valuable insights into the interplay between celestial influences and terrestrial life. As was mentioned in the section titled "What Is Astrology?" a horoscope is just what it says it is—a scope of the Horo, or view of the heavens at the hour of a person's birth; and when we say hour of birth we mean the exact minute. The minute of birth must be set according to sidereal time, or star time. Reference to Sidereal Time in the dictionary will acquaint the reader with its basis. Our clocks are governed by the motions of the Sun and we live by the local solar time of the solar system. Sidereal time, however, is reckoned by the stars beyond the Sun. In a sidereal day the stars make a circle around the heavens. It is measured from the highest point a star reaches on its daily journey. The length of a sidereal day is the time it takes the star to return to this highest point on the next day. The sidereal day is about four minutes shorter than our local solar day, and this four-minute shortage must be taken into consideration when calculating the time for the horoscope's erection.

ASTROLOGY—Simply stated, astrology is the science of planetary and star interpretation as against astronomy which is the science of planetary and star measurement. Some devotees look on their subject of astrology as a science, though not an exact one, as medicine is not an exact science; others view it as a religion; some say it is an art, and still others regard it as a philosophy. (See — Babylon and Copernicus.) i ie There are different branches of astrology, the most common being natal or genethliacal astrology, the study of individual birth charts. Then there is mundane astrology, the study of mundane and national affairs and forecasting of future trends; medical astrology, concerned solely with the health of the querent, physical and mental, spiritual and emotional; astro-meteorology, the astrology of weather forecasting and other atmospheric conditions; natural astrology, the study of earthquakes, tidal waves and so on; horary astrology, seeking solutions for on-thespot problems, the chart set for the time the question is asked; esoteric astrology, the study of the hidden meanings of astrological symbols and aspects; electional astrology, the process of choosing an auspicious time for the beginning of a project. Other separate ideas have been advanced, such as "race track astrology," and "financial astrology." Something might be said in favor of so-called financial astrology as stock-market forecasters resort to it for guidance, but charts set for this purpose really are in the field of a sub-division of mundane astrology—national astrology. (Sometimes "financial astrology" is referred to as "the astrology of economics."') There is also heliocentric astrology, placing the Sun in the center of the chart instead of the Earth. This method is employed in studying conditions in outer space that might affect radio reception and cause other electrical disturbance. Finally we have "planting by the Moon," or agricultural astrology. In brief, this may be said to mean whatever matures above the ground—corn for example—should be seeded or planted when the Moon is moving from the new to the full; and whatever matures in the ground, pota- . toes for example, should be planted when the Moon is moving from full to new. CONSTELLATIONS—A constellation is a large cluster of stars, all having been given names in astronomy, and they are to be seen in all parts of the sky. Of these the astrologer is mainly interested in only twelve, those that appear on the ecliptical belt, or the zodiac. These are named Aries to Pisces the same as the signs; in fact they were so named before signs came into existence 'as they are read today. Until about 200 B.C., when Hipparchus discovered the phenomenon of ecquinoctial precession, astrologers read only the constellations. When the change was made from constellations to signs based on the equinoxes and tropics, the point of vernal equinox was just about where the first degree of the constellation Aries was, so the twelve thirty degree angles of the new tropical zodiac were given the same names as the old constellational zodiac. The law of precession naturally spread the two points farther apart as time passed, with the result that today our first degree of Aries passes through the constellation Pisces (the equinoctial point travels backward along the ecliptic). The point moves at the rate of about fifty seconds a year. 85 De

The sidereal zodiac proponents respond with the assertion that the ancients did divide the constellational belt into twelve equal spans, to which the | tropical zodiac adherents reply that if the ancients did that, they were themselves denying value to the constella- - tions as such, for the truth is that there is considerable © variance in area among them. Ptolemy thought the Earth was the center of our system, the Sun revolving around it. Copernicus proved that the Sun was fixed in the center, the Earth revolving around it. _ At this point in history astrology fell into disfavor. Astrologers had based their calculations on Ptolemy; with Ptolemy gone, astrology was gone—but only for a while. Though Ptolemy had bequeathed to them a number of 'serious fallacies (See Rulership) astrologers soon saw that basically astrology lost no validity. They realized that the Earth revolves around the Sun, taking its twelve angles with it. As a matter of fact, very little had to be altered in astrology to revive its functioning. It should be added here that Copernicus did not enter the university to study astronomy as such. In those days astrology was an academic subject, accepted by university and royal court. He was an astrology student and that is the subject he wanted to become proficient in, but it was necessary to acquaint himself with astronomy in order to understand astrology. It was when he was studying the "music of the spheres" concept of Pythagoras that it occurred to him that Ptolemy's view might be wrong, which indeed it was. Each lists the dignities and debilities of the ruling planets. DECAN, Decanate—A ten-degree distance of a sign; each sign has three decans. There are two patterns of ruler- — ship for decans. One is: the three decans of each sign are divided according to the element of the sign itself, which governs the first decan. The second decan is governed by the next following sign of the same element, and the third by the third sign of that element. Thus the first decan of Aries is governed by Aries itself; the second by Leo, the third by Sagittarius. The first decan of Taurus is governed by Taurus itself, the second by Virgo, the third by Capricorn; the first decan of Leo is governed by Leo itself, the second by Sagittarius and the third by Aries; the first decan of Sagittarius is governed by Sagittarius itself, the second by Aries and the third by Leo, and so around the entire wheel. Thus the planetary ruler of the decan would be the ruler of the sign governing that decan. An Aquarian decan is ruled by Uranus; Sun governs a Leo decan——and so on. The other pattern of decan rulership is known as the Chaldean. Beginning with Aries in consecutive order, these rulers are Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon, Saturn, Jupiter, then Mars again, followed by Sun, and so on. This pattern places the Pisces decans under the rulership of Saturn, Jupiter and Mars. The reader will observe that the arrangement sets Mars as ruler over both the first decan of the zodiac and the last. DECILE—See Aspects. DECLINATION—Distance north or south of the celestial equator. It is the mental state experienced by people when they "feel I have been in this. place before," some accepting it as proof of reincarnation. But as psychologists point out, it is a trick played on the _ mind by the brain. An experience is had by a person and _ it sinks into the memory but by some quirk of the brain, probably brought on Dy unsuspected emotional turmoil, the matter immediately "jumps back" into the active mind again, causing the' person.to "remember" it. He "feels" that he had the experience a long time ago when in fact he had it only a few moments before. A case in point that actually happened: A lady who had lived in Connecticut all her life (she was middleaged) came to New York for the expressed purpose of going to the top of the Empire State Building. She had looked forward to this for many years, and finally made the trip. She was amazed at the sight from the observation tower of the world's tallest building and was very excited. She turned to a companion and said, "This is strange. I feel as though I have been here before." The building had been erected after she was born and she had never before in her life been in New York. It was a simple case of paramnesia, which is the psychological term for it. WOHL, Louis—The Hungarian astrologer who helped the British Admiralty to defeat the Italian fleet in World War II. De Wohl had lived in Germany, fled when the Nazis came to power and went to England; and, knowing Hitler's astrologers and their methods, offered his services to the British to counteract the work of the German astrologers. Using the German calculations he suspected that the Italian fleet would be ordered out into the Mediterranean Sea at a certain time to prey on British shipping. HORIZON—tThere are three "horizons." The sensible or visible: When a person stands erect and looks straight - ahead of him, the extension of his view is the sensible — horizon, that which he sees according to the height of his body. The physical horizon: When a person focuses his eyes in the distance where the sky and earth seem to meet or join, he looks at the physical horizon. This is the one we mean when we say "the ship disappeared below the horizon," or "we saw the ship coming up over the horizon." To see this horizon it is necessary to lower our sight, ever so slightly but we lower it nonetheless, making it different from the sensible horizon. Finally there is the true horizon; that point which is 90° below the zenith and which we cannot see. It \is this true horizon that we use in astrology. HOUSES OF THE HOROSCOPE—There are twelve. (See section What Is the Horoscope?) The word "houses" is, however, used in different ways. For example, the Sun ruling the sign Leo makes Leo the Sun's first house; this would make Virgo the Sun's second house, so around the wheel, with Cancer the Sun's twelfth house. Every ruling planet has houses of this category. Then there are "aspect houses." A trine aspect, for example, is a triangle, | and in the zodiac a trine corresponds to a trinity or trigon. Trine sign numbers form triangles, as the Fire Signs: Aries the first sign, number one; Leo the fifth sign, number. five; Sagittarius the ninth sign, number nine. Therefore all trine aspects have either a fifth or a ninth-house value. Squares have a fourth or tenth-house value: oppositions a seventh-house value. Affairs of the houses: First house—This reveals the native's temperament, the way he expresses himself, his disposition and personal tendencies and characteristics. HOUSE DIVISION—Astrologers are not all in agreement in the matter of how the twelve angles (houses) of the horoscope should be divided, though practically speaking, there is only little difference among them as far as planetary position is concerned. The different methods affect the cusps but sometimes only a few degrees. The standard method, or the one in general use—the one we employed in our Introduction—is the Placidus system, named for the astronomer Placido de Titi. Then there is the Regiomontanus system, named for the astronomer Johann Mueller who was hailed in Italy as the "king of the mountains" (Regio-montanus) because he came from beyond the Alps, from Germany. Thirdly, the Campanus system, named for the astronomer Campano. Also the Horizontal system, different from the foregoing. Then there is the Porphyry system, named for Porphyry; and the Morinus system named for Morinus. Finally we have the equal-house or Zenith system, so named because it considers the Zenith to be the top of the chart instead of the Midheaven. Many students think the Zenith and 115

Fe 1 UO _Midheaven are the same thing but they are not. The Zenith is the point overhead while the Midheaven is the great circle overhead. The Midheaven circle is drawn beginning at the Zenith downward toward the equator which it crosses at right angles, but the Zenith itself is zodiacal, depending for its position on the zodiac or ecliptic, while the Midheaven depends for its position on the equator; where the great circle happens to cross the ecliptic is then the tenth-house cusp. The Midheaven and Zenith would be the same if the ecliptic and equator were parallel but they are not. There is an angle of obliquity of about 23°. If the Midheaven were the point overhead it naturally would be exactly 90° above the Ascendant, or precisely half way between the Ascendant and Descendant, but reference to any horoscope chart will show that this is _ not the case. The only times the Midheaven could be exactly overhead is when either Aries 0° or Libra 0° are on the Ascendant, the equinoctial points. The Placidus system—The main factor here is a time arc: the time of travel is measured of a celestial body going upward from the Ascendant to the Midheaven, and this time measure is trisected. Example: Suppose a celestial body requires six hours to go from the Ascendant to the Midheaven; it is divided into three parts of two hours each. Calculations then are made to see which . zodiacal degree is reached after two hours of travel, and that point is marked as the twelfth-house cusp. The point reached after two more hours would be the eleventh-house cusp. The distance from the fourth-house cusp to the Ascendant is a similar time arc and the second and thirdhouse cusps are based on it. The cusps on the right side of the chart are always the opposite zodiacal degrees of those calculated for the left side; and so all the cusps are determined. Depending on the season of the year and the latitude of the birth, the Asc-M.C. arc of course is not six hours every time everywhere, which accounts for the difference in cusp distances among charts.' Because of the resultant "squeezing" and "expanding" of the houses, the Placidus system often is referred to as a "distortion map," as are all the other systems except the 116

Zenith system, or ne -boose fcethed, _ The Regiomontanus system—This is based on spatial arcs, as against the time arcs of the Placidus system. The Campanus, Porphyry and Morinus systems are spatial arc methods also; so, too, is the Zenith system, though the latter is purely zodiacal while the others are focused on the Earth's equator because their Midheaven is drawn at — right angles to it. Regiomontanus" believed that if the Midheaven meridian is determined on the equator, the other cusps should be also; the arc formed by extending a circle from the Midheaven_ along the horizon to the prime vertical he then divided into quadrants, or three equal parts, the meridian degree was one end of the arc and the point where the prime vertical intersected the equator was the other end. He then drew great circles from the meridian at the horizon, over to the first quadrant-division point on the equator, upward and across the ecliptic, then down to the point of the horizon opposite the point where he began. The point of intersection at the ecliptic was his eleventh-house cusp. Another such circle through the second of the quadrant-division points marked the twelfth-house cusp. The Ascendant, of course, was the first-house cusp, the zodiacal degree on the horizon itself where the prime vertical intersects it. The points on the second equatorial quadrant were treated the same way, giving Regiomontanus his second and third-house cusps. The Imum Coeli, or point opposite the Midheaven naturally was the fourthhouse cusp, being opposite the meridian or tenth-house cusp; and just as the fourth naturally is opposite the tenth, so the fifth would be opposite the eleventh, the sixth opposite the twelfth, the seventh (Descendant) opposite the first (Ascendant) the eighth opposite the second and the ninth opposite the third. The Campanus system—Campano's mode of thinking about house division was not entirely unlike that of Regiomontanus, but he used different arcs for division into quadrants. Instead of trisecting the equatorial arc from the meridian to the prime vertical he trisected the arcs of the prime vertical from the meridian or M.C. to the horizon and from the horizon to the I.C. Where his circles intersected the ecliptic he marked the cusps of his houses. The Horizontal system—Arcs of the horizon are trisected, rather than the equator or prime vertical. © The Porphyry system—In this system one only calculates the Ascendant and Midheaven meridian. The distance from one to the other along the zodiac is then arbitrarily divided into three equal sections, thus easily determining the cusps of the eleventh and twelfth houses, the Ascendant being the first and the M.C. the tenth. The - fourth or I.C. naturally being opposite the tenth, and the distance between the first and the fourth being equally divided, the second and third are easily marked. With these figured, the remaining ones are placed opposite to complete the chart. The Morinus system—This method assumes that the houses ought to be equally divided, though not zodiacal. The meridian is checked at the equator to find its degree of Right Ascension, or RA. Measurement along the equator always is done by RA. Then thirty degrees are counted from that RA point twelve times, giving each house thirty degrees of Right Ascension. These RA degrees then are converted back into zodiacal degrees which mark all the house cusps. For this reason the cusps on a Morinus chart are never far from equi-distant; on the zodiac they may emerge a bit under or over thirty degrees because of the obliquity of the ecliptic. Thus the RA meridian is not our conventional midheaven. In the Morinus system it is named the "midequator." The two are not alike because the ecliptic and equator are not parallel. Nor is our conventional ascendant found on the first cusp of a Morinus map. In this system the first cusp marks the "east point"——not the ascendant. Because the equator is exactly midway between the north and south geographical poles, as against the ecliptic, which courses up and down, only one Morinus Table of Houses is necessary, which serves for all geographical parallels of latitude. Differences in house cusps on various - Morinus charts are based solely on differences in sidereal time at birth. Refer to the illustrative house-division charts 118

Astrologers who use this method need the Table of Houses only for reference to the Ascendant, which tells them at the same time what the Descendant is. The rest is facility itself: all that is necessary is to allocate thirty degrees to each house in regular zodiacal order. The orbit of Pluto is very eccentric, its path cutting across that of Neptune at times (but not in modern times) thereby causing Neptune to be the farthest-out planet at those times. The construction of the symbols of the Sun, Moon and planets consists of a circle, a crescent and a cross. The circle represents man's individuality, the crescent is his personality, and the cross is his materiality. A dot in the circle suggests the germ of creativity. The Moon's symbol is the crescent, usually shown as a half-moon, suggesting reflection of the individuality, just as the Moon reflects the light of the Sun. Mercury's symbol is a circle with the crescent above it and the cross below. It represents the mental processes, when the entire nature of man discusses within itself the course on which it finds itself and methods of improving it. The symbol of Venus is a circle with a cross below it. This means the individuality has conquered the materiality, the nature becoming friendly and altruistic. The symbol of Mars is opposite that of Venus. It is a cross above the circle, though to avoid confusion with the Venus symbol, the cross has been altered slightly to have it appear as an arrowhead. It means materiality has conquered the individuality, resulting in greed and war. The symbol of Jupiter is the crescent above the cross, and it means the personality is master of the materiality; a jovial exterior hides the crass earthiness of the physical nature. It is a symbol of happiness and expansion. The symbol of Saturn is the opposite of that of Jupiter. It shows the cross of materiality above the crescent of personality, the basis of the word "saturnine," or sadness. Material and physical woes have mastered the urge to be free of trouble; an afflicted Saturn in a chart may indicate paranoia. PLANETARY HOURS—The hours of the day are measured from sunrise to the next sunrise; which when _ divided into four sections of six hours each are given as from sunrise to noon, then noon to sunset, then sunset to midnight, then midnight back to sunrise. Of course the hours differ according to season and geographical latitude. They do not consist of sixty minutes each. The days of the week are named for the planets: Sun- _ day, Sun; Monday, Moon; Tuesday, Mars (or Tiew, Nordic name for Mars); Wednesday, Woden (Nordic name for Mercury); Thursday, Thor (Nordic name for Jupiter); Friday, Freya (Nordic name for Venus); Saturday, Saturn. The first hour of the day at sunrise is always named for the day's planetary ruler; thus Sunday's first hour is under the Sun, Monday's first hour is under the Moon, and so on. The hours then follow consecutively in this order: Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars (notice that only the Sun, Moon and five visible planets are con-idered). The hours beginning with Sun of course are Sunday's hours. Wednesday's would run in this fashion: Mercury, Moon, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus. Saturday's would be: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon. PLANETARY RULERSHIP—See Rulership. POLARITY—That quality or condition whereby a planet or other chart factor exhibits opposite or contrasted properties or powers, in opposite or contrasted parts or directions. The Earth is always the Sun's polarity because in the horoscope they are always opposite each other. Opposite signs constitute a polarity, thus being in harmony. Air and Fire signs are more harmonious than Air "and Earth because an Air sign is always opposite a Fire sign; 161

similarly a Water sign is always opposite an Earth sign, © tending toward harmony—what the one lacks, the other has. Sometimes the Sun-Moon relationship is described as a polarity even when not in opposite signs; thus the Sun in Cancer might be polarized by the Moon in Libra even though these signs are square to each other. Broadly speaking, a polarity is a relationship. POLE—Both the geographical north pole and the ecliptical magnetic north pole are considered in astrology. The Zenith System of house division (see House Division) is based on the magnetic pole, for it is concerned only with the ecliptic or zodiac and not the equator. All other. _ methods of house division are north pole-equator oriented. POLTERGEIST—A German word meaning "troubled ghost," or a "ghost that troubles." These are spirits that haunt houses, generally old houses, but are known to do their mischief in houses that are not old and which are occupied by families. It is believed for the most part that they are attracted to young people, adolescents, for some reason not yet known, unless perhaps the youngsters may be psychic themselves and are not aware of it. Poltergeists, or the force of poltergeists, generally throw things around the room, rap on doors and walls and so on. Sometimes a poltergeist can be identified, as in cases of violent death—usually murder or suicide—when the victim's spirit haunts the place where he or she died. In some instances trance mediums have been able to communicate with such unfortunate entities, and have been successful in quieting the troubled spirits, thus bringing the haunting to an end. Ptolemy gave all the planets signs to rule, beginning with Mercury in both directions; but he had only the visible planets to work with, causing considerable confusion when Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were discovered. Counting counterclockwise from Leo, Mercury was given to 'Virgo. Counting clockwise from Cancer, Mercury was. given to Gemini. Thus Venus came to both Libra and | Taurus, Mars to both Scorpio and Aries, Jupiter to both Sagittarius and. Pisces, and finally Saturn to both Capricorn. and Aquarius. When -Uranus was discovered, astrologers removed Saturn from Aquarius and set Uranus there instead. Jupiter was accorded similar treatment when Neptune was discovered. Jupiter had to leave Pisces, turning it over to Neptune. When Pluto was discovered the natural sequence would give it to Aries, but many astrologers. said 'Pluto belongs to Scorpio. Then dual rulership was adopted: Jupiter and Neptune together are co-rulers of Pisces, Saturn and Uranus are co-rulers of Aquarius; and 'Pluto and Mars rule Aries and Scorpio together. Some of our best astrologers have cast the entire Ptolemaic rulership pattern aside, using none whatever, or having decided on one of their own. The author can attest from his own experience and from reports of other practitioners that astrology is entirely self-sustaining without any planetary rulership pattern. The greatest astrologers were the Chaldean Magi, and there is no | evidence to say that they placed the signs under separate . planetary rulership; though they may have symbolized the . TWENTY-YEAR CYCLE, American—This is the term used when referring to the fact that every American President who was elected when a Saturn-Jupiter conjunction | was in force in an Earth sign, died in office. We have heard it said that "whoever is elected in a year ending in zero, dies in office;" but that is erroneous. It is not the year ending in zero that is important; it is the conjunction of Saturn and Jupiter, and such a conjunction must form in an Earth sign. We also hear it said sometimes that such a conjunction is a mutation, but it is not. Mutation means change, in this case a change from one element to another. The Saturn-Jupiter conjunction is a mutation only when it occurs in an element different from the one it was in twenty years earlier. Nor is it true that every American Presdent who died in office was elected in a year ending in Zero. Beginning with President Kennedy and working | backward in time, let us examine the record: He was elected in 1960, a year ending with zero; he was assassinated. Twenty years earlier, in 1940, Roosevelt was elected and he died in office. Twenty years before that, 1920, Harding was elected and died in office. Then in 1900 it was McKinley; he was assassinated. Before McKinley, in 1880 Garfield was elected, and he was assassinated. Then Lincoln in 1860. And now we come to the first break in the record: In 1848, a year not ending in zero, Taylor was elected and he died in office. However, in 1840, Harrison was elected and died in office. Now the record changes completely, for in 1820, a year ending with zero, Monroe was elected and he did not die in office; and neither did Jefferson who was elected twenty years earlier, in 1800. The astrological reason for this is, 191

the Saturn-Jupiter conjunctions, which form once in nl ty years, took place in Fire signs, the first in Leo and the ~ other in Aries. Then in 1840 the mutation from Fire to — Earth occurred, and the death cycle began for the Presidency. When 1980 arrives the conjunction will form — again and it will be a mutation from Earth to Air, in the sign Libra, and the death cycle will have ended. The man © to be elected in 1980 is not expected to die in office. Every such Presidential death in the twenty-year cycles occurred when the conjunction was in an Earth sign; not Monroe and Jefferson for they were elected under Fire sign conjunctions; and not the man in 1980 for he will be elected under an Air sign conjunction. It has been said of the Seal of the United States that it is the most beautiful coat of arms in the world; and because certain of its features seem to have astrological or numerological significance, many believe it was designed by astrologers, or at least by men who were familiar with astrology. We suggest to the reader that he examine the Seal on a dollar bill where both obverse and reverse sides"

The early Congress had appointed Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Thomas Jefferson to act as a committee _ to suggest a design for the new nation's seal, an emblem of _ its sovereignty. Everyone knows that in Franklin's journal Poor Richard's Almanack he published an astrological forecast in each issue, so we can be sure he was familiar with astrology. Whether Adams was _astrologically inclined no one knows. Researchers in the Thomas Jefferson Library, now in the Library of Congress in Washington, D.C., report that in some of the books there are astrological symbols and comment in the margins of some of the pages, so we have reason to believe that he, like Franklin, knew something of astrology, and perhaps a great deal. This is the reason why some astrologers keep saying that our country's Seal was designed by these illustrious men, individuals of high character and lofty ideals. However, the assumption is not based on facts. The truth is that the design offered by Franklin, Adams and Jefferson was rejected by Congress. The Seal was designed by someone else; Franklin, Adams and Jefferson had nothing to do with it. Writing in Destiny Magazine (Nov., 1942) C. S. Wat- 220

Aes Ss aa ner reports what took place: "It was late in 'the afterni on of July 4, 1776 that the Continental Congress 'Resolved, That Dr. Franklin, Mr. J. Adams and Mr. Jefferson be a - committee to prepare a device for a Seal of the United States of America.' The Declaration of Independence had been signed earlier that afternoon and the members of the Congress desired to:complete the evidences of the act by ; formally adopting an official sign of sovereignty and a na-— } tional coat of arms.' Franklin, Adams and Jefferson knew what they wanted but none could draw; so they called in Eugene Pierre Du _ Simitiere, a West Indian Frenchman, artist and author, _ who lived in Philadelphia. As John Adams reported it in a

"Dr. Franklin proposes a device for a seal: Moses lift. _ ing up his hand dividing the Red Sea and Pharaoh in his chariot overwhelmed with the waters. This motto, 'Rebellion to tyrants is obedience to God.'" (On the reverse side): "he (the artist, Du Simitiere) proposes the arms of the several nations from whence America has been peopled, as English, Scotch, Irish, Dutch, German, etc., each in a shield. On one side of them, Liberty with her pileus (a pileus is a felt cap) on the other a rifler in his uniform, with bis rifle-gun in one hand and his toate in the other . Jefferson wrote: "Pharaoh sitting in an open chariot, a crown on his head and a sword in his hand passing through the waters of the Red Sea in pursuit of the Israelites . . ." etc., corroborating the Adams description. That the three were in agreement is proved by Franklin's note: "Moses standing on the shore and extending his hand over the sea, thereby causing the same to overwhelm Pharaoh who is sitting in an open chariot, a crown on his head and a sword in his hand. Rays from a Pillar of Fire in the clouds reaching to Moses to express that he acts by Command of the Deity. Motto, Rebellion to tyrants is obedience to God." The work Franklin, Adams and Jefferson had done as the Seal committee was not approved by Congress, and for four years the nation had no national coat of arms. In 1780 another committee was appointed under the chairmanship of James Lovell of Massachusetts, and it was this 222 SS oe eet ae {Se ae nee ee

amittee that for the first time suggested the use of the constellation of thirteen stars in the design, and the red and white stripes, adopted from the country's flag. For the first time, too, there appeared the olive branch as an emblem of peace. But the Lovell proposal met the same fate as the Franklin~Adams-Jefferson device: Congress rejected it. _ Two years later, May of 1782, another committee was appointed, consisting of Elias Boudinot of New Jersey, Arthur Middleton and Edward Rutledge of South Carolina. They consulted with William Barton of Philadelphia, son of an Episcopalian clergyman, who probably was familiar with the disciplines of heraldry. In his design the eagle appeared for the first time, but only in- Significantly. His main figures were Liberty (Miss Columbia we would say today) standing on one side of a shield and a Continental soldier on the other. For the reverse 'side he suggested the truncated Pyramid under the All- Seeing Eye, with the Latin Deo Favente Perennis. _ Then Charles Thomson, Secretary of Congress enters the scene with a suggestion to adopt Barton's Pyramid for the reverse side but to have a bird on the obverse, with the Latin E Pluribus Unum. Tf you will examine the bird (see The First Seal in our illustration) you will notice that it is not an eagle, for it plainly shows the comb of the Phoenix Bird, in mythology the mystic creature that rose from its own ashes, probably meant to be symbolic of a new nation rising from the ashes of the old order. This design was officially used as the country's Seal for fifty-nine years. In 1841 the second seal was adopted, as illustrated, and

notice only six arrows in the eagle's talon, nor are there thirteen olives and thirteen leaves on the branch in the other talon. Thus the beautiful Seal we have today is really an evolution from several earlier ones, none of which were the work of Franklin, Adams and Jefferson. As time passed many minds were at work on it, constantly improving the design. Today the central figure is the Eagle on the obverse and the Pyramid on the reverse, but let us not overlook the theme of the number thirteen thoughout. ; 223 i Scene

— Thirteen pHa colonies, hirieen arrows in one so the -eagle's talons, thirteen olives and thirteen leaves on the branch in the other, thirteen stripes on the shield red and white, thirteen stars in the glory above the eagle's head, thirteen letters in the phrase E Pluribus unum (the ribbon held in the eagle's mouth.) On the reverse: thirteen letters in the phrase Annuit Coeptis which means He Has Blessed Our Beginnings, thirteen tiers of stone in the Pyramid. The men who designed all this could not have looked on thirteen as an unlucky number; evidently they accepted it as lucky. Regarding the phrase Novus Ordo Seclorum, whic means The New Order Forever, it contains more than thirteen letters; but had it been written Novus Seclorum it would be thirteen. The New Forever seems to be more in harmony with our history. The New Order when the Seal was adopted included slavery and it did not last forever; nor will the order that we have today last forever. There always will be changes—the new forever. The clergyman's son Barton, who is credited with originating the idea of the Pyramid on the Seal, probably was _ familiar with Biblical allusions to the Pyramid of Gizeh, as for example in Mark XII: 10: ". . . the stone which the. builders rejected"; and in Acts IV: 11: "This is the stone which was set at nought of you builders . . ." The top of _the Gizeh Pyramid is flat—truncated—because, as Pyramidologists tell us, the architect's stone did not fit properly and the builders rejected it. The Bible passages, of which there are more than two, afe interpreted as meaning that tyrannical men and governments reject God in their structures of rulership. Barton therefore displayed the All-Seeing Eye above the Pyramid to remind our lawmakers that the goal should always be the will of God, for anything less can only lead to materialistic destruction. We would like to add a few lines about "Seal" and "Great Seal." Where did the word great come from? The Lovell committee—the one Congress appointed to replace the defunct Franklin-Adams-Jefferson committee—had lettered the words "The Great Seal of the United States of America" in a circle around their obverse emblem, but Congress rejected this design. Some time later, in an act 224

changing is name of the Department of Foreign Affairs to Department of State (now always referred to as the State Department) appeared this clause: "And let it be further enacted, That the SEAL heretofore used by the — United States in Congress assembled, shall be, and is — hereby declared to be, the Seal of the United States." No mention was made of the word great, and "of America" was omitted. Yet today many still say Great Seal whereas - the legal designation simply is Seal. When the President signs an important document re- - quiring the Seal, he adds, ". . . and I have caused the Seal of the United States to 'be affixed. " There is no United States lesser seal, so why should the President specify "great seal"? However, so strong is the psychological influence of the word great that it appears even on the dollar bill itself in connection with the Seal. 225
